He who, knowing thus, chants—with breath he places the gods in the world of the gods, with out-breath men in the world of men, with diffused breath the ancestors in the world of the ancestors, and with the hiṅkāra as a thunderbolt he drives away the hateful rival from this world.
Second khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ ha brūyād dūraṃ gaccheti sa yam eva lokam asurā agacchaṃs taṃ haiva gacchati |
meaning: तं ह ब्रूयाद् दूरं गच्छेति स यम् एव लोकम् असुरा अगच्छंस् तं हैव गच्छति ।
text: He should say to him: " Go afar." What world the Asuras went unto, unto that same one he goes.
text_mt:
He should say to him: “Go far away!”
To the very world to which the asuras went, he indeed goes.

sanskrit_iast: chandobhir eva vācā yajamānaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati |
meaning: छन्दोभिर् एव वाचा यजमानं स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति ।
text: With the metres, with speech, he causes the sacrificer to go to the heavenly world.
text_mt: Through the metres, through speech alone, he causes the sacrificer to reach the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: tā etā vyāhṛtayaḥ prety eti vāg bhūr bhuvas svar ity |
meaning: ता एता व्याहृतयः प्रेत्य् एति वाग् भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इत्य् ।
text: These are the sacred utterances: pra, d, vac, bhus bhuvas svar, [ud].
text_mt: These are the mystic utterances: “pra”, “iti”, “vāc”, “bhūr bhuvas svaḥ”, “ud”, “iti”.

sanskrit_iast: tad yat preti tat prāṇas tad ayaṃ lokas tad imaṃ lokam asmiṃl loka ābhajati |
meaning: तद् यत् प्रेति तत् प्राणस् तद् अयं लोकस् तद् इमं लोकम् अस्मिंल् लोक आभजति ।
text: What Śpm is, that is breath, that is this world, that gives a share of this world in this world.
text_mt: As for that “pra”, that is breath, that is this world, that shares this world in this world.

sanskrit_iast: ety apānas tad asau lokas tad amuṃ lokam amuṣmiṃl loka ābhajati |
meaning: एत्य् अपानस् तद् असौ लोकस् तद् अमुं लोकम् अमुष्मिंल् लोक आभजति ।
text: Z, that is exhalation, that is yonder world, that gives a share of yonder world in yonder world.
text_mt: “iti” is out-breath, that is that world, that shares that world in that world.

sanskrit_iast: vāg iti tad brahma tad idam antarikṣam |
meaning: वाग् इति तद् ब्रह्म तद् इदम् अन्तरिक्षम् ।
text: Vdc, that is the brahman, that is this atmosphere.
text_mt: “vāc”—that is brahman, that is this intermediate space.

sanskrit_iast: bhūr bhuvas svar iti sā trayī vidyā |
meaning: भूर् भुवस् स्वर् इति सा त्रयी विद्या ।
text: Jihus bhuvas svar, that is the threefold knowledge.
text_mt: “bhūr bhuvas svaḥ”—that is the threefold knowledge.

sanskrit_iast: ud iti so 'sāv ādityaḥ tad yad ud ity ud iva śleṣayati |
meaning: उद् इति सो ऽसाव् आदित्यः तद् यद् उद् इत्य् उद् इव श्लेषयति ।
text: Ud, that is yonder sun. Inasmuch as it is ud, it causes to cling up (Py'pKs + ud), as it were.
text_mt:
“ud”—that is yonder sun.
Now, as for “ud”, it attaches as it were upwards.

sanskrit_iast: tad yad ekam evābhisampadyate tasmād ekavīraḥ eko ha tu san vīro vīryavān bhavati ā hāsyaiko vīro vīryavān jāyate ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: तद् यद् एकम् एवाभिसम्पद्यते तस्माद् एकवीरः एको ह तु सन् वीरो वीर्यवान् भवति आ हास्यैको वीरो वीर्यवान् जायते य एवं वेद ।
text: Inasmuch as it forms a unit, therefore it is sole hero. But being one it becomes a hero possessing heroism. To him a sole hero possessing heroism is born who knows thus.
text_mt:
Because it attains only one, therefore it is the sole hero.
Being indeed one, he becomes a hero possessing heroism.
To him who knows thus, a single hero possessing heroism is born.

sanskrit_iast: tad u hovāca śāṭyāyanir bahuputra eṣa udgītha ity evopāsitavyam bahavo hy eta ādityasya raśmayas te 'sya putrāḥ tasmād bahuputra eṣa udgītha ity evopāsitavyam iti | tṛtīye 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | tṛtīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तद् उ होवाच शाट्यायनिर् बहुपुत्र एष उद्गीथ इत्य् एवोपासितव्यम् बहवो ह्य् एत आदित्यस्य रश्मयस् ते ऽस्य पुत्राः तस्माद् बहुपुत्र एष उद्गीथ इत्य् एवोपासितव्यम् इति । तृतीये ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । तृतीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: And Śatyayani said this: " One should worship [saying]: 'Possessing many sons is this udgītha.^ For many are these rays of the sun. They are its sons. Therefore one should worship [saying]: 'Possessing many sons is this udgītha.''''''
text_mt: And regarding this, Śāṭyāyani said: 'One should meditate on this udgītha simply as "rich in sons". For many are these rays of Āditya; they are his sons. Therefore one should meditate on this udgītha simply as "rich in sons".' / The third khaṇḍa in the third anuvāka. / The third anuvāka is concluded.

sanskrit_iast: devāsurās samayatantety āhuḥ na ha vai tad devāsurās samyetire prajāpatiś ca ha vai tan mṛtyuś ca samyetāte |
meaning: देवासुरास् समयतन्तेत्य् आहुः न ह वै तद् देवासुरास् सम्येतिरे प्रजापतिश् च ह वै तन् मृत्युश् च सम्येताते ।
text: They say the gods and the Asuras strove together. Truly, the gods and the Asuras did not then strive together. Both Prajapati and Death then strove together.
text_mt: They say: 'The gods and Asuras struggled together.' That was not the gods and Asuras struggling together; it was Prajāpati and Death who struggled together.

sanskrit_iast: tasya ha prajāpater devāḥ priyāḥ putrā anta āsuḥ te 'dhriyanta tenodgātrā dīkṣāmahai yenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
meaning: तस्य ह प्रजापतेर् देवाः प्रियाः पुत्रा अन्त आसुः ते ऽध्रियन्त तेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहै येनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
text: Now the gods were near to this Prajapati, [being his] dear sons. They resolved; " Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgdtar by whom, having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, we may go to the heavenly world."
text_mt: Now, the gods were Prajāpati's dear sons near him. They resolved: 'Let us consecrate ourselves with that udgātṛ through whom we may attain the heavenly world, having struck away death, having struck away evil.'

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan vācodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् वाचोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: " Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as udgdtar.''''
text_mt: They said: 'Let us consecrate ourselves with speech as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te vācodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ vāg āgāyad yad idaṃ vācā vadati yad idaṃ vācā bhuñjate |
meaning: ते वाचोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं वाग् आगायद् यद् इदं वाचा वदति यद् इदं वाचा भुञ्जते ।
text: They consecrated themselves with speech as udgdtar. Speech sang to them that which one speaks here with speech, which one enjoys here with speech.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with speech as udgātṛ. Speech sang out for them what one speaks with speech and what one enjoys with speech.

sanskrit_iast: tām pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva vācā pāpaṃ vadati sa eva sa pāpmā |
meaning: ताम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव वाचा पापं वदति स एव स पाप्मा ।
text: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one speaks with speech, that is that evil.
text_mt: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [speech] which one speaks with speech, just that is that evil.

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan na vai no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt manasodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् न वै नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् मनसोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: "Verily, this one hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with mind as udgdtar.''''
text_mt: They said: 'This one did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with mind as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te manasodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idam mana āgāyad yad idam manasā dhyāyati yad idam manasā bhuñjate |
meaning: ते मनसोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदम् मन आगायद् यद् इदम् मनसा ध्यायति यद् इदम् मनसा भुञ्जते ।
text: They consecrated themselves with mind as udgdtar. Mind sang to them that which one thinks here with the mind, which one enjoys here with the mind.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with mind as udgātṛ. Mind sang out for them what one thinks with the mind and what one enjoys with the mind.

sanskrit_iast: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva manasā pāpaṃ dhyāyati sa eva sa pāpmā |
meaning: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव मनसा पापं ध्यायति स एव स पाप्मा ।
text: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one thinks with the mind, that is that evil.
text_mt: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [thought] which one thinks with the mind, just that is that evil.

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt cakṣuṣodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् चक्षुषोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as udgdtar.^''
text_mt: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with sight as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te cakṣuṣodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ cakṣur āgāyad yad idaṃ cakṣuṣā paśyati yad idaṃ cakṣuṣā bhuñjate |
meaning: ते चक्षुषोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं चक्षुर् आगायद् यद् इदं चक्षुषा पश्यति यद् इदं चक्षुषा भुञ्जते ।
text: They consecrated themselves with sight as udgdtar. Sight sang to them that which one sees here with sight, which one enjoys here with sight.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with sight as udgātṛ. Sight sang out for them what one sees with sight and what one enjoys with sight.

sanskrit_iast: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva cakṣuṣā pāpam paśyati sa eva sa pāpmā |
meaning: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव चक्षुषा पापम् पश्यति स एव स पाप्मा ।
text: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one sees with sight, that is that evil,
text_mt: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [sight] which one sees with sight, just that is that evil.

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt śrotreṇodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as udgdtar.''''
text_mt: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with hearing as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te śrotreṇodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idaṃ śrotram āgāyad yad idaṃ śrotreṇa śṛṇoti yad idaṃ śrotreṇa bhuñjate |
meaning: ते श्रोत्रेणोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदं श्रोत्रम् आगायद् यद् इदं श्रोत्रेण शृणोति यद् इदं श्रोत्रेण भुञ्जते ।
text: They consecrated themselves with hearing as udgdtar. Hearing sang to them that which one hears here with hearing, which one enjoys here with hearing.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with hearing as udgātṛ. Hearing sang out for them what one hears with hearing and what one enjoys with hearing.

sanskrit_iast: tat pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva śrotreṇa pāpaṃ śṛṇoti sa eva sa pāpmā |
meaning: तत् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव श्रोत्रेण पापं शृणोति स एव स पाप्मा ।
text: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one hears with hearing, that is that evil.
text_mt: Evil was created following upon it. That bad [sound] which one hears with hearing, just that is that evil.

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt prāṇenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् प्राणेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: "Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as udgdtar.''''
text_mt: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with breath as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te prāṇenodgātrādīkṣanta tebhya idam prāṇa āgāyad yad idam prāṇena prāṇiti yad idam prāṇena bhuñjate |
meaning: ते प्राणेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त तेभ्य इदम् प्राण आगायद् यद् इदम् प्राणेन प्राणिति यद् इदम् प्राणेन भुञ्जते ।
text: They consecrated themselves with breath as udgdtar. Breath sang to them that which one breathes here with breath, which one enjoys here with breath.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with breath as udgātṛ. Breath sang out for them what one breathes with breath and what one enjoys with breath.

sanskrit_iast: tam pāpmānvasṛjyata sa yad eva prāṇena prāṇiti sa eva sa pāpmā |
meaning: तम् पाप्मान्वसृज्यत स यद् एव प्राणेन प्राणिति स एव स पाप्मा ।
text: Evil was created after it. Just what evil thing one breathes with breath, that is that evil.
text_mt: Evil was created following upon it. That [evil] which one breathes with breath, just that is that evil.

sanskrit_iast: te 'bruvan no nvāva no 'yam mṛtyuṃ na pāpmānam atyavākṣīt anena mukhyena prāṇenodgātrā dīkṣāmahā iti |
meaning: ते ऽब्रुवन् नो न्वाव नो ऽयम् मृत्युं न पाप्मानम् अत्यवाक्षीत् अनेन मुख्येन प्राणेनोद्गात्रा दीक्षामहा इति ।
text: They said: " Verily, this one, too, hath not carried us beyond death nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with this breath of the mouth as udgdtar.''''
text_mt: They said: 'This one certainly did not carry us beyond death, nor beyond evil. Let us consecrate ourselves with this breath in the mouth as udgātṛ.'

sanskrit_iast: te 'nena mukhyena prāṇenodgātrādīkṣanta |
meaning: ते ऽनेन मुख्येन प्राणेनोद्गात्रादीक्षन्त ।
text: They consecrated themselves with this breath of the mouth as udgdtar.
text_mt: They consecrated themselves with this breath in the mouth as udgātṛ.

sanskrit_iast: so 'bravīn mṛtyur eṣa eṣāṃ sa udgātā yena mṛtyum atyeṣyantīti |
meaning: सो ऽब्रवीन् मृत्युर् एष एषां स उद्गाता येन मृत्युम् अत्येष्यन्तीति ।
text: Death said: " This is that udgdtar by whom they will go beyond death."
text_mt: Death said: 'This is that udgātṛ of theirs through whom they will pass beyond death.'

sanskrit_iast: na hy etena prāṇena pāpaṃ vadati na pāpaṃ dhyāyati na pāpam paśyati na pāpaṃ śṛṇoti na pāpaṃ gandham apāniti |
meaning: न ह्य् एतेन प्राणेन पापं वदति न पापं ध्यायति न पापम् पश्यति न पापं शृणोति न पापं गन्धम् अपानिति ।
text: For with this breath one speaks no evil thing, thinks no evil thing, sees no evil thing, hears no evil thing, exhales no evil odor.
text_mt: For with this breath, one does not speak evil, does not think evil, does not see evil, does not hear evil, and does not inhale bad smell.

sanskrit_iast: tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam āyan apahatya haiva mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् अपहत्य हैव मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: By him having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, they went to the heavenly world. Having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus.
text_mt: Having struck away death, having struck away evil with it, they went to the heavenly world. He strikes away death, strikes away evil, and goes to the heavenly world, who knows thus. / The first khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: sa yathā hatvā pramṛdyātīyād evam evaitam mṛtyum atyāyan |
meaning: स यथा हत्वा प्रमृद्यातीयाद् एवम् एवैतम् मृत्युम् अत्यायन् ।
text: As one would pass beyond [another], having smitten him, having crushed him, even so they passed beyond that death.
text_mt: Just as one would pass beyond [an enemy] having slain and crushed him, so indeed did they pass beyond this death.

sanskrit_iast: sa vācam prathamām atyavahat tām pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt so 'gnir abhavat |
meaning: स वाचम् प्रथमाम् अत्यवहत् ताम् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् सो ऽग्निर् अभवत् ।
text: Speech he carried beyond it first. He deposited it beyond death. It became fire.
text_mt: It carried speech beyond first. It deposited it beyond death; that became Agni.

sanskrit_iast: atha mano 'tyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa candramā abhavat |
meaning: अथ मनो ऽत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स चन्द्रमा अभवत् ।
text: Then he carried mind beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became the moon.
text_mt: Then it carried mind beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became the Moon.

sanskrit_iast: atha cakṣur atyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa ādityo 'bhavat |
meaning: अथ चक्षुर् अत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स आदित्यो ऽभवत् ।
text: Then he carried sight beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became the sun.
text_mt: Then it carried sight beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became Āditya.

sanskrit_iast: atha śrotram atyavahat tat pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt tā imā diśo 'bhavan tā u eva viśve devāḥ |
meaning: अथ श्रोत्रम् अत्यवहत् तत् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् ता इमा दिशो ऽभवन् ता उ एव विश्वे देवाः ।
text: Then he carried hearing beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became these quarters; they are also all the gods.
text_mt: Then it carried hearing beyond. It deposited it beyond death; they became these directions; they are indeed the Viśve Devas.

sanskrit_iast: atha prāṇam atyavahat tam pareṇa mṛtyuṃ nyadadhāt sa vāyur abhavat |
meaning: अथ प्राणम् अत्यवहत् तम् परेण मृत्युं न्यदधात् स वायुर् अभवत् ।
text: Then he carried breath beyond it. He deposited it beyond death. It became wind.
text_mt: Then it carried breath beyond. It deposited it beyond death; that became Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast: athātmane kevalam evānnādyam āgāyata |
meaning: अथात्मने केवलम् एवान्नाद्यम् आगायत ।
text: Then he sang food-eating for himself only.
text_mt: Then for itself alone, it sang out food.

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa evāyāsyaḥ āsye dhīyate tasmād ayāsyaḥ yad v evāyam āsye ramate tasmād v evāyāsyaḥ |
meaning: स एष एवायास्यः आस्ये धीयते तस्माद् अयास्यः यद् व् एवायम् आस्ये रमते तस्माद् व् एवायास्यः ।
text: That same is Ayasya. He (ayam) is placed in the mouth [dsya); therefore he is [called] Ayasya. And as he rests in the mouth, therefore also he is [called] Ayasya.
text_mt: That very one is Ayāsya: it is placed in the mouth (āsya), therefore it is Ayāsya; or because it delights (ramate) in the mouth, therefore it is Ayāsya.

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa evāṅgirasaḥ ato hīmāny aṅgāni rasaṃ labhante tasmād āṅgirasaḥ yad v evaiṣām aṅgānāṃ rasas tasmād v evāṅgirasaḥ |
meaning: स एष एवाङ्गिरसः अतो हीमान्य् अङ्गानि रसं लभन्ते तस्माद् आङ्गिरसः यद् व् एवैषाम् अङ्गानां रसस् तस्माद् व् एवाङ्गिरसः ।
text: That same is Angirasa. For from him these limbs (anga) take their sap (rasa); therefore he is [called] Angirasa. And because he is the sap of these limbs, therefore also he is Angirasa.
text_mt: That very one is Āṅgirasa: for from it these limbs (aṅgāni) obtain essence (rasam), therefore it is Āṅgirasa; or because it is the essence of these limbs, therefore it is Āṅgirasa.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ devā abruvan kevalaṃ vā ātmane 'nnādyam āgāsīḥ anu na etasminn annādya ābhaja etad asyānāmayatvam astīti |
meaning: तं देवा अब्रुवन् केवलं वा आत्मने ऽन्नाद्यम् आगासीः अनु न एतस्मिन्न् अन्नाद्य आभज एतद् अस्यानामयत्वम् अस्तीति ।
text: The gods said to him: " Only for thyself hast thou sung foodeating. Let us also have a share in this food-eating. That is his immunity from illness (?)."
text_mt: The gods said to it: 'You have sung out food for yourself alone. Grant us a share in this food; thus may this [body] be free from disease.'

sanskrit_iast: taṃ vai praviśateti sa vā ākāśān kuruṣveti sa imān prāṇān ākāśān akuruta |
meaning: तं वै प्रविशतेति स वा आकाशान् कुरुष्वेति स इमान् प्राणान् आकाशान् अकुरुत ।
text: "Verily enter that." "Then make spaces." He made these breaths spaces [for them]. \i. Fire, having become speech, entered that; [so did] the moon, having become mind; the sun, having become light; the quarters, having become hearing; the wind, having become breath,
text_mt: [It said:] 'Enter into me, then.' [They said:] 'Then make spaces [for us].' It made these vital breaths into spaces.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ vāg eva bhūtvāgniḥ prāviśan mano bhūtvā candramāś cakṣur bhūtvādityaś śrotram bhūtvā diśaḥ prāṇo bhūtvā vāyuḥ |
meaning: तं वाग् एव भूत्वाग्निः प्राविशन् मनो भूत्वा चन्द्रमाश् चक्षुर् भूत्वादित्यश् श्रोत्रम् भूत्वा दिशः प्राणो भूत्वा वायुः ।
text: Verily, this is the divine assembly, the divine congregation, the divine conference.
text_mt: Becoming speech, Agni entered it; becoming mind, the Moon; becoming sight, Āditya; becoming hearing, the directions; becoming breath, Vāyu.

sanskrit_iast: eṣā vai daivī pariṣad daivī sabhā daivī saṃsat |
meaning: एषा वै दैवी परिषद् दैवी सभा दैवी संसत् ।
text_mt: This indeed is the divine assembly, the divine gathering, the divine council.

sanskrit_iast: gacchati ha vā etāṃ daivīm pariṣadaṃ daivīṃ sabhāṃ daivīṃ saṃsadaṃ ya evaṃ veda | caturthe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: गच्छति ह वा एतां दैवीम् परिषदं दैवीं सभां दैवीं संसदं य एवं वेद । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: He goes to that divine assembly, divine congregation, divine conference, who knows thus.
text_mt: He indeed goes to this divine assembly, divine gathering, divine council, who knows thus. / The second khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: yatro ha vai kva caitā devatā nispṛśanti na haiva tatra kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśiṣyate |
meaning: यत्रो ह वै क्व चैता देवता निस्पृशन्ति न हैव तत्र कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशिष्यते ।
text: Verily, wheresoever these divinities touch, there no evil whatever, [not a] trace, is left.
text_mt: Wherever indeed these deities touch, not the least trace of evil is left behind.

sanskrit_iast: sa vidyān neha kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśekṣyate sarvam evaitā devatāḥ pāpmānaṃ nidhakṣyantīti tathā haiva bhavati |
meaning: स विद्यान् नेह कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशेक्ष्यते सर्वम् एवैता देवताः पाप्मानं निधक्ष्यन्तीति तथा हैव भवति ।
text: He should know: "No evil whatever, [not a] trace, will be left here; these divinities will burn down all evil." Truly it happens thus.
text_mt: He should know: 'No trace of evil will be left behind here; these deities will burn up all evil.' Thus indeed it happens.

sanskrit_iast: ya u ha vā evaṃvidam ṛcchati yathaitā devatā ṛtvā nīyād evaṃ nyeti etāsu hy evainaṃ devatāsu prapannam etāsu vasantam upavadati |
meaning: य उ ह वा एवंविदम् ऋच्छति यथैता देवता ऋत्वा नीयाद् एवं न्येति एतासु ह्य् एवैनं देवतासु प्रपन्नम् एतासु वसन्तम् उपवदति ।
text: And whoso encounters one knowing thus, as one having encountered these divinities would perish, even so he perishes. For he speaks ill of him who has resorted to these divinities, who dwells in them.
text_mt: And whoever offends one who knows thus, just as if one were to perish having collided with these deities, so does he perish. For he speaks ill of him who has taken refuge in these deities, who dwells in them.

sanskrit_iast: tasya haitasya naiva kā canārtir asti ya evaṃ veda ya evainam upavadati sa ārtim ārcchati |
meaning: तस्य हैतस्य नैव का चनार्तिर् अस्ति य एवं वेद य एवैनम् उपवदति स आर्तिम् आर्च्छति ।
text: Verily, of one who knows thus there is no misfortune whatever; he who speaks ill of one knowing thus, he meets with misfortune.
text_mt: There is no misfortune whatsoever for him who knows thus. Whoever speaks ill of him, he incurs misfortune.

sanskrit_iast: sa ya enam ṛcchād eva tā devatā upasṛtya brūyād ayam mārat sa imām ārtiṃ nyetv iti tāṃ haivārtiṃ nyeti |
meaning: स य एनम् ऋच्छाद् एव ता देवता उपसृत्य ब्रूयाद् अयम् मारत् स इमाम् आर्तिं न्येत्व् इति तां हैवार्तिं न्येति ।
text: If one should harm him, he should say, approaching these divinities: " This one hath harmed me. Let him go down unto this misfortune." He goes down unto that misfortune.
text_mt: Whoever should offend him, he should approach those deities and say: 'This one has offended me; let him perish in this misfortune.' Thus he perishes in that misfortune.

sanskrit_iast: yāvadāvāsā u hāsyeme prāṇā asmiṃl loka etāvadāvāsā u hāsyaitā devatā amuṣmiṃl loke bhavanti |
meaning: यावदावासा उ हास्येमे प्राणा अस्मिंल् लोक एतावदावासा उ हास्यैता देवता अमुष्मिंल् लोके भवन्ति ।
text: And as many abodes as these breaths of him have in this world, so many abodes these divinities of him come to have in yonder world.
text_mt: As many dwellings as these vital breaths of his have in this world, so many dwellings do these deities of his have in yonder world.

sanskrit_iast: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā me devatā asmiṃl loke gṛhān kariṣyanti etā amuṣmiṃl loke bhavanti tasmād u lokam pradāsyantīti |
meaning: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता मे देवता अस्मिंल् लोके गृहान् करिष्यन्ति एता अमुष्मिंल् लोके भवन्ति तस्माद् उ लोकम् प्रदास्यन्तीति ।
text: Therefore one knowing thus should not be in fear of houselessness, nor of worldlessness [thinking]: "These divinities will make houses for me in this world. They come to be in yonder world; and therefore they will give me the world."
text_mt: Therefore, one who knows thus should neither fear being without a house nor being without a world: 'These deities will make houses for me in this world; they are in yonder world, and therefore they will give me a world.'

sanskrit_iast: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā me devatā asmiṃl loke gṛhebhyo gṛhān kariṣyanti svebhya āyatanebhya iti haiva vidyād devatā amuṣmiṃl loke lokam pradāsyantīti |
meaning: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता मे देवता अस्मिंल् लोके गृहेभ्यो गृहान् करिष्यन्ति स्वेभ्य आयतनेभ्य इति हैव विद्याद् देवता अमुष्मिंल् लोके लोकम् प्रदास्यन्तीति ।
text: And therefore one knowing thus should not be in fe,ar of houselessness, nor of worldlessness. "These divinities will make in this world houses for me from [their] houses, from abodes of their own," he should know; "these divinities will give a world in yonder world."
text_mt: Therefore, one who knows thus should neither fear being without a house nor being without a world: 'These deities will make houses for me in this world for the sake of their own homes,' thus indeed should he know; '[these] deities will give a world in yonder world.'

sanskrit_iast: tasmād u haivaṃ vidvān naivāgṛhatāyai bibhīyān nālokatāyai etā ma etad ubhayaṃ saṃnaṃsyantīti haiva vidyāt tathā haiva bhavati | caturthe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ caturtho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तस्माद् उ हैवं विद्वान् नैवागृहतायै बिभीयान् नालोकतायै एता म एतद् उभयं संनंस्यन्तीति हैव विद्यात् तथा हैव भवति । चतुर्थे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः चतुर्थो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: And therefore one knowing thus should not be in fear of houselessness, nor of worldlessness. Let him know: " They will bring about both for me." Verily so it comes to pass.
text_mt: Therefore, one who knows thus should fear neither being without a home nor being without a world. One should know: 'These [deities] will bring about both for me.' And so it indeed happens. / Third khaṇḍa in the fourth anuvāka. The fourth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: devā vai brahmaṇo vatsena vācam aduhran agnir ha vai brahmaṇo vatsaḥ |
meaning: देवा वै ब्रह्मणो वत्सेन वाचम् अदुह्रन् अग्निर् ह वै ब्रह्मणो वत्सः ।
text: Verily, the gods milked speech by means of the calf of the brahman. Verily, fire is the calf of the brahman.
text_mt: The gods milked speech by means of the calf of brahman. Agni is indeed the calf of brahman.

sanskrit_iast: sā yā sā vāg brahmaiva tat atha yo 'gnir mṛtyus saḥ |
meaning: सा या सा वाग् ब्रह्मैव तत् अथ यो ऽग्निर् मृत्युस् सः ।
text: This speech, that is the brahman; and fire, that is death. From this same speech—as one would milk a given cow by means of a calf, admitting [it to her]—even so the gods milked from speech all desires.
text_mt: That which is speech is brahman itself. And that which is Agni is death.

sanskrit_iast: tām etāṃ vācaṃ yathā dhenuṃ vatsenopasṛjya prattāṃ duhītaivam eva devā vācaṃ sarvān kāmān aduhran |
meaning: ताम् एतां वाचं यथा धेनुं वत्सेनोपसृज्य प्रत्तां दुहीतैवम् एव देवा वाचं सर्वान् कामान् अदुह्रन् ।
text_mt: Just as one would milk that speech, having brought the calf near like a cow, when she has yielded [her milk], even so the gods milked all desires from speech.

sanskrit_iast: duhe ha vai vācaṃ sarvān kāmān ya evaṃ veda sa haiṣo 'nānṛto vācaṃ devīm udindhe vada vada vadeti |
meaning: दुहे ह वै वाचं सर्वान् कामान् य एवं वेद स हैषो ऽनानृतो वाचं देवीम् उदिन्धे वद वद वदेति ।
text: Verily, he milks from speech all desires who knows thus. He, not being untruthful, kindles (?) divine speech [saying]: " Speak, speak, speak."
text_mt: He indeed milks all desires from speech who knows thus. Unduped, he kindles the divine speech, saying: 'Speak, speak, speak!'

sanskrit_iast: tad yad iha puruṣasya pāpaṃ kṛtam bhavati tad āviṣkaroti yad ihainad api rahasīva kurvan manyate 'tha hainad āvir eva karoti tasmād vāva pāpaṃ na kuryāt | pañcame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् यद् इह पुरुषस्य पापं कृतम् भवति तद् आविष्करोति यद् इहैनद् अपि रहसीव कुर्वन् मन्यते ऽथ हैनद् आविर् एव करोति तस्माद् वाव पापं न कुर्यात् । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: What evil is done here by man, that it makes manifest. Although he thinks that he does it secretly, as it were, still it makes it manifest. Verily, therefore he should not do evil.
text_mt: Whatever evil is done here by a man, that it brings to light. Even what one thinks he does here in secret, as it were, that it brings to light. Therefore, one should not do evil. / First khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: eṣa u ha vāva devānāṃ nediṣṭham upacaryo yad agniḥ |
meaning: एष उ ह वाव देवानां नेदिष्ठम् उपचर्यो यद् अग्निः ।
text: Verily, he of the gods is to be next served, viz. Agni.
text_mt: This Agni is indeed to be served nearest of all the gods.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ sādhūpacaret ya enam asmiṃl loke sādhūpacarati tam eṣo 'muṣmiṃl loke sādhūpacarati atha ya enam asmiṃl loke nādriyate tam eṣo 'muṣmiṃl loke nādriyate tasmād vā agniṃ sādhūpacaret |
meaning: तं साधूपचरेत् य एनम् अस्मिंल् लोके साधूपचरति तम् एषो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके साधूपचरति अथ य एनम् अस्मिंल् लोके नाद्रियते तम् एषो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोके नाद्रियते तस्माद् वा अग्निं साधूपचरेत् ।
text: Him one should serve well. Whoso serves him well in this world, him he (A.) serves well in yonder world. And who does not care for him in this world, him he (A.) does not care for in yonder world. Verily, therefore one should serve Agni well.
text_mt: One should serve him well. Whoever serves him well in this world, him this [Agni] serves well in yonder world. But whoever does not respect him in this world, him this [Agni] does not respect in yonder world. Therefore, one should serve Agni well.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ naiva hastābhyāṃ spṛśen na pādābhyāṃ na daṇḍena |
meaning: तं नैव हस्ताभ्यां स्पृशेन् न पादाभ्यां न दण्डेन ।
text: Him one should not touch with the hands, nor with the feet, nor with a stick.
text_mt: One should not touch him with one's hands, nor with one's feet, nor with a stick.

sanskrit_iast: hastābhyāṃ spṛśati yad asyāntikam avanenikte atha yad abhiprasārayati tat pādābhyām |
meaning: हस्ताभ्यां स्पृशति यद् अस्यान्तिकम् अवनेनिक्ते अथ यद् अभिप्रसारयति तत् पादाभ्याम् ।
text: He touches him with the hands, when he washes himself in his neighborhood; and when he stretches himself out towards [him], then [he touches him] with the feet.
text_mt: One touches him with one's hands when one washes oneself near him; and when one stretches out towards him, that is with the feet.

sanskrit_iast: sa enam āspṛṣta īśvaro durdhāyāṃ dhātoḥ tasmād vā agniṃ sādhūpacarati sudhāyāṃ haivainaṃ dadhāti | pañcame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स एनम् आस्पृष्त ईश्वरो दुर्धायां धातोः तस्माद् वा अग्निं साधूपचरति सुधायां हैवैनं दधाति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: He, being touched, is liable to place him in discomfort. Therefore one serves Agni well. Truly, he places such a one in comfort.
text_mt: He, having been touched, is capable of placing him in distress. Therefore, one serves Agni well; and he places him in well-being. / Second khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: eṣa u ha vāva devānām mahāśanatamo yad agniḥ |
meaning: एष उ ह वाव देवानाम् महाशनतमो यद् अग्निः ।
text: And verily he of the gods is the most voracious one, viz. Agni.
text_mt: This Agni is indeed the greatest eater among the gods.

sanskrit_iast: tan na vratyam adadāno 'śnīyāt yo vai mahāśane 'naśnaty aśnātīśvāro hainam abhiṣaṅktoḥ pūtim iva hāśnīyāt |
meaning: तन् न व्रत्यम् अददानो ऽश्नीयात् यो वै महाशने ऽनश्नत्य् अश्नातीश्वारो हैनम् अभिषङ्क्तोः पूतिम् इव हाश्नीयात् ।
text_mt: Therefore, one should not eat without having given him his vow-portion. He who eats while the great eater is not eating, [the fire] is capable of seizing him; he would eat as if it were putrid.

sanskrit_iast: atho ha prokte 'śane brūyāt samintsvāgnim iti sa yathā prokte 'śane śreyāṃsam pariveṣṭavai brūyāt tādṛk tat |
meaning: अथो ह प्रोक्ते ऽशने ब्रूयात् समिन्त्स्वाग्निम् इति स यथा प्रोक्ते ऽशने श्रेयांसम् परिवेष्टवै ब्रूयात् तादृक् तत् ।
text: Therefore he should not eat what belongs to a vow without having given [him]. Verily, if one eats while the voracious one does not eat, he is likely to fasten on him. Truly he would eat what is putrid, as it were. a. So then, when the meal is announced, he should say: " Kindle the fire." As, when the meal is announced, one would direct that one's superior be served [first], even so is that.
text_mt: And when the meal has been announced, he should say: 'Kindle Agni!' That is just as when a meal has been announced, one would tell an elder to serve [food].

sanskrit_iast: etad u ha vāva sāma yad vāk yo vai cakṣus sāma śrotraṃ sāmety upāste na ha tena karoti |
meaning: एतद् उ ह वाव साम यद् वाक् यो वै चक्षुस् साम श्रोत्रं सामेत्य् उपास्ते न ह तेन करोति ।
text: And that is also the sāman, viz. speech. Verily, he who worships [saying]: "Sight is the sāman; hearing is the sāman,'''' he does not thereby perform it.
text_mt: The sāman is indeed speech. He who worships [thinking]: 'The eye is the sāman, the ear is the sāman,' does not accomplish anything by that.

sanskrit_iast: atha ya ādityas sāma candramās sāmety upāste na haiva tena karoti |
meaning: अथ य आदित्यस् साम चन्द्रमास् सामेत्य् उपास्ते न हैव तेन करोति ।
text: And he who worships [saying]: " The sun is the sāman; the moon is the sāman" he does not thereby perform it.
text_mt: And he who worships [thinking]: 'The sun is the sāman, the moon is the sāman,' does not accomplish anything by that.

sanskrit_iast: atha yo vāk sāmety upāste sa evānuṣṭhyā sāma veda vācā hi sāmnārtvijyaṃ kriyate |
meaning: अथ यो वाक् सामेत्य् उपास्ते स एवानुष्ठ्या साम वेद वाचा हि साम्नार्त्विज्यं क्रियते ।
text: Now he who worships [saying]: " Speech is the sāman" he at once knows the sdm,an. For with speech as the sāman the priestly office is performed.
text_mt: But he who worships [thinking]: 'Speech is the sāman,' he alone knows the sāman according to its proper order. For by speech the priestly office is performed with the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: sa yo vācas svaro jāyate so 'gnir vāg v eva vāk tad atraikadhā sāma bhavati |
meaning: स यो वाचस् स्वरो जायते सो ऽग्निर् वाग् व् एव वाक् तद् अत्रैकधा साम भवति ।
text: The tone which is born from speech, that is Agni, and speech is just speech. That becomes here one, the sāman.
text_mt: The tone that arises from speech, that is Agni; but speech is indeed speech. Thus here the sāman becomes one.

sanskrit_iast: sa ya evam etad ekadhā sāma bhavad vedaivaṃ haitad ekadhā sāma bhavatīty ekadheva śreṣṭhas svānām bhavati |
meaning: स य एवम् एतद् एकधा साम भवद् वेदैवं हैतद् एकधा साम भवतीत्य् एकधेव श्रेष्ठस् स्वानाम् भवति ।
text: He who thus knows that which becomes one, the sdm,an [saying]: "Verily that becomes one, the sāman" he becomes one, as it were, the best of his [people].
text_mt: He who knows this sāman as becoming one, that this sāman thus becomes one, becomes singly the best among his own people.

sanskrit_iast: tasmād u haivaṃvidam eva sāmnārtvijyaṃ kārayeta sa ha vāva sāma veda ya evaṃ veda | pañcame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | pañcamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तस्माद् उ हैवंविदम् एव साम्नार्त्विज्यं कारयेत स ह वाव साम वेद य एवं वेद । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । पञ्चमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: And therefore one should cause one knowing thus to perform the priestly office with the sāman. Verily he knows the sāman who knows thus.
text_mt: Therefore, one should have the priestly office performed with the sāman only by one who knows thus. He indeed knows the sāman who knows thus. / Third khaṇḍa in the fifth anuvāka. The fifth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: ekā ha vāva kṛtsnā devatārdhadevatā evānyāḥ ayam eva yo 'yam pavate |
meaning: एका ह वाव कृत्स्ना देवतार्धदेवता एवान्याः अयम् एव यो ऽयम् पवते ।
text: One entire deity there is; the others are half-deities. [It is] this one namely who cleanses here (the wind).
text_mt: One deity alone is complete; the other deities are only half-deities: namely, this one who purifies here [the wind].

sanskrit_iast: eṣa eva sarveṣāṃ devānāṃ grahāḥ |
meaning: एष एव सर्वेषां देवानां ग्रहाः ।
text: He [represents] the seizers of all the gods.
text_mt: He alone is the cups of all the gods.

sanskrit_iast: sa haiṣo 'staṃ nāma astam iti heha paścād grahān ācakṣate |
meaning: स हैषो ऽस्तं नाम अस्तम् इति हेह पश्चाद् ग्रहान् आचक्षते ।
text: He, indeed, is'setting' by name. ' Setting' they call here the seizers in the west.
text_mt: He is indeed named 'home' (asta). For here behind, they call the grahas 'the home'.

sanskrit_iast: sa yad ādityo 'stam agād iti grahān agād iti haitat tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
meaning: स यद् आदित्यो ऽस्तम् अगाद् इति ग्रहान् अगाद् इति हैतत् तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
text: In that the sun has gone to setting, it has gone to the seizers. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god].
text_mt: When [people say]: 'The sun has set (astam agāt),' this means: 'He has gone to the grahas.' By that he is incomplete. He merges into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: astaṃ candramā eti tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
meaning: अस्तं चन्द्रमा एति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
text: The moon sets. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god].
text_mt: The moon sets. By that it is incomplete. It merges into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: astaṃ nakṣatrāṇi yanti tena tāny asarvāṇi tāny etam evāpiyanti |
meaning: अस्तं नक्षत्राणि यन्ति तेन तान्य् असर्वाणि तान्य् एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
text: The asterisms set. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
text_mt: The lunar mansions set. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: anv agnir gacchati tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
meaning: अन्व् अग्निर् गच्छति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
text: The fire goes out. Therefore it is not whole. It goes unto that [god],
text_mt: Fire goes out. By that it is incomplete. It merges into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: ety ahaḥ eti rātriḥ tena te asarve te etam evāpītaḥ |
meaning: एत्य् अहः एति रात्रिः तेन ते असर्वे ते एतम् एवापीतः ।
text: Day goes; night goes. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
text_mt: Day departs; night departs. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: muhyanti diśo na vai tā rātrim prajñāyante tena tā asarvāḥ tā etam evāpiyanti |
meaning: मुह्यन्ति दिशो न वै ता रात्रिम् प्रज्ञायन्ते तेन ता असर्वाः ता एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
text: The quarters are confounded; they are not known by night. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god].
text_mt: The directions become confused; they are not discerned at night. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: varṣati ca parjanya uc ca gṛhṇāti tena so 'sarvaḥ sa etam evāpyeti |
meaning: वर्षति च पर्जन्य उच् च गृह्णाति तेन सो ऽसर्वः स एतम् एवाप्येति ।
text: Parjanya rains and holds up. Therefore he is not whole. He goes unto that [god],
text_mt: Parjanya rains and holds back [the rain]. By that he is incomplete. He merges into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: kṣīyanta āpa evam oṣadhaya evaṃ vanaspatayaḥ tena tāny asarvāṇi tāny etam evāpiyanti |
meaning: क्षीयन्त आप एवम् ओषधय एवं वनस्पतयः तेन तान्य् असर्वाणि तान्य् एतम् एवापियन्ति ।
text: The waters are exhausted, even so the herbs, even so the foresttrees. Therefore they are not whole. They go unto that [god],
text_mt: Waters dwindle, plants likewise, trees likewise. By that they are incomplete. They merge into this one alone.

sanskrit_iast: tad yad etat sarvaṃ vāyuṃ evāpyeti tasmād vāyur eva sāma |
meaning: तद् यद् एतत् सर्वं वायुं एवाप्येति तस्माद् वायुर् एव साम ।
text: So, as this all goes unto wind, therefore is wind the sāman.
text_mt: Since all this merges into Vāyu alone, therefore Vāyu alone is the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha vai sāmavit sa sāma veda ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: स ह वै सामवित् स साम वेद य एवं वेद ।
text: He is sāman-'know'mg, he knows the [entire] sāman, who knows thus.
text_mt: He indeed is a knower of the sāman, he knows the complete sāman, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: athādhyātmam na vai svapan vācā vadati seyam eva prāṇam apyeti |
meaning: अथाध्यात्मम् न वै स्वपन् वाचा वदति सेयम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
text: Now with regard to the self. One who sleeps speaks not with the voice. That same [voice] goes unto breath,
text_mt: Now as pertaining to the self. One who is sleeping does not speak with speech. It merges into the breath alone.

sanskrit_iast: na manasā dhyāyati tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
meaning: न मनसा ध्यायति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
text: He thinks not with the mind. That same [mind] goes unto breath.
text_mt: He does not think with the mind. It merges into the breath alone.

sanskrit_iast: na cakṣuṣā paśyati tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
meaning: न चक्षुषा पश्यति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
text: He sees not with sight. That same [sight] goes unto breath.
text_mt: He does not see with the eye. It merges into the breath alone.

sanskrit_iast: na śrotreṇa śṛṇoti tad idam eva prāṇam apyeti |
meaning: न श्रोत्रेण शृणोति तद् इदम् एव प्राणम् अप्येति ।
text: He hears not witli hearing. That same [hearing] goes unto breath.
text_mt: He does not hear with the ear. It merges into the breath alone.

sanskrit_iast: tad yad etat sarvam prāṇam evābhisameti tasmāt prāṇa eva sāma |
meaning: तद् यद् एतत् सर्वम् प्राणम् एवाभिसमेति तस्मात् प्राण एव साम ।
text: So, as this all goes together unto breath, therefore is breath the sāman.
text_mt: Since all this gathers together into the breath alone, therefore breath alone is the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha vai sāmavit sa kṛtsnaṃ sāma veda ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: स ह वै सामवित् स कृत्स्नं साम वेद य एवं वेद ।
text: He is sawaw-knowing, he knows the entire sāman, who knows thus.
text_mt: He indeed is a knower of the sāman, he knows the complete sāman, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: tad yad idam āhur na batādya vātīti haitat puruṣe 'ntar niramate sa pūrṇas svedamāna āste |
meaning: तद् यद् इदम् आहुर् न बताद्य वातीति हैतत् पुरुषे ऽन्तर् निरमते स पूर्णस् स्वेदमान आस्ते ।
text: Now when they say: "Lo! it doth not blow to-day," it is then resting within man; he sits full, sweating.
text_mt: As to what they say: 'Ah, the wind is not blowing today,' it rests inside the person; he sits filled and sweating.

sanskrit_iast: tad dha śaunakaṃ ca kāpeyam abhipratāriṇaṃ ca brāhmaṇaḥ pariveviṣyamāṇā upāvavrāja | prathame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् ध शौनकं च कापेयम् अभिप्रतारिणं च ब्राह्मणः परिवेविष्यमाणा उपावव्राज । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: Now unto Śaunaka Kapeya and Abhipratarin [Kaksaseni], while they were being waited upon, a Brahman came.
text_mt: Now a brahmin approached Śaunaka Kāpeya and Abhipratārin Kākṣaseni while they were being served. / First khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tau ha bibhikṣe taṃ ha nādadrāte ko vā ko veti manyamānau |
meaning: तौ ह बिभिक्षे तं ह नादद्राते को वा को वेति मन्यमानौ ।
text: He begged [food] of them. They paid no attention to him, thinking: "Who or who is he?"
text_mt: He begged food of the two. Thinking, 'Who is he, anyway?' the two did not pay attention to him.

sanskrit_iast: tau hopajagau mahātmanaś caturo deva ekaḥ kas sa jagāra bhuvanasya gopāḥ taṃ kāpeya na vijānanty eke 'bhipratārin bahudhā niviṣṭam iti |
meaning: तौ होपजगौ महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एकः कस् स जगार भुवनस्य गोपाः तं कापेय न विजानन्त्य् एके ऽभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा निविष्टम् इति ।
text: He sang unto them: "One [god]—who is he?—swallowed up four magnanimous ones, being a keeper of ci'eation; liim, O Kapeya, some do not know; him, O Abhipratarin, settled down in many places."
text_mt: He sang beside them: / 'Four great-souled ones has the one god swallowed—who is that protector of the world? / Him, O Kāpeya, some do not recognize, O Abhipratārin, who is entered into many places.'

sanskrit_iast: sa hovācābhipratārīmaṃ vāva prapadya pratibrūhīti tvayā vā ayam pratyucya iti |
meaning: स होवाचाभिप्रतारीमं वाव प्रपद्य प्रतिब्रूहीति त्वया वा अयम् प्रत्युच्य इति ।
text: Said Abhipratarin: " Stepping forward, answer this man; by thee must this man be answered."
text_mt: Abhipratārin said: 'Go up to this one and answer him; he must be answered by you.'

sanskrit_iast: taṃ ha pratyuvāca ātmā devānām uta martyānāṃ hiraṇyadanto rapaso na sūnuḥ mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur anadyamāno yad adantam attī ti |
meaning: तं ह प्रत्युवाच आत्मा देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानां हिरण्यदन्तो रपसो न सूनुः महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् अनद्यमानो यद् अदन्तम् अत्ती ति ।
text: Him he answered: " The self of the gods and of mortals, with golden teeth, defective (?), not a son. Great they call his greatness, in that he, not being eaten, eats him who eats."
text_mt: He answered him: / 'The self of the gods and of mortals, with golden teeth, not the son of disease, / they speak of his great majesty, that uneaten, he eats the eater.'

sanskrit_iast: mahātmanaś caturo eka iti vāg vā agniḥ sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tad vācam prāṇo girati |
meaning: महात्मनश् चतुरो एक इति वाग् वा अग्निः स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तद् वाचम् प्राणो गिरति ।
text: 'One [god] four magnanimous ones:' speech verily is fire; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up speech.
text_mt: 'Four great-souled ones has the one god [swallowed]'—speech is Agni; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows speech.

sanskrit_iast: manaś candramās sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tan manaḥ prāṇo girati |
meaning: मनश् चन्द्रमास् स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तन् मनः प्राणो गिरति ।
text: Mind [is] the moon; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up mind.
text_mt: The mind is the moon; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows the mind.

sanskrit_iast: cakṣur ādityas sa mahātmā devaḥ sa yatra svapiti tac cakṣuḥ prāṇo girati |
meaning: चक्षुर् आदित्यस् स महात्मा देवः स यत्र स्वपिति तच् चक्षुः प्राणो गिरति ।
text: Sight [is] the sun; that is a magnanimous god. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up sight,
text_mt: The eye is the sun; he is a great-souled god; when one sleeps, breath swallows the eye.

sanskrit_iast: śrotraṃ diśas tā mahātmāno devāḥ sa yatra svapiti tac chrotram prāṇo girati |
meaning: श्रोत्रं दिशस् ता महात्मानो देवाः स यत्र स्वपिति तच् छ्रोत्रम् प्राणो गिरति ।
text: Hearing [is] the quarters; those are magnanimous gods. When one sleeps, then breath swallows up hearing.
text_mt: The ear is the directions; they are great-souled gods; when one sleeps, breath swallows the ear.

sanskrit_iast: tad yan mahātmanaś caturo deva eka ity etad dha tat |
meaning: तद् यन् महात्मनश् चतुरो देव एक इत्य् एतद् ध तत् ।
text: So, when [it is said]: 'One god four magnanimous ones,' this is what that means.
text_mt: So when it says, 'Four great-souled ones has the one god [swallowed],' that is this.

sanskrit_iast: kas sa jagāreti prajāpatir vai kaḥ sa haitaj jagāra |
meaning: कस् स जगारेति प्रजापतिर् वै कः स हैतज् जगार ।
text: 'Who (ka) is he who swallowed up:' Ka is Prajapati. He swallowed this up.
text_mt: 'Who is that who swallowed them?' Ka is Prajāpati; he swallowed them.

sanskrit_iast: bhuvanasya gopā iti sa u vāva bhuvanasya gopāḥ |
meaning: भुवनस्य गोपा इति स उ वाव भुवनस्य गोपाः ।
text: 'A keeper of creation:' he, indeed, is a keeper of creation.
text_mt: 'The protector of the world'—he indeed is the protector of the world.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ kāpeya na vijānanty eka iti na hy etam eke vijānanti |
meaning: तं कापेय न विजानन्त्य् एक इति न ह्य् एतम् एके विजानन्ति ।
text: 'Him, O Kapeya, some do not know:' for some do not know him.
text_mt: 'Him, O Kāpeya, some do not recognize'—for some do not recognize him.

sanskrit_iast: abhipratārin bahudhā niviṣṭam iti bahudhā hy evaiṣa niviṣṭo yat prāṇaḥ |
meaning: अभिप्रतारिन् बहुधा निविष्टम् इति बहुधा ह्य् एवैष निविष्टो यत् प्राणः ।
text: ' Him, O Abhiprattirin, settled down in many places:' for this breath has settled down in many places.
text_mt: 'O Abhipratārin, who is entered into many places'—for he is entered into many places, namely breath.

sanskrit_iast: ātmā devānām uta martyānām iti ātmā hy eṣa devānām uta martyānām |
meaning: आत्मा देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानाम् इति आत्मा ह्य् एष देवानाम् उत मर्त्यानाम् ।
text: 'The self of the gods and of mortals:' for he is the self of the gods and of mortals,
text_mt: 'The self of the gods and of mortals'—for he is the self of the gods and of mortals.

sanskrit_iast: hiraṇyadanto rapaso na sūnur iti na hy eṣa sūnuḥ sūnurūpo hy eṣa san na sūnuḥ |
meaning: हिरण्यदन्तो रपसो न सूनुर् इति न ह्य् एष सूनुः सूनुरूपो ह्य् एष सन् न सूनुः ।
text: ' With golden teeth, defective, not a son:' for he is not a son; for he, having the form of a son, is not a son.

sanskrit_iast: mahāntam asya mahimānam āhur iti mahāntaṃ hy etasya mahimānam āhuḥ |
meaning: महान्तम् अस्य महिमानम् आहुर् इति महान्तं ह्य् एतस्य महिमानम् आहुः ।
text: 'Great they call his greatness:' for they call his greatness great.
text_mt:
"Great they call his greatness":
for great indeed they call his greatness.

sanskrit_iast: anadyamāno yad adantam attīti anadyamāno hy eṣo 'dantam atti | prathame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: अनद्यमानो यद् अदन्तम् अत्तीति अनद्यमानो ह्य् एषो ऽदन्तम् अत्ति । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: 'In that he, not being eaten, eats him who eats:' for he, not being eaten, eats him who eats.
text_mt:
"Eaten by none, he eats him that eats":
for being eaten by none, he eats him that eats.
[This is] the second khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tasyaiṣa śrīr ātmā samudrūḍho yad asāv ādityaḥ tasmād gāyatrasya stotre ṇāvānyān nec chriyā avachidyā iti |
meaning: तस्यैष श्रीर् आत्मा समुद्रूढो यद् असाव् आदित्यः तस्माद् गायत्रस्य स्तोत्रे णावान्यान् नेच् छ्रिया अवछिद्या इति ।
text: Of it he is the fortune, the self completely risen (?), viz. yonder sun. Therefore one should not take breath in (during) the stotra of the ydyatra [-sāman'] [saying]: "May I not be cut off from fortune."
text_mt:
His prosperous self, risen high, is that sun up there.
Therefore, in the chant of the gāyatra, let him not breathe out, thinking: "Lest I be cut off from prosperity."

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa evoktham yat purastād avāniti tad etad ukthasya śiro yad dakṣiṇatas sa dakṣiṇaḥ pakṣo yad uttaratas sa uttaraḥ pakṣo yat paścāt puccham |
meaning: स एष एवोक्थम् यत् पुरस्ताद् अवानिति तद् एतद् उक्थस्य शिरो यद् दक्षिणतस् स दक्षिणः पक्षो यद् उत्तरतस् स उत्तरः पक्षो यत् पश्चात् पुच्छम् ।
text: That same is the uktha. When one takes breath eastward, that is the head of the uktha/ when southward, that is the right side (wing); when northward, that is the left side (wing); when westward, that is the tail.
text_mt:
This very one is the uktha.
That which breathes forward in front, that is the head of the uktha; that which is to the right is the right wing; that which is to the left is the left wing; that which is behind is the tail.

sanskrit_iast: ayam eva prāṇa ukthasyātmā sa ya evam etam ukthasyātmānam ātman pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda sa hāmuṣmiṃl loke sāṅgas satanus sambhavati |
meaning: अयम् एव प्राण उक्थस्यात्मा स य एवम् एतम् उक्थस्यात्मानम् आत्मन् प्रतिष्ठितं वेद स हामुष्मिंल् लोके साङ्गस् सतनुस् सम्भवति ।
text: This breath is the self of the uktha. Who thus knows this self of the uktha firmly established in the self, truly he comes into being in yonder world with limbs, with a body, [whole].
text_mt:
This breath alone is the self of the uktha.
He who knows this self of the uktha thus established in the self, comes into being in yonder world with [all his] limbs, with his body, [complete].

sanskrit_iast: śaśvad dha vā amuṣmiṃl loke yad idam puruṣasyāṇḍau śiśnaṃ karṇau nāsike yat kiṃ cānasthikaṃ na sambhavati |
meaning: शश्वद् ध वा अमुष्मिंल् लोके यद् इदम् पुरुषस्याण्डौ शिश्नं कर्णौ नासिके यत् किं चानस्थिकं न सम्भवति ।
text: Verily, that is certainly in yonder world, viz. a man's two testicles, the penis, the two ears, the two nostrils: whatever does not come into being boneless,
text_mt: For indeed, constantly in yonder world, what is in this man the testicles, penis, ears, nostrils, and whatever is boneless, does not come into being.

sanskrit_iast: atha ya evam etam ukthasyātmānam ātman pratiṣṭhitaṃ veda sa haivāmuṣmiṃl loke sāṅgas satanus sarvas sambhavati |
meaning: अथ य एवम् एतम् उक्थस्यात्मानम् आत्मन् प्रतिष्ठितं वेद स हैवामुष्मिंल् लोके साङ्गस् सतनुस् सर्वस् सम्भवति ।
text: Now whoso thus knows this self of the uktha firmly established in the self, truly he comes into being in yonder world with limbs, with a body, whole.
text_mt: Now he who knows this self of the uktha thus established in the self, comes into being in yonder world with [all his] limbs, with his body, complete.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad vaiśvāmitram uktham tad annaṃ vai viśvam prāṇo mitram |
meaning: तद् एतद् वैश्वामित्रम् उक्थम् तद् अन्नं वै विश्वम् प्राणो मित्रम् ।
text: That same is the uktha belonging to Vigvamitra. Verily, food is all (vipva), breath is a friend (mitra).
text_mt:
This is that Vaiśvāmitra uktha.
Food is indeed all (viśva); breath is friend (mitra).

sanskrit_iast: tad dha viśvāmitraś śrameṇa tapasā vratacaryeṇendrasya priyaṃ dhāmopajagāma |
meaning: तद् ध विश्वामित्रश् श्रमेण तपसा व्रतचर्येणेन्द्रस्य प्रियं धामोपजगाम ।
text: Now Vi9vamitra through exertion, through penance, through the performance of vows, went unto the dear abode of Indra. e. And he proclaimed to him that which has come to men here.
text_mt: Through weariness, ascetic heat, and observance of vows, Viśvāmitra approached Indra's beloved domain.

sanskrit_iast: tasmā u haitat provāca yad idam manuṣyān āgatam |
meaning: तस्मा उ हैतत् प्रोवाच यद् इदम् मनुष्यान् आगतम् ।
text: Now he went for instruction [to him] [saying]: " Light is this uktha."
text_mt: To him he proclaimed that which has reached men here.

sanskrit_iast: tad dha sa upaniṣasāda jyotir etad uktham iti |
meaning: तद् ध स उपनिषसाद ज्योतिर् एतद् उक्थम् इति ।
text_mt: He [Viśvāmitra] approached him [saying], "This uktha is light."

sanskrit_iast: jyotir iti dve akṣare prāṇa iti dve annam iti dve tad etad anna eva pratiṣṭhitam |
meaning: ज्योतिर् इति द्वे अक्षरे प्राण इति द्वे अन्नम् इति द्वे तद् एतद् अन्न एव प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
text: ' Light' has two syllables,' breath' has two, ' food' has two. That same is firmly established in food.
text_mt:
"Light" (jyotis) has two syllables; "breath" (prāṇa) has two; "food" (anna) has two.
Thus it is established in food alone.

sanskrit_iast: atha hainaṃ jamadagnir upaniṣasādāyur etad uktham iti |
meaning: अथ हैनं जमदग्निर् उपनिषसादायुर् एतद् उक्थम् इति ।
text: Then Jamadagni went for instruction to him [saying]: "Life is this uktha."
text_mt: Then Jamadagni approached him [saying], "This uktha is lifespan (āyus)."

sanskrit_iast: āyur iti dve akṣare prāṇa iti dve annam iti dve tad etad anna eva pratiṣṭhitam |
meaning: आयुर् इति द्वे अक्षरे प्राण इति द्वे अन्नम् इति द्वे तद् एतद् अन्न एव प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
text: ' Life' has two syllables, ' breath' two, ' food ' two. That same is firmly established in food.
text_mt:
"Lifespan" (āyus) has two syllables; "breath" (prāṇa) has two; "food" (anna) has two.
Thus it is established in food alone.

sanskrit_iast: atha hainaṃ vasiṣṭha upaniṣasāda gaur etad uktham iti tad etad annam eva annaṃ hi gauḥ |
meaning: अथ हैनं वसिष्ठ उपनिषसाद गौर् एतद् उक्थम् इति तद् एतद् अन्नम् एव अन्नं हि गौः ।
text: Then Vasistha went for instruction to him [saying]: " The cow is this uktha." That same is just food. For the cow is food.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhur yad asya prāṇasya puruṣaś śarīram atha kenānye prānāś śarīravanto bhavantīti |
meaning: तद् आहुर् यद् अस्य प्राणस्य पुरुषश् शरीरम् अथ केनान्ये प्रानाश् शरीरवन्तो भवन्तीति ।
text: This they say: " If man be the body of this breath, how then do the other breaths .(senses) come to have bodies?"
text_mt: They say: "If the man is the body of this breath, then by what do the other breaths possess a body?"

sanskrit_iast: sa brūyād yad vācā vadati tad vācaś śarīraṃ yan manasā dhyāyati tan manasaś śarīraṃ yac cakṣuṣā paśyati tac cakṣuṣaś śarīraṃ yac chrotreṇa śṛṇoti tac chrotrasya śarīram evam u hānye prāṇāś śarīravanto bhavantīti | prathame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स ब्रूयाद् यद् वाचा वदति तद् वाचश् शरीरं यन् मनसा ध्यायति तन् मनसश् शरीरं यच् चक्षुषा पश्यति तच् चक्षुषश् शरीरं यच् छ्रोत्रेण शृणोति तच् छ्रोत्रस्य शरीरम् एवम् उ हान्ये प्राणाश् शरीरवन्तो भवन्तीति । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
text: Let him say: " What he speaks with speech, that is the body of speech. What he thinks with the mind, that is the body of the mind. What he sees with sight, that is the body of sight. What he hears with hearing, that is the body of hearing. Thus the other breaths (senses) also come to have bodies."
text_mt:
He should say: "What one speaks with speech, that is the body of speech; what one meditates with mind, that is the body of mind; what one sees with the eye, that is the body of the eye; what one hears with the ear, that is the body of the ear.
Thus indeed do the other breaths possess a body."
[This is] the third khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad ukthaṃ saptavidham śasyate stotriyo 'nurūpo dhāyyā pragāthas sūktaṃ nivit paridhānīyā |
meaning: तद् एतद् उक्थं सप्तविधम् शस्यते स्तोत्रियो ऽनुरूपो धाय्या प्रगाथस् सूक्तं निवित् परिधानीया ।
text: That same uktha is sevenfold. Chanted is the stotriya (strophe), the anurupa (antistrophe), the dhdyyd (kindling verse), the pragdtha (tristich), the sukta (hymn), the 7iivid (notification), [and] the paridhdnlyd (closing verse).
text_mt:
Now this uktha is sevenfold:
there are recited the stotriya, the anurūpa, the dhāyyā, the pragātha, the sūkta, the nivid, and the paridhānīyā.

sanskrit_iast: iyam eva stotriyo 'gnir anurūpo vāyur dhāyyāntarikṣam pragātho dyaus sūktam ādityo nivit tasmād bahvṛcā udite nividam adhīyante ādityo hi nivit diśaḥ paridhānīyety adhidevatam |
meaning: इयम् एव स्तोत्रियो ऽग्निर् अनुरूपो वायुर् धाय्यान्तरिक्षम् प्रगाथो द्यौस् सूक्तम् आदित्यो निवित् तस्माद् बह्वृचा उदिते निविदम् अधीयन्ते आदित्यो हि निवित् दिशः परिधानीयेत्य् अधिदेवतम् ।
text: This [earth] is the stotriya; Agni the anurupa; VSyu the dhdyyd; the atmosphere the pragdtha; the sky the sukta; the sun the nivid— therefore the Rig-veda scholars study the nivid when [the sun] has risen; for the sun is the tiivid—the quarters the paridhdnlyd. Thus with regard to the divinities.
text_mt:
This [earth] is the stotriya; Agni is the anurūpa; Vāyu is the dhāyyā; the intermediate space is the pragātha; heaven is the sūkta; the sun is the nivid—
therefore the Ṛgvedins recite the nivid when [the sun] has risen;
for the sun is the nivid—
the directions are the paridhānīyā. Thus pertaining to the deities.

sanskrit_iast: athādhyātmam ātmaiva stotriyaḥ prajānurūpaḥ prāṇo dhāyyā manaḥ pragāthaś śiras sūktaṃ cakṣur nivic chrotram paridhānīyā |
meaning: अथाध्यात्मम् आत्मैव स्तोत्रियः प्रजानुरूपः प्राणो धाय्या मनः प्रगाथश् शिरस् सूक्तं चक्षुर् निविच् छ्रोत्रम् परिधानीया ।
text: Now with regard to the self. The self itself is the stotriya; offspring the anurupa; breath the dhdyyd; mind the pragdtha; the head the sukta; sight the/n'yeV^,- heaving the paridhdniyd.
text_mt:
Now pertaining to the self:
The self alone is the stotriya; offspring is the anurūpa; breath is the dhāyyā; mind is the pragātha; the head is the sūkta; the eye is the nivid; the ear is the paridhānīyā.

sanskrit_iast: tad dhaitad eke triṣṭubhā paridadhaty anuṣṭubhaike triṣṭubhā tv eva paridadhyāt |
meaning: तद् धैतद् एके त्रिष्टुभा परिदधत्य् अनुष्टुभैके त्रिष्टुभा त्व् एव परिदध्यात् ।
text: Now some recite its paridhdnlyd with a tristubh, others with an anustubh. But let him recite the paridhdnlyd with a tristubh.
text_mt:
Some conclude it with a triṣṭubh, some with an anuṣṭubh.
One should indeed conclude it with a triṣṭubh.

sanskrit_iast: tad dhaitad eka etā vyāhṛtīr abhivyāhṛtya śaṃsanti mahān mahyā samadhatta devo devyā samadhatta brahma brāhmaṇyā samadhatta tad yat samadhatta samadhatteti |
meaning: तद् धैतद् एक एता व्याहृतीर् अभिव्याहृत्य शंसन्ति महान् मह्या समधत्त देवो देव्या समधत्त ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण्या समधत्त तद् यत् समधत्त समधत्तेति ।
text: That same some chant having uttered these sacred utterances: " He, the great one, united with her, the great one; the god united with the goddess; the brahman united with the brdhmanl. In that he united, he united."
text_mt:
Some recite [the uktha] after uttering these mystic utterances: "The great joined with the great [female]; the god joined with the goddess; the brahman joined with the brāhmaṇī."
Because [they say], "He joined, he joined."

sanskrit_iast: tasmād idānīm puruṣasya śarīrāṇi pratisaṃhitāni puruṣo hy etad uktham |
meaning: तस्माद् इदानीम् पुरुषस्य शरीराणि प्रतिसंहितानि पुरुषो ह्य् एतद् उक्थम् ।
text: Therefore the bodies of men are now united respectively. For man is this uktha.
text_mt:
Therefore now the bodies of a man are joined together;
for the man is this uktha.

sanskrit_iast: mahān mahyā samadhatteti agnir vai mahān iyam eva mahī |
meaning: महान् मह्या समधत्तेति अग्निर् वै महान् इयम् एव मही ।
text: ' He, the great one, united with her, the great one.' Verily Agni is he, the great one, this [earth] is she, the great one.
text_mt:
"The great joined with the great [female]":
Agni is the great; this [earth] is the great [female].

sanskrit_iast: devo devyā samadhatteti vāyur vai devo 'ntarikṣaṃ devī |
meaning: देवो देव्या समधत्तेति वायुर् वै देवो ऽन्तरिक्षं देवी ।
text: 'The god united with the goddess.' Verily Vayu is the god, the atmosphere is the goddess.
text_mt:
"The god joined with the goddess":
Vāyu is the god; the intermediate space is the goddess.

sanskrit_iast: brahma brāhmaṇyā samadhatteti ādityo vai brahma dyaur brāhmaṇī |
meaning: ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण्या समधत्तेति आदित्यो वै ब्रह्म द्यौर् ब्राह्मणी ।
text: ' The brahman united with the brdhmanV Verily the sun is the brahman, the sky is the brdhmanl.
text_mt:
"The brahman joined with the brāhmaṇī":
the sun is the brahman; heaven is the brāhmaṇī.

sanskrit_iast: tāsāṃ vā etāsāṃ devatānāṃ dvayor-dvayor devatayor nava-navākṣarāṇi sampadyante etad ime lokās triṇavā bhavanti |
meaning: तासां वा एतासां देवतानां द्वयोर्-द्वयोर् देवतयोर् नव-नवाक्षराणि सम्पद्यन्ते एतद् इमे लोकास् त्रिणवा भवन्ति ।
text: Of these divinities each two divinities make up nine syllables respectively. Thus these worlds come to be thrice nine.
text_mt:
Of these deities, two deities together make nine syllables;
thus these worlds are ninefold-thrice (triṇava).

sanskrit_iast: tad brahma vai trivṛt tad brahmābhivyāhṛtya śaṃsanti eṣa u eva stomas so 'nucaraḥ |
meaning: तद् ब्रह्म वै त्रिवृत् तद् ब्रह्माभिव्याहृत्य शंसन्ति एष उ एव स्तोमस् सो ऽनुचरः ।
text: Verily that brahman is threefold. Having uttered the sacred utterances they chant unto this brahman. And this is also the stoma, this the anucura (sequel).
text_mt:
The brahman is threefold (trivṛt).
Having uttered that brahman, they recite.
This very stoma is that follower.

sanskrit_iast: yad imam āhur ekastoma ity ayam eva yo 'yam pavate eṣo 'dhidevatam prāṇo 'dhyātmam tasya śarīram anucaraḥ |
meaning: यद् इमम् आहुर् एकस्तोम इत्य् अयम् एव यो ऽयम् पवते एषो ऽधिदेवतम् प्राणो ऽध्यात्मम् तस्य शरीरम् अनुचरः ।
text: When they call him 'possessing one stomal that is he who cleanses here. That [he is] with regard to the divinities; breath [he is] with regard to the self. The anucara is its body.
text_mt:
What they call this one single-stoma (ekastoma) is this one who purifies here [the wind].
This is pertaining to the deities.
Breath is pertaining to the self.
His body is the follower.

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā ha vai maṇau maṇisūtraṃ samprotaṃ syād | prathame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् यथा ह वै मणौ मणिसूत्रं सम्प्रोतं स्याद् । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
text: As the thread of a jewel would be twined in with the jewel,—
text_mt:
Just as a thread would be strung through a jewel—
[This is] the fourth khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ haitasmin sarvam idaṃ samprotaṃ gandharvāpsarasaḥ paśavo manuṣyāḥ |
meaning: एवं हैतस्मिन् सर्वम् इदं सम्प्रोतं गन्धर्वाप्सरसः पशवो मनुष्याः ।
text: — Even so this all is twined in with it, viz. Gandharvas, Apsarases, domestic animals, [and] men.
text_mt: —so upon this all this is strung: the gandharvas and apsarases, animals, and men.

sanskrit_iast: tad dha muñjas sāmaśravasaḥ prayayau tasmai ha śvājanir vaiśyaḥ preyāya |
meaning: तद् ध मुञ्जस् सामश्रवसः प्रययौ तस्मै ह श्वाजनिर् वैश्यः प्रेयाय ।
text: Now Munja Srima5ravasa went forth, Śviijani, a Vaigya, went before him.
text_mt:
Now Muñja Sāmaśravasa set out on a journey.
Towards him Śvājani, a vaiśya, came forward.

sanskrit_iast: tasya hāntarikṣāt patitvā navanītapiṇḍa urasi nipapāta taṃ hādāyānudadhau |
meaning: तस्य हान्तरिक्षात् पतित्वा नवनीतपिण्ड उरसि निपपात तं हादायानुदधौ ।
text: Falling from the atmosphere, a lump of fresh butter fell down on his breast. He, taking it, put it in addition [in the fire (?)].
text_mt:
Having fallen from the intermediate space, a lump of butter dropped upon his chest.
Taking it, he ran after [Muñja].

sanskrit_iast: tato haiva stomaṃ dadarśāntarikṣe vitatam bahu śobhamānam tasyo ha yuktiṃ dadarśa |
meaning: ततो हैव स्तोमं ददर्शान्तरिक्षे विततम् बहु शोभमानम् तस्यो ह युक्तिं ददर्श ।
text: Thereupon he saw the stoma spi-ead out in the atmosphere, greatly shining; he also saw its application (?).
text_mt:
Then indeed he saw the stoma stretched out in the intermediate space, shining greatly;
and he saw its application.

sanskrit_iast: bahiṣpavamānam āsadya ṭītra viyi prāṇya iti kūryāt ṭītra gṛhitra apānya iti vācā didṛkṣetaivākṣibhyaṃ śuśrūṣetaiva karṇābhyām svayam idam manoyuktam |
meaning: बहिष्पवमानम् आसद्य टीत्र वियि प्राण्य इति कूर्यात् टीत्र गृहित्र अपान्य इति वाचा दिदृक्षेतैवाक्षिभ्यं शुश्रूषेतैव कर्णाभ्याम् स्वयम् इदम् मनोयुक्तम् ।
text: Having set himself about the bahispavamdna, he should say fitra viyi prdnya; tUra grhitra apdnya, with speech. He should wish to see with the eyes, he should wish_ to hear with the ears. This is of itself yoked to mind. Now when an arrow is too pointed, verily it then does not hurt. Verily thus he would not attain it. Let him breathe out [saying] simply j>a. As one would attract a deer by means of a mirror, even thus he attracts it (?) by means of this divinity. He (?) performs yoked, and he is yoked also.

sanskrit_iast: tad yatra vā iṣur atyagro bhavati na vai sa tato hinasti tad u vā etaṃ nopāpnuyāt pa ity evāpānyāt tad yathā bimbena mṛgam ānayed evam evainam etayā devatayānayati sa yuktaḥ karoti eṣa evāpi yuktaḥ | prathame 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | prathamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तद् यत्र वा इषुर् अत्यग्रो भवति न वै स ततो हिनस्ति तद् उ वा एतं नोपाप्नुयात् प इत्य् एवापान्यात् तद् यथा बिम्बेन मृगम् आनयेद् एवम् एवैनम् एतया देवतयानयति स युक्तः करोति एष एवापि युक्तः । प्रथमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । प्रथमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text_mt:
Where an arrow is overly sharp, it does not harm from there, nor would it reach this [target].
He should breathe out just with "pa".
Just as one would lead a deer with a reflection/decoy, even so one leads him with this deity.
He acts when yoked;
and this one also is yoked.
[This is] the fifth khaṇḍa in the first anuvāka.
The first anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: yo 'sau sāmnaḥ prattiṃ veda pra hāsmai dīyate |
meaning: यो ऽसौ साम्नः प्रत्तिं वेद प्र हास्मै दीयते ।
text: That one yonder who knows the delivery of the sāman, verily unto him it is delivered,
text_mt: Whoever knows that gift-giving (pratti) of the sāman, to him [wealth] is given forth.

sanskrit_iast: dadā iti ha vā ayam agnir dīpyate tatheti vāyuḥ pavate hanteti candramā om ity ādityaḥ |
meaning: ददा इति ह वा अयम् अग्निर् दीप्यते तथेति वायुः पवते हन्तेति चन्द्रमा ओम् इत्य् आदित्यः ।
text: [Uttering] dadd, this fire here shines; [uttering] tathd, the wind cleanses (blows); hanta the moon [utters], om the sun.
text_mt: "Give!" (dadā) this Agni blazes forth; "So be it!" (tathā) Vāyu blows; "Come!" (hanta) the Moon; "Om!" the sun.

sanskrit_iast: eṣā ha vai sāmnaḥ prattiḥ etāṃ ha vai sāmnaḥ prattiṃ sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir vidāṃ cakāra |
meaning: एषा ह वै साम्नः प्रत्तिः एतां ह वै साम्नः प्रत्तिं सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् विदां चकार ।
text: Verily this is the delivery of the sāman. Verily this delivery of the sāman Sudaksiua Ksfiimi knew.
text_mt:
This indeed is the gift-giving of the sāman.
Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi knew this gift-giving of the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ haitāṃ hotur vājye gāyen maitrāvaruṇasya vā tāṃ dadā3 tathā3 hantā3 him bhā ovā iti pra ha vā asmai dīyate |
meaning: तां हैतां होतुर् वाज्ये गायेन् मैत्रावरुणस्य वा तां ददा3 तथा3 हन्ता3 हिम् भा ओवा इति प्र ह वा अस्मै दीयते ।
text: One should sing that same in the «/»/«-chant hanta, him bhd ovd. Verily it is delivered unto him.
text_mt:
One should sing that in the hotṛ's or the maitrāvaruṇa's vājya [śastra], [chanting] it: "dadā3 tathā3 hantā3 him bhā ovā".
To him indeed [wealth] is given forth.

sanskrit_iast: 'py anyān bahūn uparyupari ya evam etāṃ sāmnaḥ prattiṃ veda |
meaning: ऽप्य् अन्यान् बहून् उपर्युपरि य एवम् एतां साम्नः प्रत्तिं वेद ।
text: He is much superior to even many others who thus knows this delivery of the sāman.
text_mt: He [surpasses] even many others, higher and higher—he who thus knows this gift-giving of the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: ya u ha vā abandhur bandhumat sāma veda yatra hāpy enaṃ na vidur yatra roṣanti yatra parīva cakṣate tad dhāpi śraiṣṭhyam ādhipatyam annādyam purodhām paryeti |
meaning: य उ ह वा अबन्धुर् बन्धुमत् साम वेद यत्र हाप्य् एनं न विदुर् यत्र रोषन्ति यत्र परीव चक्षते तद् धापि श्रैष्ठ्यम् आधिपत्यम् अन्नाद्यम् पुरोधाम् पर्येति ।
text: And whoso being without relatives knows the sdmany:\cS\ in relatives, even where they do not know him, where they are angry at him, where they overlook liim, as it were, he thus compasses excellence, supremacy, food-eating, [and] the office of &purohita.
text_mt: And he who knows the sāman having relatives though having no relative—even where they do not know him, where they are angry with him, where they speak ill of him—even there he attains pre-eminence, overlordship, abundance of food, and priesthood.

sanskrit_iast: agnir ha vā abandhur bandhumat sāma kasmād vā hy enaṃ dārvoḥ kasmād vā paryāvṛtya manthanti sa śraiṣṭhyāyādhipatyāyānnādyāya purodhāyai jāyate |
meaning: अग्निर् ह वा अबन्धुर् बन्धुमत् साम कस्माद् वा ह्य् एनं दार्वोः कस्माद् वा पर्यावृत्य मन्थन्ति स श्रैष्ठ्यायाधिपत्यायान्नाद्याय पुरोधायै जायते ।
text: Verily Agni, being without relatives, is the sāman rich in relatives. For in whatever way they churn him, from the wood, or by turning, he is born for excellence, for supremacy, for food-eating, [and] for the office of a purohita.
text_mt:
Agni indeed is the sāman having relatives though having no relative.
For why, turning it round and round, do they churn him from two pieces of wood? He is born for pre-eminence, overlordship, abundance of food, and priesthood.

sanskrit_iast: sa yatra ha vā apy evaṃvidaṃ na vidur yatra roṣanti yatra parīva cakṣate tad dhāpi śraiṣṭhyam ādhipatyam annādyam purodhām paryeti | dvitīye 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स यत्र ह वा अप्य् एवंविदं न विदुर् यत्र रोषन्ति यत्र परीव चक्षते तद् धापि श्रैष्ठ्यम् आधिपत्यम् अन्नाद्यम् पुरोधाम् पर्येति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: Verily even where they do not know one knowing thus, where they are angry at him, where they so to speak overlook him, he thus compasses excellence, supremacy, food-eating, [and] the office of & purohita.
text_mt:
And when they do not recognise such a knower, when they are angry, when they censure him, even then he attains pre-eminence, lordship, eating of food, and the office of domestic priest.
First khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: svayam u tatra yatrainaṃ viduḥ |
meaning: स्वयम् उ तत्र यत्रैनं विदुः ।
text: And [that happens] of itself where they know him.
text_mt: Naturally so where they do recognise him.

sanskrit_iast: sudakṣiṇo ha vai kṣaimiḥ prācīnaśālir jābālau te ha sabrahmacāriṇa āsuḥ |
meaning: सुदक्षिणो ह वै क्षैमिः प्राचीनशालिर् जाबालौ ते ह सब्रह्मचारिण आसुः ।
text: Sudaksina Ksaimi, Pracinagali, the two Jabalas—they were fellow-students.
text_mt: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi, Prācīnaśāli, and the two Jābālas were fellow-students of sacred knowledge.

sanskrit_iast: te heme bahu japyasya cānyasya cānūcire prācīnaśāliś ca jābālau ca |
meaning: ते हेमे बहु जप्यस्य चान्यस्य चानूचिरे प्राचीनशालिश् च जाबालौ च ।
text: These, viz. Pracinagali and the two Jabalas, recited much of what is to be muttered and of other [prayers].
text_mt: Now these—Prācīnaśāli and the two Jābālas—had studied much of what is to be muttered and of other things.

sanskrit_iast: atha ha sma sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir yad eva yajñasyāñjo yat suviditaṃ tad dha smaiva pṛcchati |
meaning: अथ ह स्म सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् यद् एव यज्ञस्याञ्जो यत् सुविदितं तद् ध स्मैव पृच्छति ।
text: Then Sudaksina Ksaimi used to ask [them] concerning that which is easy of the sacrifice, concerning that which is well known,
text_mt: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi, on the other hand, used to inquire only into what was the direct path of the sacrifice, what was well understood.

sanskrit_iast: ta u ha vā apoditā vyākrośamānāś ceruś śūdro duranūcāna iti ha sma sudakṣiṇaṃ kṣaimim ākrośanti prācīnaśāliś ca jābālau ca |
meaning: त उ ह वा अपोदिता व्याक्रोशमानाश् चेरुश् शूद्रो दुरनूचान इति ह स्म सुदक्षिणं क्षैमिम् आक्रोशन्ति प्राचीनशालिश् च जाबालौ च ।
text: And they, being distracted, kept crying out: " Śudra, ignoramus!" Thus they, viz. Priiclnagali and the two Jabalas, used to cry out against Sudaksina Ksaimi.
text_mt: Being slighted, they went about reviling him. "A Śūdra, an incompetent scholar!" Prācīnaśāli and the two Jābālas thus kept reviling Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha smāha sudakṣiṇaḥ kṣaimir yatra bhūyiṣṭhāḥ kurupañcālās samāgatā bhavitāras tan na eṣa saṃvādo nānupadṛṣṭe śūdrā iva saṃvadiṣyāmaha iti |
meaning: स ह स्माह सुदक्षिणः क्षैमिर् यत्र भूयिष्ठाः कुरुपञ्चालास् समागता भवितारस् तन् न एष संवादो नानुपदृष्टे शूद्रा इव संवदिष्यामह इति ।
text: Then Sudaksina Ksaimi used to say: "Where most of the Kurupaiiealas shall be assembled together, there shall be this disputation of ours; we will not dispute without witnesses, like Śtiiiras."
text_mt: Sudakṣiṇa Kṣaimi said: "Where the most Kuru-Pañcālas are assembled, there our debate shall take place. We will not debate like Śūdras out of sight."

sanskrit_iast: tā u ha vai jābālau didīkṣāte śukraś ca gośruś ca tayor ha prācīnaśālir vṛta udgātā |
meaning: ता उ ह वै जाबालौ दिदीक्षाते शुक्रश् च गोश्रुश् च तयोर् ह प्राचीनशालिर् वृत उद्गाता ।
text: Now the two Jabalas, Śukra and Gogru, consecrated themselves. Of them Pracinagali [was] chosen udgdtar.
text_mt:
Then the two Jābālas, Śukra and Gośru, underwent consecration [for a sacrifice].
Prācīnaśāli was chosen as their udgātṛ.

sanskrit_iast: sa tad dha sudakṣiṇo 'nububudhe jābālau hādīkṣiṣātām iti sa ha saṃgrahītāram uvācānayasvāre jābālau hādīkṣiṣātāṃ tad gamiṣyāva iti | dvitīye 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स तद् ध सुदक्षिणो ऽनुबुबुधे जाबालौ हादीक्षिषाताम् इति स ह संग्रहीतारम् उवाचानयस्वारे जाबालौ हादीक्षिषातां तद् गमिष्याव इति । द्वितीये ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: Then Sudaksina became aware: " The two Jabalas have consecrated themselves." He said to his driver: '' Sirrah, conduct [me thither]. The two Jabalas have consecrated themselves. Thither we will go."
text_mt:
Sudakṣiṇa perceived this: "The two Jābālas have undergone consecration."
He said to his charioteer: "Bring [the chariot] near, friend; the two Jābālas have undergone consecration; thither we two will go."
Second khaṇḍa in the second anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tasya ha jñātikā aśrumukhā ivāsur anyatarāṃ vā ayam upāgād iti |
meaning: तस्य ह ज्ञातिका अश्रुमुखा इवासुर् अन्यतरां वा अयम् उपागाद् इति ।
text: Now his relatives were tear-faced, as it were [saying]: " This one hath gone unto one or the other."
text_mt: His kinsmen were as if tearful, thinking: "He has undertaken one or the other [perilous contest]."

sanskrit_iast: atha ha sma vai yaḥ purā brahmavādyaṃ vadaty anyatarām upāgād iti ha smainam manyante atho ha smainam mṛtam ivaivopāsate |
meaning: अथ ह स्म वै यः पुरा ब्रह्मवाद्यं वदत्य् अन्यतराम् उपागाद् इति ह स्मैनम् मन्यन्ते अथो ह स्मैनम् मृतम् इवैवोपासते ।
text: Now whenever one formerly engaged in a theological disputation, they used to think of him: " He hath gone unto one or the other;" and they used to wait on him as on one dead.
text_mt:
For in ancient times, when anyone engaged in a theological disputation, they thought: "He has undertaken one or the other [survival or destruction]."
And they treated him as if he were already dead.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ ha saṃgrahītovācātha yad bhagavas te tābhyāṃ na kuśalaṃ kathettham āttheti |
meaning: तं ह संग्रहीतोवाचाथ यद् भगवस् ते ताभ्यां न कुशलं कथेत्थम् आत्थेति ।
text: The driver said to him: " Since, sir, thou art not on good terms with these two, why dost thou speak thus?"
text_mt: The charioteer said to him: "Sir, since you are not on good terms with them, why do you speak thus?"

sanskrit_iast: om iti hovāca gantavyam ma ācāryas suyamān amanyateti |
meaning: ओम् इति होवाच गन्तव्यम् म आचार्यस् सुयमान् अमन्यतेति ।
text: "Yes," he said, "I must go; the teacher thought [them] easily governed."
text_mt: "Om," he said, "I must go; my teacher considered me easy to guide."

sanskrit_iast: sa ha ratham āsthāya pradhāvayāṃ cakāra taṃ ha sma pratīkṣante |
meaning: स ह रथम् आस्थाय प्रधावयां चकार तं ह स्म प्रतीक्षन्ते ।
text: He, mounting the chariot, drove off. They catch sight of him.
text_mt:
Mounting the chariot, he drove forward.
They looked toward him:

sanskrit_iast: kaṃ jānīteti sudakṣiṇa iti na vai nūnaṃ sa idam abhyaveyād iti sa eveti |
meaning: कं जानीतेति सुदक्षिण इति न वै नूनं स इदम् अभ्यवेयाद् इति स एवेति ।
text: "Do you know who this is?" "Sudaksina." " May he not come down hither now." " [It is] just he."
text_mt:
"Whom do you recognise?"
"Sudakṣiṇa."
"Surely he would not come down here!"
"It is he indeed."

sanskrit_iast: sa ha sopānād evāntarvedy avasthāyovācāṅga nv itthaṃ gṛhapatā3 iti taṃ ha nānūdatiṣṭhāsat sa hovācānūtthātā ma edhi kṛṣṇājino 'sīti tad ime kurupañcālā avidur anūtthātaiva ta iti hocuḥ |
meaning: स ह सोपानाद् एवान्तर्वेद्य् अवस्थायोवाचाङ्ग न्व् इत्थं गृहपता3 इति तं ह नानूदतिष्ठासत् स होवाचानूत्थाता म एधि कृष्णाजिनो ऽसीति तद् इमे कुरुपञ्चाला अविदुर् अनूत्थातैव त इति होचुः ।
text: He, descending from the steps within the sacred enclosure, said: " Verily now is it thus, O householder?" He did not wish to attend upon him. He said: "Be thou attending upon me; thou art [dressed] in the skin of a black antelope." These Kurupancalas knew this. "He is thy attendant," they said.
text_mt:
Remaining in his shoes, he stood inside the sacrificial altar ground and said: "Well now, householder!"
He would not stand up for him.
He said: "Rise up for me! You are wearing a black antelope skin."
These Kuru-Pañcālas realised that, and said: "Rise up indeed for him!"

sanskrit_iast: taṃ ha kanīyān bhrātovācānūttiṣṭha bhagava udgātāram iti taṃ hānūttasthau |
meaning: तं ह कनीयान् भ्रातोवाचानूत्तिष्ठ भगव उद्गातारम् इति तं हानूत्तस्थौ ।
text: His younger brother said to him: " Sir, attend upon the udgdtar." He attended upon him.
text_mt:
The younger brother said to him: "Sir, rise up for the udgātṛ."
He rose up for him.

sanskrit_iast: sa hovāca trir vai gṛhapate puruṣo jāyate pitur evāgre 'dhi jāyate 'tha mātur atha yajñāt |
meaning: स होवाच त्रिर् वै गृहपते पुरुषो जायते पितुर् एवाग्रे ऽधि जायते ऽथ मातुर् अथ यज्ञात् ।
