Therefore, both gods and men bring nourishment to you truly.
He who knows you thus becomes an eater of food.

sanskrit_iast: sambhūr devo 'si sam aham bhūyāsam ābhūtir asy ābhūyāsam bhūtir asi bhūyāsam |
meaning: सम्भूर् देवो ऽसि सम् अहम् भूयासम् आभूतिर् अस्य् आभूयासम् भूतिर् असि भूयासम् ।
text_mt:
You are the deity Sambhū; may I be fully united.
You are Ābhūti; may I fully become.
You are Bhūti; may I prosper.

sanskrit_iast: yās te prajā upadiṣṭā nāhaṃ tava tāḥ paryemi upa te tā diśāmi |
meaning: यास् ते प्रजा उपदिष्टा नाहं तव ताः पर्येमि उप ते ता दिशामि ।
text_mt:
The creatures of yours that are pointed out, I do not bypass them of yours;
I point them out to you.

sanskrit_iast: mano me reto me prajā me punassambhūtir me tan me tvayi tan me mopahṛthā iti candramasam avocat |
meaning: मनो मे रेतो मे प्रजा मे पुनस्सम्भूतिर् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे मोपहृथा इति चन्द्रमसम् अवोचत् ।
text: "My mind, my seed, my offspring, my second birth: that of me is in thee. Do not take that of me unto thee," thus he said to the moon.
text_mt: My mind, my semen, my offspring, my rebirth—that of mine is in you; do not take that away from me,” he said to the Moon.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ tathaivāgataṃ candramāḥ pratinandaty ayaṃ te bhagavo lokaḥ saha nāv ayaṃ loka iti |
meaning: तं तथैवागतं चन्द्रमाः प्रतिनन्दत्य् अयं ते भगवो लोकः सह नाव् अयं लोक इति ।
text: Him having come thus the moon joyfully receives [saying]: "Thine is this world, reverend sir. This world is ours in common." i«. = 20. 7.
text_mt: When he has arrived in this way, the Moon welcomes him: “This is your world, venerable sir; this world is ours together.”

sanskrit_iast: yad vāva me tvayīty āha tad vāva me punar dehīti |
meaning: यद् वाव मे त्वयीत्य् आह तद् वाव मे पुनर् देहीति ।
text: " What now of thee is there in me?" "My mind, my seed, my offspring, my second birth: that of me is in thee. Give that back to me." That the moon gives back to him.
text_mt: He says: “Whatever of mine is in you, give that back to me.”

sanskrit_iast: kiṃ nu te mayīti mano me reto me prajā me punassambhūtir me tan me tvayi tan me punar dehīti tad asmai candramāḥ punar dadāti |
meaning: किं नु ते मयीति मनो मे रेतो मे प्रजा मे पुनस्सम्भूतिर् मे तन् मे त्वयि तन् मे पुनर् देहीति तद् अस्मै चन्द्रमाः पुनर् ददाति ।
text: He says to it: " Carry me forth."
text_mt:
“What then of yours is in me?”
“My mind, my semen, my offspring, my rebirth—
that of mine is in you;
give that back to me.”
The Moon gives that back to him.

sanskrit_iast: tam āha pra mā vaheti | pañcame 'nuvāke 'ṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तम् आह प्र मा वहेति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके ऽष्टमः खण्डः ।
text_mt:
He says to him: “Convey me forward.”
Eighth section in the fifth lesson.

sanskrit_iast: kim abhīti brahmaṇo lokam iti tam ādityam abhipravahati |
meaning: किम् अभीति ब्रह्मणो लोकम् इति तम् आदित्यम् अभिप्रवहति ।
text: "To what?" "To the world of brahman." It carries him forth to the sun.
text_mt:
“Towards what?”
“Towards the world of Brahman.”
He conveys him towards Āditya.

sanskrit_iast: sa ādityam āha pra mā vaheti kim abhīti brahmaṇo lokam iti taṃ candramasam abhipravahati sa evam ete devate anusaṃcarati |
meaning: स आदित्यम् आह प्र मा वहेति किम् अभीति ब्रह्मणो लोकम् इति तं चन्द्रमसम् अभिप्रवहति स एवम् एते देवते अनुसंचरति ।
text: He says to the sun: " Carry me forth." " To what?" " To the world of brahman." It carries him forth to the moon. He thus wanders to and fro between these divinities,
text_mt:
He says to Āditya: “Convey me forward.”
“Towards what?”
“Towards the world of Brahman.”
He conveys him towards the Moon.
In this way he travels between these two deities.

sanskrit_iast: eso 'nto 'taḥ paraḥ pravāho nāsti yān u kāṃś cātaḥ prāco lokān abhyavādiṣma te sarva āptā bhavanti te jitās teṣv asya sarveṣu kāmacāro bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: एसो ऽन्तो ऽतः परः प्रवाहो नास्ति यान् उ कांश् चातः प्राचो लोकान् अभ्यवादिष्म ते सर्व आप्ता भवन्ति ते जितास् तेष्व् अस्य सर्वेषु कामचारो भवति य एवं वेद ।
text: This is the end. There is no carrying forth beyond this [limit]. And all the worlds beyond this [limit] of which we have spoken, they are all obtained, they are conquered, in all of them there is unrestricted movement for him who knows thus.
text_mt:
This is the end; beyond this there is no carrying forward.
Whatever worlds east of this we have mentioned, all of them become attained, they are won; in all of them he has freedom of movement according to his desire, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: sa yadi kāmayeta punar ihājāyeyeti yasmin kule 'bhidhyāyed yadi brāhmaṇakule yadi rājakule tasminn ājāyate sa etam eva lokam punaḥ prajānann abhyārohann eti |
meaning: स यदि कामयेत पुनर् इहाजायेयेति यस्मिन् कुले ऽभिध्यायेद् यदि ब्राह्मणकुले यदि राजकुले तस्मिन्न् आजायते स एतम् एव लोकम् पुनः प्रजानन्न् अभ्यारोहन्न् एति ।
text: If he should wish: " May I be born here again," on whatever family he might fix his thoughts, be it a Brahman-family, be it a royal family, into that he is born. He keeps on ascending to this world again fore-knowing,
text_mt:
If he should desire: “May I be born here again,” into whatever family he sets his mind—whether into a family of Brahmins or into a family of kings—into that he is born.
Knowing again, he goes climbing up into this very world.

sanskrit_iast: tad u hovāca śāṭyāyanir bahuvyāhito vā ayam bahuśo lokaḥ etasya vai kāmāya nu bruvate śrāmyanti vā ka etat prāsya punar iheyād atraiva syād iti | pañcame 'nuvāke navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ pañcamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तद् उ होवाच शाट्यायनिर् बहुव्याहितो वा अयम् बहुशो लोकः एतस्य वै कामाय नु ब्रुवते श्राम्यन्ति वा क एतत् प्रास्य पुनर् इहेयाद् अत्रैव स्याद् इति । पञ्चमे ऽनुवाके नवमः खण्डः पञ्चमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: And Śatyayani said: " Ofttimes, indeed, this world here is very ill. Now for the sake of it they talk to each other or toil [saying]: ' Who having thrown that away would come here again? he would be only there.'"
text_mt:
And on this Śāṭyāyani used to say: “Truly this world has many obstacles in many ways.
Indeed, for the sake of desire for this [higher state] do they speak or exert themselves; who, having cast this away, would come back here? One should remain right there.”
Ninth section in the fifth lesson.
The fifth lesson is complete.

sanskrit_iast: uccaiśśravā ha kaupayeyaḥ kauravyo rājāsa tasya ha keśī dārbhyaḥ pāñcālo rājā svasrīya āsa tau hānyonyasya priyāv āsatuḥ |
meaning: उच्चैश्श्रवा ह कौपयेयः कौरव्यो राजास तस्य ह केशी दार्भ्यः पाञ्चालो राजा स्वस्रीय आस तौ हान्योन्यस्य प्रियाव् आसतुः ।
text: Uccai59ravas Kaupayeya was a king of the Kurus. Now Ke9in Darbhya, king of the Pancalas, was his sister's son. And they were dear to each other.
text_mt:
Uccaiḥśravas Kaupayeya was a king of the Kurus.
Keśin Dārbhya, king of the Pañcālas, was his sister’s son.
The two were dear to one another.

sanskrit_iast: sa hoccaiśśravāḥ kaupayeyo 'smāl lokāt preyāya tasmin ha prete keśī dārbhyo 'raṇye mṛgayāṃ cacārāpriyaṃ vininīṣamāṇaḥ |
meaning: स होच्चैश्श्रवाः कौपयेयो ऽस्माल् लोकात् प्रेयाय तस्मिन् ह प्रेते केशी दार्भ्यो ऽरण्ये मृगयां चचाराप्रियं विनिनीषमाणः ।
text: This Uccaiggravas Kaupayeya departed from this world. When he had departed, Ke9in Darbhya went hunting in the woods, wishing to remove his sadness.
text_mt:
That Uccaiḥśravas Kaupayeya departed from this world.
When he had died, Keśin Dārbhya roamed in the forest on a hunt, wishing to dispel his grief.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha tathaiva palyayamāno mṛgān prasarann antareṇaivoccaiśśravasaṃ kaupayeyam adhijagāma |
meaning: स ह तथैव पल्ययमानो मृगान् प्रसरन्न् अन्तरेणैवोच्चैश्श्रवसं कौपयेयम् अधिजगाम ।
text: While he was thus roaming about, chasing deer, he perceived just between [himself and the game] Uccai§9ravas Kaupayeya.
text_mt: Rushing along in that very manner, pursuing the wild beasts, he came right upon Uccaiśśravas Kaupayeya.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hovāca dṛpyāmi svī3j jānāmīti na dṛpyasīti hovāca jānāsi sa evāsmi yam mā manyasa iti |
meaning: तं होवाच दृप्यामि स्वी3ज् जानामीति न दृप्यसीति होवाच जानासि स एवास्मि यम् मा मन्यस इति ।
text: He said to him: " Am I really crazy, [or] do I know?" "Thou art not crazy," he (U.) said, "thou knoVest. I am he whom thou thinkest me to be."
text_mt:
He said to him: "Am I mad, or do I recognise [you]?"
"You are not mad," he said, "you recognise [me]. I am indeed he whom you think me to be."

sanskrit_iast: atha yad bhagava āhur iti hovāca ya āvir bhavaty anye 'sya lokam upayantīty atha katham aśako ma āvir bhavitum iti |
meaning: अथ यद् भगव आहुर् इति होवाच य आविर् भवत्य् अन्ये ऽस्य लोकम् उपयन्तीत्य् अथ कथम् अशको म आविर् भवितुम् इति ।
text: " Now since they say, reverend sir," he (K.) said, "'if one becometh manifest, others go to his world,' how then hast thou been able to become manifest unto me?"
text_mt: "Now, revered sir, they say," he said, "'He who becomes manifest—others enter into his world.' How then were you able to become manifest to me?"

sanskrit_iast: om iti hovāca yadā vai tasya lokasya goptāram avide 'tas ta āvir abhūvam apriyaṃ cāsya vineṣyāmy anu cainaṃ śāsiṣyāmīti |
meaning: ओम् इति होवाच यदा वै तस्य लोकस्य गोप्तारम् अविदे ऽतस् त आविर् अभूवम् अप्रियं चास्य विनेष्याम्य् अनु चैनं शासिष्यामीति ।
text: " Yes," he (IT.) said; " when I have found the keeper of that world, thereupon I have become manifest unto thee [thinking]: 'I will remove his sadness and I will teach him.'"
text_mt: "Om," he said. "When indeed I found a guardian for that world, then I became manifest to you, [thinking:] 'I shall dispel his sorrow and instruct him.'"

sanskrit_iast: tathā bhagava iti hovāca taṃ vai nu tvā pariṣvajā iti taṃ ha sma pariṣvajamāno yathā dhūmaṃ vāpīyād vāyuṃ vākāśaṃ vāgnyarciṃ vāpo vaivaṃ ha smainaṃ vyeti na ha smainam pariṣvaṅgāyopalabhate | ṣaṣthe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तथा भगव इति होवाच तं वै नु त्वा परिष्वजा इति तं ह स्म परिष्वजमानो यथा धूमं वापीयाद् वायुं वाकाशं वाग्न्यर्चिं वापो वैवं ह स्मैनं व्येति न ह स्मैनम् परिष्वङ्गायोपलभते । षष्थे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: "Even so, reverend sir," he (K.) said; "verily now let me embrace thee." When he [tried to] embrace him, as if one were to approach smoke, or wind, or space, or the gleam of fire, or water, even thus he escaped him. He [could] not take hold of him for an embrace.
text_mt:
"So be it, revered sir," he said. "Let me then embrace you."
Whenever he embraced him, he slipped away from him just as one might pass through smoke, or wind, or space, or the flame of a fire, or water. He could not grasp him in an embrace.
First subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: sa hovāca yad vai te purā rūpam āsīt tat te rūpam na tu tvā pariṣvaṅgāyopalabha iti |
meaning: स होवाच यद् वै ते पुरा रूपम् आसीत् तत् ते रूपम् न तु त्वा परिष्वङ्गायोपलभ इति ।
text: He (K.) said: " Verily, what appearance thou hadst formerly, that appearance thou hast [even now]; yet I [can] not take hold of thee for an embrace."
text_mt: He said: "That form which was yours of old is your form; but I cannot grasp you in an embrace."

sanskrit_iast: om iti hovāca brāhmaṇo vai me sāma vidvān sāmnodagāyat sa me 'śarīreṇa sāmnā śarīrāṇy adhūnot tad yasya vai kila sāma vidvān sāmnodgāyati devatānām eva salokatāṃ gamayatīti |
meaning: ओम् इति होवाच ब्राह्मणो वै मे साम विद्वान् साम्नोदगायत् स मे ऽशरीरेण साम्ना शरीराण्य् अधूनोत् तद् यस्य वै किल साम विद्वान् साम्नोद्गायति देवतानाम् एव सलोकतां गमयतीति ।
text: "Yes," he (U.) said; "a Brahman who knew the sāman sang the udgītha for me with the sāman. By means of the bodiless sāman he shook off my bodies. 80. ' A. 'va. ' we. ' -goyo. ^ 'palabhate, e cancelled in red. ^ -rarany. Verily, whose udgītha one who knoweth the sāman singeth with the saw«w, him he causeth to go to the same world with the divinities."
text_mt: "Om," he said. "A brāhmaṇa who knew the sāman chanted the udgītha for me with the sāman; with the bodiless sāman he shook off my bodies. For when one who knows the sāman chants the udgītha for a man with the sāman, he causes him to attain sharing the same world with the deities."

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgaḥ prājāpatya iti hovāca prajāpateḥ priyaḥ putra āsa sa tasmā etat sāmābravīt tena sa ṛṣīṇām udagāyat ta eta ṛṣayo dhūtaśarīrā iti |
meaning: पतङ्गः प्राजापत्य इति होवाच प्रजापतेः प्रियः पुत्र आस स तस्मा एतत् सामाब्रवीत् तेन स ऋषीणाम् उदगायत् त एत ऋषयो धूतशरीरा इति ।
text: " Patariga Prajapatya," he said, " was a dear son of Prajapati. To him he told this sāman. With it he sang the ndgltha of (for) the sages {rsi). [Thus] these same sages have shaken off their bodies.
text_mt: "Pataṅga Prājāpatya," he said, "was Prajāpati's beloved son. To him he spoke this sāman. With it he chanted the udgītha for the seers. Those seers [yonder] have had their bodies shaken off."

sanskrit_iast: eteno eva sāmneti hovāca prajāpatir devānām udagāyat ta eta upari devā dhūtaśarīrā iti |
meaning: एतेनो एव साम्नेति होवाच प्रजापतिर् देवानाम् उदगायत् त एत उपरि देवा धूतशरीरा इति ।
text: And with this sāman," he said, "Prajapati sang the udgītha of (for) the gods. [Thus] these same gods above have shaken off their bodies."
text_mt: "With this very sāman," he said, "Prajāpati chanted the udgītha for the gods. Those gods above have had their bodies shaken off."

sanskrit_iast: tasmin hainam anuśaśāsa taṃ hānuśiṣyovāca yas smaivaitat sāma vidyāt sa smaiva ta udgāyatv iti |
meaning: तस्मिन् हैनम् अनुशशास तं हानुशिष्योवाच यस् स्मैवैतत् साम विद्यात् स स्मैव त उद्गायत्व् इति ।
text: In this he (TJ.) instructed him (K.). Having instructed him, he said: " Whoever shall know this sāman, let only him sing the udgītha for thee."
text_mt: In this he instructed him. Having instructed him, he said: "Only he who knows this sāman shall chant the udgītha for you."

sanskrit_iast: sa hānuśiṣṭa ājagāma sa ha sma kurupañcālānām brāhmaṇān upapṛcchamānaś carati | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स हानुशिष्ट आजगाम स ह स्म कुरुपञ्चालानाम् ब्राह्मणान् उपपृच्छमानश् चरति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: He, being instructed, returned. He went about asking questions of the Brahmans of the Kurus and Pancalas.
text_mt:
Having been instructed, he returned. He went about inquiring among the brāhmaṇas of the Kuru-Pañcālas.
Second subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: vyūḍhacchandasā vai dvādaśāhena yakṣyamāṇo 'smi sa yo vas tat sāma veda yad ahaṃ veda sa eva ma udgāsyati mīmāṃsadhvam iti |
meaning: व्यूढच्छन्दसा वै द्वादशाहेन यक्ष्यमाणो ऽस्मि स यो वस् तत् साम वेद यद् अहं वेद स एव म उद्गास्यति मीमांसध्वम् इति ।
text: [He said:] "lam going to sacrifice with a twelveday sacrifice having its metres transposed. Who of you knoweth that sāman which I know, he alone shall sing the udgītha for me. Ponder!"
text_mt: "I am going to sacrifice with a twelve-day rite with shifted metres. He among you who knows that sāman which I know, he alone shall chant the udgītha for me. Reflect upon it!"

sanskrit_iast: tasmai ha mīmāṃsamānānām ekaś cana sampraty abhidadhāti |
meaning: तस्मै ह मीमांसमानानाम् एकश् चन सम्प्रत्य् अभिदधाति ।
text: Of them pondering not one answered him precisely,
text_mt: To him, as they were reflecting, not a single one correctly explained it.

sanskrit_iast: sa ha tathaiva palyayamānaś śmaśāne vā vane vāvṛtīśayānam upādhāvayāṃ cakāra taṃ ha cāyamānaḥ prajahau |
meaning: स ह तथैव पल्ययमानश् श्मशाने वा वने वावृतीशयानम् उपाधावयां चकार तं ह चायमानः प्रजहौ ।
text: He wandering about in the same way, drove up unto one lying covered in a cemetery or a grove. Fearing him he (P.) started away.
text_mt: Rushing along in that very manner, he drove up to someone lying down wrapped in garments in a cremation ground or in the forest; and observing him, he turned aside.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hovāca ko 'sīti brāhmaṇo 'smi prātṛdo bhālla iti |
meaning: तं होवाच को ऽसीति ब्राह्मणो ऽस्मि प्रातृदो भाल्ल इति ।
text: He (K.) said to him: " Who art thou?" "lam a Brahman, Pratrda Bhalla."
text_mt:
He said to him: "Who are you?"
"I am a brāhmaṇa, Prātṛda Bhālla."

sanskrit_iast: sa kiṃ vettheti sāmeti |
meaning: स किं वेत्थेति सामेति ।
text: " As such what dost thou know?" "The sāman."
text_mt:
"What do you know?"
"The sāman."

sanskrit_iast: om iti hovāca vyūḍhacchandasā vai dvādaśāhena yakṣyamāṇo 'smi sa yadi tvaṃ tat sāma vettha yad ahaṃ veda tvam eva ma udgāsyasi mīmāṃsasveti |
meaning: ओम् इति होवाच व्यूढच्छन्दसा वै द्वादशाहेन यक्ष्यमाणो ऽस्मि स यदि त्वं तत् साम वेत्थ यद् अहं वेद त्वम् एव म उद्गास्यसि मीमांसस्वेति ।
text: "Very well," he (K.) said; "lam going to sacrifice with a twelve-day sacrifice having its metres transposed. If thou knowest that sāman which I know, thou shalt sing the udgītha for me. Ponder."
text_mt: "Om," he said. "I am going to sacrifice with a twelve-day rite with shifted metres. If you know that sāman which I know, you alone shall chant the udgītha for me. Reflect upon it!"

sanskrit_iast: tasmai ha mīmāṃsamānas tad eva sampraty abhidadhau |
meaning: तस्मै ह मीमांसमानस् तद् एव सम्प्रत्य् अभिदधौ ।
text: He, pondering, answered him that precisely,
text_mt: To him, upon reflecting, he correctly explained that very thing.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hovācāyam ma udgāsyatīti |
meaning: तं होवाचायम् म उद्गास्यतीति ।
text: He (K) said to him: " This one here shall sing the udgītha for me."
text_mt: He said to him: "This one shall chant the udgītha for me."

sanskrit_iast: tasmai ha kurupañcālānām brāhmaṇā asūyanta āhur eṣu ha vā ayaṃ kulyeṣu satsūdgāsyati kasmā ayam alam iti |
meaning: तस्मै ह कुरुपञ्चालानाम् ब्राह्मणा असूयन्त आहुर् एषु ह वा अयं कुल्येषु सत्सूद्गास्यति कस्मा अयम् अलम् इति ।
text: Complaining of him the Brahmans of the Kurus and Pancalas said: " While those here are of the family, shall he sing the udgītha? To whom is he acceptable?"
text_mt: The brāhmaṇas of the Kuru-Pañcālas, envying him, said: "Will he chant the udgītha when these of noble lineage are present? For what is he competent?"

sanskrit_iast: alam nvai mahyam iti ha smāha saivālam masyālam matāyaitasya hālam evojjagau tasmād ālamyailājodgātety ākhyāpayanti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: अलम् न्वै मह्यम् इति ह स्माह सैवालम् मस्यालम् मतायैतस्य हालम् एवोज्जगौ तस्माद् आलम्यैलाजोद्गातेत्य् आख्यापयन्ति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
text: " Verily, he is acceptable (alam) to me," he (K.) said; he sang his udgītha acceptably (alam!). Therefore they call him
text_mt:
"He is indeed competent for me," he said. He was competent for him who regarded him as competent; and he chanted the udgītha with competence for him. Therefore they declare: "Ālamya Ilāja was the udgātṛ."
Third subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tad dha sātyakīrtā āhur yāṃ vayaṃ devatām upāsmaha ekam eva vayaṃ tasyai devatāyai rūpaṃ gavy ādiśāma ekaṃ vāhana ekaṃ hastiny ekam puruṣa ekaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tasyā evedaṃ devatāyai sarvaṃ rūpam iti |
meaning: तद् ध सात्यकीर्ता आहुर् यां वयं देवताम् उपास्मह एकम् एव वयं तस्यै देवतायै रूपं गव्य् आदिशाम एकं वाहन एकं हस्तिन्य् एकम् पुरुष एकं सर्वेषु भूतेषु तस्या एवेदं देवतायै सर्वं रूपम् इति ।
text: This the Satyaklrtas say: "As'to the divinity which we worship, of that divinity we point out one form to be in the cow, one in a draught-animal, one in the elephant, one in man, one in all creatures. This is the complete form of this divinity."
text_mt: As to that, the Sātyakīrtas say: "Whichever deity we revere, we designate one and the same form of that deity in cattle, one in the draft-animal, one in the elephant, one in man, one in all beings. All this is the form of that deity alone."

sanskrit_iast: tad etad ekam eva rūpam prāṇa eva yāvad dhy eva prāṇena prāṇiti tāvad rūpam bhavati tad rūpam bhavati |
meaning: तद् एतद् एकम् एव रूपम् प्राण एव यावद् ध्य् एव प्राणेन प्राणिति तावद् रूपम् भवति तद् रूपम् भवति ।
text: That same one form is breath. For as long as one breathes with breath so long there is form; that is form.
text_mt: That single form is breath alone; for as long as one breathes with the breath, so long there is form, then there is form.

sanskrit_iast: tad atha yadā prāṇa utkrāmati dārv eveva bhūto 'narthyaḥ pariśiṣyate na kiṃ cana rūpam |
meaning: तद् अथ यदा प्राण उत्क्रामति दार्व् एवेव भूतो ऽनर्थ्यः परिशिष्यते न किं चन रूपम् ।
text: And when breath departs he is left useless, having become just like a log, [and] no form whatever [is left].
text_mt: Then, when the breath departs, one remains as if turned to a block of wood, useless—there is no form whatsoever.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāntarātmā tapaḥ tasmāt tapyamānasyoṣṇataraḥ prāṇo bhavati |
meaning: तस्यान्तरात्मा तपः तस्मात् तप्यमानस्योष्णतरः प्राणो भवति ।
text: His inner self is heat (penance). Therefore the breath of one who is heated (who practices penance) becomes hotter,
text_mt: Its inner self is heat (tapas). Therefore the breath of one who is hot is hotter.

sanskrit_iast: tapaso 'ntarātmāgniḥ sa niruktaḥ tasmāt sa dahati |
meaning: तपसो ऽन्तरात्माग्निः स निरुक्तः तस्मात् स दहति ।
text: The inner self of heat (penance) is fire. That is distinct. Therefore it burns,
text_mt: The inner self of heat is fire (Agni). It is expressed (nirukta). Therefore it burns.

sanskrit_iast: athādhidevatam iyam evaiṣā devatā yo 'yam pavate tasminn etasminn āpo 'ntaḥ tad annam so 'rūkṣa upāsitavyaḥ yad asminn āpo 'ntas tenārūkṣaḥ |
meaning: अथाधिदेवतम् इयम् एवैषा देवता यो ऽयम् पवते तस्मिन्न् एतस्मिन्न् आपो ऽन्तः तद् अन्नम् सो ऽरूक्ष उपासितव्यः यद् अस्मिन्न् आपो ऽन्तस् तेनारूक्षः ।
text: Now with regard to the divinities. He is this divinity who cleanses here. Within him are the waters. These are food. He is to be worshiped as soft. Because the waters are in him, therefore [he is] soft.
text_mt: Now pertaining to the deities: this very deity is he who purifies here [the wind]. Within this one are the waters; that is food. He is to be revered as not dry; in that the waters are within him, thereby he is not dry.

sanskrit_iast: tasyāntarātmā tapas tasmād eṣa ātapaty uṣṇataraḥ pavate |
meaning: तस्यान्तरात्मा तपस् तस्माद् एष आतपत्य् उष्णतरः पवते ।
text: His inner self is heat. Therefore it blows hotter when [the sun] shines.
text_mt: His inner self is heat. Therefore, when it shines intensely, it blows hotter.

sanskrit_iast: tapaso 'ntarātmā vidyut sa niruktaḥ tasmāt so 'pi dahati |
meaning: तपसो ऽन्तरात्मा विद्युत् स निरुक्तः तस्मात् सो ऽपि दहति ।
text: The inner self of heat is lightning. That is distinct. Therefore it also burns.
text_mt: The inner self of heat is lightning. It is expressed. Therefore it too burns.

sanskrit_iast: tāni vā etāni catvāri sāma prāṇo vāṅ manas svaraḥ sa eṣa praṇo vācā karoti manonetraḥ tasya svara eva prajāḥ prajāvān bhavati ya evaṃ veda | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तानि वा एतानि चत्वारि साम प्राणो वाङ् मनस् स्वरः स एष प्रणो वाचा करोति मनोनेत्रः तस्य स्वर एव प्रजाः प्रजावान् भवति य एवं वेद । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
text: Verily these four [are] the sāman: breath, speech, mind, [and] tone. That same breath, having mind as its guide, acts through speech. Of it tone is the offspring. Rich in offspring becomes he who knows thus.
text_mt:
These four, indeed, are the sāman: breath, speech, mind, sound (svara). This breath acts through speech, guided by the mind. His offspring is sound alone. Possessed of offspring becomes he who knows thus.
Fourth subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: sa yo vāyuḥ prāṇa eva saḥ yo 'gnir vāg eva sā yaś candramā mana eva tad ya ādityas svara eva saḥ tasmād etam ādityam āhus svara etīti |
meaning: स यो वायुः प्राण एव सः यो ऽग्निर् वाग् एव सा यश् चन्द्रमा मन एव तद् य आदित्यस् स्वर एव सः तस्माद् एतम् आदित्यम् आहुस् स्वर एतीति ।
text: Vayu is breath, Agni is speech, the moon is mind, the sun is tone. Therefore they say of this sun: " He goeth as tone."
text_mt: That which is wind (Vāyu) is breath alone; that which is fire (Agni) is speech alone; that which is the Moon (Candramas) is mind alone; that which is the sun (Āditya) is sound alone. Therefore they say of this sun: "Sound goes."

sanskrit_iast: sa yo ha vā amūr devatā upāste yā amūr adhidevataṃ dūrūpā vā etā duranusamprāpyā iva kas tad veda yady etā anu vā samprāpnuyān na vā |
meaning: स यो ह वा अमूर् देवता उपास्ते या अमूर् अधिदेवतं दूरूपा वा एता दुरनुसम्प्राप्या इव कस् तद् वेद यद्य् एता अनु वा सम्प्राप्नुयान् न वा ।
text: If any one worships yonder divinities, namely those [that are defined] with regard to the divinities—verily, they are of evil form, hard to be completely attained, as it were. Who knows whether he will completely attain unto them or not?
text_mt: Now, whoever reveres those deities that are yonder pertaining to the deities—they are of difficult form, as it were, difficult to reach completely. Who knows whether one may reach them completely or not?

sanskrit_iast: atha ya enā adhyātmam upāste sa hāntidevo bhavati nirjīryantīva vā ita etā tasya vā etāś śarīrasya saha prāṇena nirjīryanti ka u eva tad veda yady etā anu vā samprāpnuyān na vā |
meaning: अथ य एना अध्यात्मम् उपास्ते स हान्तिदेवो भवति निर्जीर्यन्तीव वा इत एता तस्य वा एताश् शरीरस्य सह प्राणेन निर्जीर्यन्ति क उ एव तद् वेद यद्य् एता अनु वा सम्प्राप्नुयान् न वा ।
text: Now if any one worships them [as defined] with regard to the self, he becomes one who is near the gods. They waste away, as it were, from here. Verily these [divinities] waste away along with the breath of his body. And who knows whether he will completely attain unto them or not?
text_mt: Now he who reveres these pertaining to the self, he is near the gods. From here these [faculties], as it were, waste away; along with the breath of his body, these waste away. And who knows whether one may reach them completely or not?

sanskrit_iast: atha ya enā ubhayīr ekadhā bhavantīr veda sa evānuṣṭhyā sāma veda sa ātmānaṃ veda sa brahma veda |
meaning: अथ य एना उभयीर् एकधा भवन्तीर् वेद स एवानुष्ठ्या साम वेद स आत्मानं वेद स ब्रह्म वेद ।
text: Now he who knows both these kinds [of divinities] as unified, he immediately knows the sāman, he knows the self, he knows the brahman,
text_mt: Now he who knows these both as becoming one, he truly knows the sāman in proper order; he knows the self; he knows brahman.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhuḥ prādeśamātrād vā ita etā ekam bhavanti ato hy ayam prāṇas svarya upary upari vartata iti |
meaning: तद् आहुः प्रादेशमात्राद् वा इत एता एकम् भवन्ति अतो ह्य् अयम् प्राणस् स्वर्य उपर्य् उपरि वर्तत इति ।
text: This they say: " From the size of a span from here these [divinities] become one. For from here this breath turneth sounding upward and upward."
text_mt: Concerning this they say: "At the distance of a span from here they become one; for from there this sounding breath moves higher and higher."

sanskrit_iast: atha haika āhuś caturaṅgulād vā ita etā ekam bhavantīti ato hy evāyam prāṇas svarya upary upari vartata iti |
meaning: अथ हैक आहुश् चतुरङ्गुलाद् वा इत एता एकम् भवन्तीति अतो ह्य् एवायम् प्राणस् स्वर्य उपर्य् उपरि वर्तत इति ।
text: And some say: " From [the size of] four fingers from here these [divinities] become one. For from here this breath turneth sounding upward and upward."
text_mt: Now some say: "At the distance of four fingers from here they become one; for from there this sounding breath moves higher and higher."

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa brahmaṇa āvartaḥ sa ya evam etam brahmaṇa āvartaṃ vedābhy enam prajāḥ paśava āvartante sarvam āyur eti |
meaning: स एष ब्रह्मण आवर्तः स य एवम् एतम् ब्रह्मण आवर्तं वेदाभ्य् एनम् प्रजाः पशव आवर्तन्ते सर्वम् आयुर् एति ।
text: That is the turn of the brahman. He who thus knows this turn of the brahman, unto him offspring [and] domestic animals turn; he goes to complete age.
text_mt: This is the vortex of brahman. Whoever thus knows this vortex of brahman, toward him offspring and cattle turn; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: sa yo haivaṃ vidvān prāṇena prāṇyāpānenāpānya manasaitā ubhayīr devatā ātmany etya mukha ādhatte tasya sarvam āptam bhavati sarvaṃ jitam na hāsya kaś cana kāmo 'nāpto bhavati ya evaṃ veda | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स यो हैवं विद्वान् प्राणेन प्राण्यापानेनापान्य मनसैता उभयीर् देवता आत्मन्य् एत्य मुख आधत्ते तस्य सर्वम् आप्तम् भवति सर्वं जितम् न हास्य कश् चन कामो ऽनाप्तो भवति य एवं वेद । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः ।
text: He who, knowing thus, breathing with breath, exhaling with exhalation, coming into the self, puts these divinities of both kinds with the mind in the mouth, by him everything is obtained, everything conquered. No wish soever of him is unattained who knows thus.
text_mt:
Knowing thus, breathing in with the in-breath, breathing out with the out-breath, grasping these both deities in the self by means of the mind, whoever places [them] in the mouth—for him everything is obtained, everything is conquered. No desire whatsoever of his remains unobtained, who knows thus.
Fifth subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tad etan mithunaṃ yad vāk ca prāṇaś ca mithunam ṛksāme ācaturaṃ vāva mithunam prajananam |
meaning: तद् एतन् मिथुनं यद् वाक् च प्राणश् च मिथुनम् ऋक्सामे आचतुरं वाव मिथुनम् प्रजननम् ।
text: Those are this couple, viz. speech and breath; a couple are re and sāman. Verily to the fourth [generation] a pair is generative.
text_mt: This is the pair: speech and breath; the pair is the ṛc and the sāman; a pair is procreative up to fourfold.

sanskrit_iast: tad yatrāda āha somaḥ pavata iti vopāvartadhvam iti vā tat sahaiva vācā manasā prāṇena svareṇa hiṅkurvanti tad hiṅkāreṇa mithunaṃ kriyate |
meaning: तद् यत्राद आह सोमः पवत इति वोपावर्तध्वम् इति वा तत् सहैव वाचा मनसा प्राणेन स्वरेण हिङ्कुर्वन्ति तद् हिङ्कारेण मिथुनं क्रियते ।
text: Now where one says here either "Soma cleanses itself," or "Turn ye hither," they thus utter the hinkdra along with speech, with mind, with breath, with tone. With the hinkdra a couple is thus brought about.
text_mt: So when yonder [the priest] says, "Soma purifies itself," or "Turn toward [us]," then together with speech, mind, breath, and sound they utter the hiṅkāra. Thus by the hiṅkāra a pair is formed.

sanskrit_iast: sahaiva vācā manasā prāṇena svareṇa nidhanam upayanti tan nidhanena mithunam kriyate |
meaning: सहैव वाचा मनसा प्राणेन स्वरेण निधनम् उपयन्ति तन् निधनेन मिथुनम् क्रियते ।
text: They also perform the nidJiana along with speech, with mind, with breath, with tone. With the nidhana a couple is thus brought about.
text_mt: Together with speech, mind, breath, and sound, they attain the finale. Thus a pair is formed through the finale.

sanskrit_iast: tat saptavidhaṃ sāmnaḥ saptakṛtva udgātātmānaṃ ca yajamānaṃ ca śarīrāt prajanayati |
meaning: तत् सप्तविधं साम्नः सप्तकृत्व उद्गातात्मानं च यजमानं च शरीरात् प्रजनयति ।
text: That is the sevenfold of the sāman. Seven times the udgdtar causes himself and the sacrificer to be born from the body.
text_mt: That belongs sevenfold to the sāman. Seven times the udgātṛ engenders both himself and the sacrificer from the body.

sanskrit_iast: yādṛśasyo ha vai reto bhavati tādṛśaṃ sambhavati yadi vai puruṣasya puruṣa eva yadi gor gaur eva yady aśvasyāśva eva yadi mṛgasya mṛga eva yasyaiva reto bhavati tad eva sambhavati |
meaning: यादृशस्यो ह वै रेतो भवति तादृशं सम्भवति यदि वै पुरुषस्य पुरुष एव यदि गोर् गौर् एव यद्य् अश्वस्याश्व एव यदि मृगस्य मृग एव यस्यैव रेतो भवति तद् एव सम्भवति ।
text: And verily of what kind [of being] the seed is, that kind [of being] arises: if it be of a man, a man; if of a cow, a cow; if of a horse, a horse; if of a deer, a deer. Of what [being] the seed is, just that being is born.
text_mt: Whatever [creature's] semen it is, of such a kind does [the offspring] come into being: if indeed of a human, a human; if of a cow, a cow; if of a horse, a horse; if of a wild beast, a wild beast. Whosever semen it is, that very one comes into being.

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā ha vai suvarṇaṃ hiraṇyam agnau prāsyamānaṃ kalyāṇataraṃ kalyāṇataram bhavaty evam eva kalyāṇatareṇa kalyāṇatareṇātmanā sambhavati ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: तद् यथा ह वै सुवर्णं हिरण्यम् अग्नौ प्रास्यमानं कल्याणतरं कल्याणतरम् भवत्य् एवम् एव कल्याणतरेण कल्याणतरेणात्मना सम्भवति य एवं वेद ।
text: Now as gold of good color being cast into the fire becomes more and more beautiful, even so he comes into being with a more and more beautiful self who knows thus.
text_mt: Now, just as golden gold thrown into the fire becomes ever fairer and fairer, even so he comes into being with an ever fairer and fairer self, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad ṛcābhyanūcyate | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke ṣaṣṭhaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्यनूच्यते । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके षष्ठः खण्डः ।
text: That same is referred to in a re.
text_mt: Regarding this, it is declared by a verse: / Sixth subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgam aktam asurasya māyayā hṛdā paśyanti manasā vipaścitaḥ samudre antaḥ kavayo vi cakṣate marīcīnām padam icchanti vedhasa iti |
meaning: पतङ्गम् अक्तम् असुरस्य मायया हृदा पश्यन्ति मनसा विपश्चितः समुद्रे अन्तः कवयो वि चक्षते मरीचीनाम् पदम् इच्छन्ति वेधस इति ।
text: " The winged one, adorned with the magic of an Asura, with the heart the inspired [bards] see, with the mind. Within the sea the sages look about; the faithful seek the track of the rays."
text_mt: "The bird anointed by the Asura's craft, the wise see with heart and mind; / Within the sea the inspired poets behold; the wise seek the track of the rays."

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgam aktam iti prāṇo vai pataṅgaḥ patann iva hy eṣv aṅgeṣv ati ratham udīkṣate pataṅga ity ācakṣate |
meaning: पतङ्गम् अक्तम् इति प्राणो वै पतङ्गः पतन्न् इव ह्य् एष्व् अङ्गेष्व् अति रथम् उदीक्षते पतङ्ग इत्य् आचक्षते ।
text: 'The winged one, adorned': breath is the winged one. For flying (patan), as it were, in these limbs (aflga), he looks up beyond the chariot (?). [Therefore] he is called winged one [patanga).
text_mt: "The bird anointed": breath is indeed the bird. For flying, as it were, through these limbs, it gazes beyond the chariot; therefore they call it the bird.

sanskrit_iast: asurasya māyayeti mano vā asuram tad dhy asuṣu ramate tasyaiṣa māyayāktaḥ |
meaning: असुरस्य माययेति मनो वा असुरम् तद् ध्य् असुषु रमते तस्यैष माययाक्तः ।
text: ' With the magic of an Asura': mind is asura[-like]. For it rests {Śram) in the vital airs {asu). He is adorned with its magic.
text_mt: "By the Asura's craft": the mind indeed is the Asura, for it delights in the vital powers (asu). By its craft this [breath] is anointed.

sanskrit_iast: hṛdā paśyanti manasā vipaścita iti hṛdaiva hy ete paśyanti yan manasā vipaścitaḥ |
meaning: हृदा पश्यन्ति मनसा विपश्चित इति हृदैव ह्य् एते पश्यन्ति यन् मनसा विपश्चितः ।
text: ' With the heart, with the mind the inspired [bards] see': for verily the inspired ones see with the heart as with the mind.
text_mt: "The wise see with heart and mind": for with the heart alone these see what the wise [perceive] with the mind.

sanskrit_iast: samudre antaḥ kavayo vi cakṣata iti puruṣo vai samudra evaṃvida u kavayaḥ ta imām puruṣe 'ntar vācaṃ vicakṣate |
meaning: समुद्रे अन्तः कवयो वि चक्षत इति पुरुषो वै समुद्र एवंविद उ कवयः त इमाम् पुरुषे ऽन्तर् वाचं विचक्षते ।
text: ' Within the sea the sages look about': verily man is the sea, and those who know thus are the sages. They look about for this speech within man.
text_mt: "Within the sea the inspired poets behold": the person indeed is the sea, and those who know thus are the inspired poets. They behold this speech within the person.

sanskrit_iast: marīcīnām padam icchanti vedhasa iti marīcya iva vā etā devatā yad agnir vāyur ādityaś candramāḥ |
meaning: मरीचीनाम् पदम् इच्छन्ति वेधस इति मरीच्य इव वा एता देवता यद् अग्निर् वायुर् आदित्यश् चन्द्रमाः ।
text: ' The faithful seek the track of the rays': rays, as it were, are these divinities, viz. Agni, Vayu, sun, [and] moon.
text_mt: "The wise seek the track of the rays": these deities—namely, Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, and the Moon—are indeed like rays.

sanskrit_iast: na ha vā etāsāṃ devatānām padam asti padeno ha vai punarmṛtyur anveti |
meaning: न ह वा एतासां देवतानाम् पदम् अस्ति पदेनो ह वै पुनर्मृत्युर् अन्वेति ।
text: Verily, of those divinities there is no track. [For] by means of a track second death goes after.
text_mt: Indeed there is no track of these deities; and by a track, repeated death pursues.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad ananvitaṃ sāma punarmṛtyunā ati punarmṛtyum tarati ya evaṃ veda | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke saptamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् एतद् अनन्वितं साम पुनर्मृत्युना अति पुनर्मृत्युम् तरति य एवं वेद । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके सप्तमः खण्डः ।
text: That same is the sāman vs^hich is not gone after by second death. He crosses over second death who knows thus.
text_mt: This sāman is unpursued by repeated death. He crosses beyond repeated death who knows thus. / Seventh subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgo vācam manasā bibharti tāṃ gandharvo 'vadad garbhe antaḥ tāṃ dyotamānāṃ svaryam manīṣām ṛtasya pade kavayo ni pāntī ti |
meaning: पतङ्गो वाचम् मनसा बिभर्ति तां गन्धर्वो ऽवदद् गर्भे अन्तः तां द्योतमानां स्वर्यम् मनीषाम् ऋतस्य पदे कवयो नि पान्ती ति ।
text: "The winged one beareth speech with the mind; that [speech] the Gandharva spoke within the womb; this brilliant sounding wisdom the poets guard in the place of [sacred] order."
text_mt: "The bird bears speech with the mind; the gandharva spoke it within the womb; / That shining, heavenly-sounding inspiration the inspired poets guard in the place of cosmic order."

sanskrit_iast: pataṅgo vācam manasā bibhartīti prāṇo vai pataṅgaḥ sa imāṃ vācam manasā bibharti |
meaning: पतङ्गो वाचम् मनसा बिभर्तीति प्राणो वै पतङ्गः स इमां वाचम् मनसा बिभर्ति ।
text: 'The winged one beareth speech with the mind': verily, breath is the winged one; he bears this speech with the mind.
text_mt: "The bird bears speech with the mind": breath is indeed the bird. It bears this speech with the mind.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ gandharvo 'vadad garbhe antar iti prāṇo vai gandharvaḥ puruṣa u garbhaḥ sa imām puruṣe 'ntar vācaṃ vadati |
meaning: तां गन्धर्वो ऽवदद् गर्भे अन्तर् इति प्राणो वै गन्धर्वः पुरुष उ गर्भः स इमाम् पुरुषे ऽन्तर् वाचं वदति ।
text: 'That [speech] the Gandharva spoke within the womb': verily breath is the Gandharva, and man is the womb. He speaks this speech within man.
text_mt: "The gandharva spoke it within the womb": breath is indeed the gandharva, and the person is the womb. It speaks this speech within the person.

sanskrit_iast: tāṃ dyotamānāṃ svaryam manīṣām iti svaryā hy eṣā manīṣā yad vāk |
meaning: तां द्योतमानां स्वर्यम् मनीषाम् इति स्वर्या ह्य् एषा मनीषा यद् वाक् ।
text: 'This brilliant, sounding wisdom': for sounding is this wisdom, viz. speech.
text_mt: "That shining, heavenly-sounding inspiration": for this inspiration, which is speech, is indeed heavenly-sounding.

sanskrit_iast: ṛtasya pade kavayo ni pāntīti mano vā ṛtam evaṃvida u kavayaḥ om ity etad evākṣaram ṛtam tena yad ṛcam mīmāṃsante yad yajur tat sāma tad enāṃ nipānti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke 'ṣṭamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: ऋतस्य पदे कवयो नि पान्तीति मनो वा ऋतम् एवंविद उ कवयः ओम् इत्य् एतद् एवाक्षरम् ऋतम् तेन यद् ऋचम् मीमांसन्ते यद् यजुर् तत् साम तद् एनां निपान्ति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके ऽष्टमः खण्डः ।
text: 'The poets guard in the place of [sacred] order': verily, mind is the [sacred] order, and those who know thus are the poets; om, that syllable is the [sacred] order. In that they reflect with it on the re, on the yajus, on the sāman, thereby they guard this [wisdom]. 35. 8 A. ve.
text_mt: "The inspired poets guard in the place of cosmic order": the mind is indeed the cosmic order, and those who know thus are the inspired poets. This very syllable 'om' is cosmic order. Whereby they reflect upon the ṛc, whereby the yajus, whereby the sāman, thereby they guard it. / Eighth subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: apaśyaṃ gopām anipadyamānam ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carantam sa sadhrīcīs sa viṣūcīr vasāna ā varīvartti bhuvaneṣv antar iti |
meaning: अपश्यं गोपाम् अनिपद्यमानम् आ च परा च पथिभिश् चरन्तम् स सध्रीचीस् स विषूचीर् वसान आ वरीवर्त्ति भुवनेष्व् अन्तर् इति ।
text: "I saw the keeper who doth not fall down moving to and fro by the paths. Clad in the converging and diverging ones, he oft turneth hither within created beings."
text_mt: "I saw the herdsman who never stumbles, wandering hither and thither along the paths; / Clothing himself in those that converge and those that diverge, he keeps rolling within the worlds."

sanskrit_iast: apaśyaṃ gopām anipadyamānam iti prāṇo vai gopāḥ sa hīdaṃ sarvam anipadyamāno gopāyati |
meaning: अपश्यं गोपाम् अनिपद्यमानम् इति प्राणो वै गोपाः स हीदं सर्वम् अनिपद्यमानो गोपायति ।
text: 'I saw the keeper who doth not fall down': verily breath is the keeper. For he keeps this all without falling down.
text_mt: "I saw the herdsman who never stumbles": breath is indeed the herdsman, for, never stumbling, it guards all this.

sanskrit_iast: ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carantam iti tad ye ca ha vā ime prāṇā amī ca raśmaya etair ha vā eṣa etad ā ca parā ca pathibhiś carati |
meaning: आ च परा च पथिभिश् चरन्तम् इति तद् ये च ह वा इमे प्राणा अमी च रश्मय एतैर् ह वा एष एतद् आ च परा च पथिभिश् चरति ।
text: ' Moving to and fro by the paths': now what these breaths here and yonder rays are, by them as paths he thus moves to and fro.
text_mt: "Wandering hither and thither along the paths": both these breaths and those rays—along these paths this [breath] wanders hither and thither.

sanskrit_iast: sa sadhrīcīs sa viṣūcīr vasāna iti sadhrīcīś ca hy eṣa etad viṣūcīś ca prajā vaste |
meaning: स सध्रीचीस् स विषूचीर् वसान इति सध्रीचीश् च ह्य् एष एतद् विषूचीश् च प्रजा वस्ते ।
text: ' Clad in the converging and diverging ones': for he is thus clad in converging and diverging offspring.
text_mt: "Clothing himself in those that converge and those that diverge": for it clothes itself in these creatures that converge and diverge.

sanskrit_iast: ā varīvartti bhuvaneṣv antar iti eṣa hy evaiṣu bhuvaneṣv antar āvarīvartti |
meaning: आ वरीवर्त्ति भुवनेष्व् अन्तर् इति एष ह्य् एवैषु भुवनेष्व् अन्तर् आवरीवर्त्ति ।
text: ' He oft turneth hither within created beings': for he often does turn hither within these created beings, e-s = I. 45. 4-6.
text_mt: "He keeps rolling within the worlds": for it indeed keeps rolling within these worlds.

sanskrit_iast: sa eṣa indra udgīthaḥ sa yadaiṣa indra udgītha āgacchati naivodgātuś copagātṝṇāṃ ca vijñāyate ita evordhvas svar udeti sa upari mūrdhno lelāyati |
meaning: स एष इन्द्र उद्गीथः स यदैष इन्द्र उद्गीथ आगच्छति नैवोद्गातुश् चोपगातॄणां च विज्ञायते इत एवोर्ध्वस् स्वर् उदेति स उपरि मूर्ध्नो लेलायति ।
text_mt: He is this Indra, the udgītha. When this Indra, the udgītha, arrives, neither [the voice] of the udgātṛ nor of the accompanying choristers is distinguished. Directly from here upward rises the tone; it vibrates above the crown of the head.

sanskrit_iast: sa vidyād āgamad indro neha kaś cana pāpmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśekṣyata iti tasmin ha na kaś cana papmā nyaṅgaḥ pariśiṣyate |
meaning: स विद्याद् आगमद् इन्द्रो नेह कश् चन पाप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशेक्ष्यत इति तस्मिन् ह न कश् चन पप्मा न्यङ्गः परिशिष्यते ।
text_mt: He should know: "Indra has arrived; no evil trace will be left here." In him no evil trace is left.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad abhrātṛvyaṃ sāma na ha vā indraḥ kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyate sa yathendro na kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyata evam eva kaṃ cana bhrātṛvyam paśyate ya etad evaṃ vedātho yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke navamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | ṣaṣṭho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तद् एतद् अभ्रातृव्यं साम न ह वा इन्द्रः कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यते स यथेन्द्रो न कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यत एवम् एव कं चन भ्रातृव्यम् पश्यते य एतद् एवं वेदाथो यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके नवमः खण्डः । षष्ठो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text_mt: This is the rival-free sāman. Indra indeed sees no rival. Just as Indra sees no rival, even so he sees [no] rival who knows this thus, and also he for whom one who knows thus sings the udgītha. / Ninth subsection in the sixth anuvāka. / The sixth anuvāka is finished.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatim brahmāsṛjata tam apaśyam amukham asṛjata |
meaning: प्रजापतिम् ब्रह्मासृजत तम् अपश्यम् अमुखम् असृजत ।
text: The brahman created, Prajapati. It created him not seeing, without mouth,
text_mt: Brahman created Prajāpati. It created him without sight and without a mouth.

sanskrit_iast: tam aprapaśyam amukhaṃ śayānam brahmāviśat puruṣyaṃ tat prāṇo vai brahma prāṇo vāvainaṃ tad āviśat |
meaning: तम् अप्रपश्यम् अमुखं शयानम् ब्रह्माविशत् पुरुष्यं तत् प्राणो वै ब्रह्म प्राणो वावैनं तद् आविशत् ।
text: Him lying not looking, without mouth, the brahman entered. That [became?] hum'an. Verily the brahman is breath. Breath, indeed, entered him thus.
text_mt: As he lay unable to see and without a mouth, brahman entered him. That was pertaining to the person. Breath is indeed brahman; breath indeed entered him then.

sanskrit_iast: sa udatiṣṭhat prajānāṃ janayitā taṃ rakṣāṃsy anvasacanta |
meaning: स उदतिष्ठत् प्रजानां जनयिता तं रक्षांस्य् अन्वसचन्त ।
text: He arose, a generator of progeny. Him the Raksases fastened on.
text_mt: He stood up as the begetter of creatures. Demons attached themselves to him.

sanskrit_iast: tam etad eva sāma gāyann atrāyata yad gāyann atrāyata tad gāyatrasya gāyatratvam |
meaning: तम् एतद् एव साम गायन्न् अत्रायत यद् गायन्न् अत्रायत तद् गायत्रस्य गायत्रत्वम् ।
text: Him one singing this same sāman rescued. Because he singing (gdyan) rescued (atrdyata), that is the reason why the gāyatra Y-sāman\ is called so.
text_mt: Singing this very sāman, he protected him. That he protected (atrāyata) while singing (gāyan), that is the gāyatra nature of the gāyatra chant.

sanskrit_iast: trāyata enaṃ sarvasmāt pāpmano mucyate ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: त्रायत एनं सर्वस्मात् पाप्मनो मुच्यते य एवं वेद ।
text: One rescues him, from all evil he is delivered, who knows thus.
text_mt: It protects him; he is freed from all evil, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: tam upāsmai gāyatā nara ity ṛcāśravaṇīyenopāgāyan |
meaning: तम् उपास्मै गायता नर इत्य् ऋचाश्रवणीयेनोपागायन् ।
text: They sang unto him with the re which belongs to the preliminary invocation: " Sing, ye men, unto this one." Inasmuch as [it runs]: "Sing (y'Śa), ye men, unto this one," hence it became the gāyatra (sāman). Therefore this is to be made the introductory verse.
text_mt: They sang up to him, in an inaudible manner, with the verse: "Sing up to him, O men!"

sanskrit_iast: yad upāsmai gāyatā nara iti tena gāyatram abhavat tasmād eṣaiva pratipat kāryā |
meaning: यद् उपास्मै गायता नर इति तेन गायत्रम् अभवत् तस्माद् एषैव प्रतिपत् कार्या ।
text_mt: Because of "Sing up (upa... gāyata) to him, O men!", it thereby became the gāyatra chant. Therefore, this very [verse] should be made the opening verse.

sanskrit_iast: pavamānāyendāvā abhi devam iyā-hum-bhā-kṣātā iti ṣoḍaśākṣarāṇy abhyagāyanta ṣoḍaśakalaṃ vai brahma kalāśa evainaṃ tad brahmāviśat |
meaning: पवमानायेन्दावा अभि देवम् इया-हुम्-भा-क्षाता इति षोडशाक्षराण्य् अभ्यगायन्त षोडशकलं वै ब्रह्म कलाश एवैनं तद् ब्रह्माविशत् ।
text: " Unto Indu, who is being purified, who desires to sacrifice to the god," thus they sang sixteen syllables unto [him]. Verily sixteenfold is the brahman. Part by part the brahman thus entered him,
text_mt: They chanted the sixteen syllables: "pavamānāyendāvā abhi devam iyā-hum-bhā-kṣātā". Brahman has sixteen parts. Part by part brahman then entered him.

sanskrit_iast: tad etac caturviṃśatyakṣaraṃ gāyatram aṣṭākṣaraḥ prastāvaḥ ṣoḍaśākṣaraṃ gītaṃ tac caturviṃśatis sampadyante caturviṃśatyardhamāsas saṃvatsaraḥ saṃvatsaras sāma |
meaning: तद् एतच् चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरं गायत्रम् अष्टाक्षरः प्रस्तावः षोडशाक्षरं गीतं तच् चतुर्विंशतिस् सम्पद्यन्ते चतुर्विंशत्यर्धमासस् संवत्सरः संवत्सरस् साम ।
text: That same is the gāyatra [sāman] with twenty-four syllables. The prastāva has eight syllables. The song (glta) has sixteen syllables. Thus twenty-four are obtained. Twenty-four half-months has the year; the year is the sāman.
text_mt: This gāyatra chant has twenty-four syllables. The prelude (prastāva) has eight syllables. The sung portion has sixteen syllables; thus they amount to twenty-four. The year has twenty-four half-months. The year is the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: tā ṛcaś śarīreṇa mṛtyur anvaitat tad yac charīravat tan mṛtyor āptam atha yad aśarīraṃ tad amṛtam tasyāśarīreṇa sāmnā śarīrāṇy adhūnot | saptame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: ता ऋचश् शरीरेण मृत्युर् अन्वैतत् तद् यच् छरीरवत् तन् मृत्योर् आप्तम् अथ यद् अशरीरं तद् अमृतम् तस्याशरीरेण साम्ना शरीराण्य् अधूनोत् । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: Because of the body death went after these ṛc's. What is possessed of a body, that is obtained by death; and what is bodiless, that is immortal. By means of the bodiless sāman he shook off this one's bodies.
text_mt: Death pursued that verse through the body. Whatever possesses a body is seized by Death; but what is bodiless is immortal. With the bodiless sāman, he shook off his bodies. / First subsection in the seventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: ovā3c ovā3c ovā3c hum bhā ovā iti ṣoḍaśākṣarāṇy abhyagāyata ṣoḍaśakalo vai puruṣaḥ kalāśa evāsya tac charīrāṇy adhūnot |

text_mt: He is this one whose evil is destroyed, whose bodies are shaken off. He sings... 'o' is the emission; 'ā' is the turn; 'vāc' is that brahman; that is the atmosphere, this Vāyu that blows; 'hum' is the Moon; 'bhā' is Āditya.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad amṛtaṃ gāyatram atha yāny anyāni gītāni kāmyāny eva tāni kāmyāny eva tāni | saptame 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | saptamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: तद् एतद् अमृतं गायत्रम् अथ यान्य् अन्यानि गीतानि काम्यान्य् एव तानि काम्यान्य् एव तानि । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । सप्तमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: That is the immortal gāyatra[-saman'\; and what other chants there are, they are optional only, they are optional only.
text_mt:
Now this gāyatra chant is immortal. But whatever other songs there are, they are only for desired ends, they are only for desired ends.
[This is] the fifth subsection in the seventh section.
The seventh section is finished.

sanskrit_iast: śvetāśvo darśato harinīlo 'si haritaspṛśas samānabuddho mā hiṃsīḥ na māṃ tvaṃ vettha pradrava |
meaning: श्वेताश्वो दर्शतो हरिनीलो ऽसि हरितस्पृशस् समानबुद्धो मा हिंसीः न मां त्वं वेत्थ प्रद्रव ।
text: Possessing white horses, conspicuous, yellow-blue art thou, do not harm. Thou knowest me not; run away.
text_mt:
White horse, worthy of sight, dark-green-blue art thou, touching greenness; sharing one mind, do not injure [me]!
Thou dost not know me; run away!

sanskrit_iast: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidam aśmamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
meaning: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदम् अश्ममयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
text: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a stone armor.
text_mt:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of stone!

sanskrit_iast: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidam ayasmayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
meaning: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदम् अयस्मयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
text: When moving- down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a brass armor.
text_mt:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of metal!

sanskrit_iast: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidaṃ lohamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
meaning: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदं लोहमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
text: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a copper armor.
text_mt:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of copper!

sanskrit_iast: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣam akovidaṃ rajatamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
meaning: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषम् अकोविदं रजतमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
text: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a silver armor.
text_mt:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, inexperienced man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of silver!

sanskrit_iast: yad abhyavacaraṇo 'bhyavaiṣi svapantam puruṣaṃ suvarṇamayena varmaṇā varuṇo 'ntar dadhātu mā |
meaning: यद् अभ्यवचरणो ऽभ्यवैषि स्वपन्तम् पुरुषं सुवर्णमयेन वर्मणा वरुणो ऽन्तर् दधातु मा ।
text: When moving down against [him] thou descendest against the sleeping man unknowing, let Varuna cover me with a golden armor.
text_mt:
When, descending, thou approachest the sleeping, [inexperienced] man,
let Varuṇa shield me with an armor made of gold!

sanskrit_iast: āyur mātā matiḥ pitā namas ta āviśoṣaṇa graho nāmāsi viśvāyus tasmai te viśvāhā namo namas tāmrāya namo varuṇāya namo jighāṃsate |
meaning: आयुर् माता मतिः पिता नमस् त आविशोषण ग्रहो नामासि विश्वायुस् तस्मै ते विश्वाहा नमो नमस् ताम्राय नमो वरुणाय नमो जिघांसते ।
text: Life is the mother, thought the father. Homage to thee, O drying one. Thou art seizer by name, possessing all life. TJnto thee then homage for ever. Homage to the copper-red one, homage to Varuna, homage to him who desires to slay.
text_mt:
Life is mother, mind is father; homage to thee, O consumer!
Graha is thy name, of full life; to that thee, ever homage! Homage to the copper-colored! Homage to Varuṇa! Homage to him who desires to slay!

sanskrit_iast: yakṣma rājan mā māṃ hiṃsīḥ rājan yakṣma mā hiṃsīḥ tayos saṃvidānayos sarvam āyur ayāny aham | prathamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: यक्ष्म राजन् मा मां हिंसीः राजन् यक्ष्म मा हिंसीः तयोस् संविदानयोस् सर्वम् आयुर् अयान्य् अहम् । प्रथमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Consumption king, do not hurt me. King consumption, do not hurt. These two being harmonious, may I go to complete life.
text_mt:
O King Consumption, do not injure me!
O King, do not injure [me], Consumption!
With those two agreeing together, may I attain a full life!
The first section is finished.

sanskrit_iast: puruṣo vai yajñaḥ |
meaning: पुरुषो वै यज्ञः ।
text: Man is the sacrifice.
text_mt: Man, indeed, is the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast: tasya yāni caturviṃśatir varṣāṇi tat prātassavanam caturviṃśatyakṣarā gāyatrī gāyatram prātassavanam |
meaning: तस्य यानि चतुर्विंशतिर् वर्षाणि तत् प्रातस्सवनम् चतुर्विंशत्यक्षरा गायत्री गायत्रम् प्रातस्सवनम् ।
text: His [first] twenty-four years are the morning-libation. The gdyatri has twenty-four syllables. The morning-libation is connected with the gdyatri.

sanskrit_iast: tad vasūnām prāṇā vai vasavaḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vasv ādadate |
meaning: तद् वसूनाम् प्राणा वै वसवः प्राणा हीदं सर्वं वस्व् आददते ।
text: It belongs to the Vasus. The breaths are the Vasus; for the breaths take to themselves all this that is good (vasu).
text_mt:
That belongs to the Vasus.
The vital breaths, indeed, are the Vasus,
for the vital breaths appropriate everything here as wealth.

sanskrit_iast: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā vasava idam me prātassavanam mādhyandinena savanenānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
meaning: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा वसव इदम् मे प्रातस्सवनम् माध्यन्दिनेन सवनेनानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
text: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Vasus, continue this morning-libation of mine by the noon-libation." Verily he becomes well.
text_mt:
If disease should assail him at this time, he should say: 'O vital breaths, O Vasus, continue this morning pressing of mine to the midday pressing.'
He indeed becomes free from sickness.

sanskrit_iast: atha yāni catuścatvāriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi tan mādhyandinaṃ savanam catuścatvāriṃśadakṣarā triṣṭup traiṣṭubham mādhyandinaṃ savanam |
meaning: अथ यानि चतुश्चत्वारिंशतं वर्षाणि तन् माध्यन्दिनं सवनम् चतुश्चत्वारिंशदक्षरा त्रिष्टुप् त्रैष्टुभम् माध्यन्दिनं सवनम् ।
text: His [next] forty-four years are the noon-libation. The tristubh has forty-four syllables. The noon-libation is connected with the tristubh.

sanskrit_iast: tad rudrāṇām prāṇā vai rudrāḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvaṃ rodayanti |
meaning: तद् रुद्राणाम् प्राणा वै रुद्राः प्राणा हीदं सर्वं रोदयन्ति ।
text: It belongs to the Rudras. The breaths are the Rudras; for the breaths cause the whole [universe] to wail {Śrud).
text_mt:
That belongs to the Rudras.
The vital breaths, indeed, are the Rudras,
for the vital breaths make everything here weep.

sanskrit_iast: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā rudrā idam me mādhyandinaṃ savanaṃ tṛtīyasavanenānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
meaning: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा रुद्रा इदम् मे माध्यन्दिनं सवनं तृतीयसवनेनानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
text: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Rudras, continue this noon-libation of mine by the evening-libation." Verily he becomes well.
text_mt:
If disease should assail him at this time, he should say: 'O vital breaths, O Rudras, continue this midday pressing of mine to the third pressing.'
He indeed becomes free from sickness.

sanskrit_iast: atha yāny aṣṭācatvāriṃśataṃ varṣāṇi tat tṛtīyasavanam aṣṭācatvāriṃśadakṣarā jagatī jāgataṃ tṛtīyasavanam |
meaning: अथ यान्य् अष्टाचत्वारिंशतं वर्षाणि तत् तृतीयसवनम् अष्टाचत्वारिंशदक्षरा जगती जागतं तृतीयसवनम् ।
text: Moreover his [next] forty-eight years are the evening-libation. The jagati has forty-eight syllables. The evening-libation is connected with the jagati.
text_mt: Now, the forty-eight years that follow are the third pressing. The jagatī [metre] has forty-eight syllables; the third pressing belongs to the jagatī.

sanskrit_iast: tad ādityānām prāṇā vā ādityāḥ prāṇā hīdaṃ sarvam ādadate |
meaning: तद् आदित्यानाम् प्राणा वा आदित्याः प्राणा हीदं सर्वम् आददते ।
text: It belongs to the Adityas. The breaths are the Adityas; for the breaths take to themselves (,Śdd + d) this all.
text_mt: That belongs to the Ādityas. The breaths indeed are the Ādityas, for the breaths take up (ādadate) all this.

sanskrit_iast: sa yady enam etasmin kāla upatapad upadravet sa brūyāt prāṇā ādityā idam me tṛtīyasavanam āyuṣānusaṃtanuteti agado haiva bhavati |
meaning: स यद्य् एनम् एतस्मिन् काल उपतपद् उपद्रवेत् स ब्रूयात् प्राणा आदित्या इदम् मे तृतीयसवनम् आयुषानुसंतनुतेति अगदो हैव भवति ।
text: If in that time an illness should attack him, he should say: " Ye breaths, ye Adityas, continue this my evening-libation by my life-time." Verily he becomes well.
text_mt: If illness should attack him during this period, let him say: 'O breaths, Ādityas, unite this third pressing of mine with life!' He indeed becomes free from disease.

sanskrit_iast: etad dha tad vidvān brāhmaṇa uvāca mahidāsa aitareya upatapati kim idam upatapasi yo 'ham anenopatapatā na preṣyāmīti sa ha ṣoḍaśaśataṃ varṣāṇi jijīva pra ha ṣoḍaśaśataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati nainam prāṇas sāmy āyuṣo jahāti ya evaṃ veda | dvitīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: एतद् ध तद् विद्वान् ब्राह्मण उवाच महिदास ऐतरेय उपतपति किम् इदम् उपतपसि यो ऽहम् अनेनोपतपता न प्रेष्यामीति स ह षोडशशतं वर्षाणि जिजीव प्र ह षोडशशतं वर्षाणि जीवति नैनम् प्राणस् साम्य् आयुषो जहाति य एवं वेद । द्वितीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Now the Brahman Mahidasa Aitareya, knowing this, said in [his] illness: " Why dost thou now attack me, who am not to die of this illness?" He lived a hundred and sixteen years. He lives on to a hundred and sixteen years, [his] breath does not leave him in the midst of his lifetime, who knows thus.
text_mt:
Knowing this, the brāhmaṇa Mahidāsa Aitareya said when he fell ill: 'Why do you plague me with this illness, when I shall not die of it?' He lived for a hundred and sixteen years. Indeed, he who knows this lives for a hundred and sixteen years; the breath does not leave him midway through his life.
The second anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: tryāyuṣaṃ kaśyapasya jamadagnes tryāyuṣam trīṇy amṛtasya puṣpāṇi trīṇy āyūṃṣi me 'kṛṇoḥ |
meaning: त्र्यायुषं कश्यपस्य जमदग्नेस् त्र्यायुषम् त्रीण्य् अमृतस्य पुष्पाणि त्रीण्य् आयूंषि मे ऽकृणोः ।
text: The threefold life-time of Ka5yapa, of Jamadagni the threefold life-time, the three flowers of immortality, three life-times thou madest for me.
text_mt: 'A triple lifespan of Kaśyapa, a triple lifespan of Jamadagni, / three flowers of immortality: you have made three lifespans for me.

sanskrit_iast: sa no mayobhūḥ pitav āviśasva śāntiko yas tanuve syonaḥ |
meaning: स नो मयोभूः पितव् आविशस्व शान्तिको यस् तनुवे स्योनः ।
text: Enter into us, O thou beneficent food, which, tranquilizing, art pleasing to the body.
text_mt: O food, enter us as our joy, bringing peace, pleasant to the body.

sanskrit_iast: ye 'gnayaḥ purīṣyāḥ praviṣṭāḥ pṛṭhivīm anu teṣāṃ tvam asy uttamaḥ pra ṇo jīvātave suva | tṛtīyo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: ये ऽग्नयः पुरीष्याः प्रविष्टाः पृठिवीम् अनु तेषां त्वम् अस्य् उत्तमः प्र णो जीवातवे सुव । तृतीयो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: What dirty fires are entered into the earth along, of them thou art the highest; impel us unto life.
text_mt:
Those fires that are rich in soil, entered along the earth, / among them you are the highest: impel us toward life.'
The third anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: araṇyasya vatso 'si viśvanāmā viśvābhirakṣaṇo 'pām pakvo 'si varuṇasya dūto 'ntardhināma |
meaning: अरण्यस्य वत्सो ऽसि विश्वनामा विश्वाभिरक्षणो ऽपाम् पक्वो ऽसि वरुणस्य दूतो ऽन्तर्धिनाम ।
text: Thou art the calf of the forest, possessing all names, all-defending; ripe of the waters art thou, Varuna's messenger, concealment by name.
text_mt: You are the calf of the wilderness, all-named, all-protecting, the ripened product of the waters, the messenger of Varuṇa, your name is concealment.

sanskrit_iast: yathā tvam amṛto martyebhyo 'ntarhito 'sy evaṃ tvam asmān aghāyubhyo 'ntar dhehi antardhir asi stenebhyaḥ | caturtho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: यथा त्वम् अमृतो मर्त्येभ्यो ऽन्तर्हितो ऽस्य् एवं त्वम् अस्मान् अघायुभ्यो ऽन्तर् धेहि अन्तर्धिर् असि स्तेनेभ्यः । चतुर्थो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: As thou, immortal, art concealed from mortals, so do thou conceal us from the wicked. Thou art concealment from robbers.
text_mt:
Just as you, being immortal, are concealed from mortals, so conceal us from the malicious. You are a concealment against thieves.
The fourth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: vyuṣi savitā bhavasy udeṣyan viṣṇur udyan puruṣa udito bṛhaspatir abhiprayan maghavendro vaikuṇṭho mādhyandine bhago 'parāhna ugro devo lohitāyann astamite yamo bhavasi |
meaning: व्युषि सविता भवस्य् उदेष्यन् विष्णुर् उद्यन् पुरुष उदितो बृहस्पतिर् अभिप्रयन् मघवेन्द्रो वैकुण्ठो माध्यन्दिने भगो ऽपराह्न उग्रो देवो लोहितायन्न् अस्तमिते यमो भवसि ।
text: When it dawns, thou becomest Savitar; when about to rise, Visnu; rising, Purusa; risen, Brhaspati; ascending, the bounteous one; at noon, Indra Vfiikuntha; in the afternoon, Bhaga; growing red, the formidable god; having set, thou becomest Yama.
text_mt: At dawn you become Savitṛ; about to rise, Viṣṇu; rising, Puruṣa; risen, Bṛhaspati; marching forth, Indra Maghavat Vaikuṇṭha; at midday, Bhaga; in the afternoon, Ugra Deva; turning red, [Rudra]; set, you become Yama.

sanskrit_iast: aśnasu somo rājā niśāyām pitṛrājas svapne manuṣyān praviśasi payasā paśūn |
meaning: अश्नसु सोमो राजा निशायाम् पितृराजस् स्वप्ने मनुष्यान् प्रविशसि पयसा पशून् ।
text: In the stones king Soma, in the night the king of the Fathers. In sleep thou enterest into men; with the milk, into cattle.
text_mt: Among food-eaters [you are] King Soma; in the night, the king of the ancestors; in sleep you enter human beings; with milk, the cattle.

sanskrit_iast: virātre bhavo bhavasy apararātre 'ṅgirā agnihotravelāyām bhṛguḥ |
meaning: विरात्रे भवो भवस्य् अपररात्रे ऽङ्गिरा अग्निहोत्रवेलायाम् भृगुः ।
text: In the middle of night thou art Bhava; in the after-part of the night, Angiras; at the time of the Agnihotra, Bhrgu.
text_mt: In the deep of the night you become Bhava; in the latter part of the night, Aṅgiras; at the time of the agnihotra, Bhṛgu.

sanskrit_iast: tasya tad etad eva maṇḍalam ūdhaḥ tasyaitau stanau yad vāk ca prāṇaś ca tābhyām me dhukṣvādhyāyam brahmacaryam prajām paśūn svargaṃ lokaṃ sajātavanasyām |
meaning: तस्य तद् एतद् एव मण्डलम् ऊधः तस्यैतौ स्तनौ यद् वाक् च प्राणश् च ताभ्याम् मे धुक्ष्वाध्यायम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् प्रजाम् पशून् स्वर्गं लोकं सजातवनस्याम् ।
text: This disk is its udder, speech and breath are these two teats. From them milk for me the lesson, Vedic studentship, oifspring, domestic animals, the heavenly world, the prayer for supremacy over [my] fellows,
text_mt: This very orb of his is the udder. Its two teats are speech and breath. From them milk out for me Vedic study, celibacy, offspring, cattle, the heavenly world, and dominance over my kinsmen.

sanskrit_iast: etā āśiṣa āśāse bhūr bhuvas svaḥ udite śukram ādiśa tad atman dadhe | pañcamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: एता आशिष आशासे भूर् भुवस् स्वः उदिते शुक्रम् आदिश तद् अत्मन् दधे । पञ्चमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: These wishes I wish. Hhus, bhuvas, svar. When [the sun] hath risen, show brightness. I place that in [my]self.
text_mt:
These blessings I pray for: bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ! When [the sun] has risen, point to its brightness: 'That I place in myself.'
The fifth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: bhageratho haikṣvāko rājā kāmapreṇa yajñena yakṣyamāṇa āsa |
meaning: भगेरथो हैक्ष्वाको राजा कामप्रेण यज्ञेन यक्ष्यमाण आस ।
text: King Bhageratha Aiksvaka was about to sacrifice with a wish-fulfilling sacrifice.
text_mt: Bhageratha, an Aikṣvāka king, was about to sacrifice with a sacrifice that grants all desires.

sanskrit_iast: tad u ha kurupañcālānām brāhmaṇā ūcur bhageratho ha vā ayam aikṣvāko rājā kāmapreṇa yajñena yakṣyamāṇaḥ etena kathāṃ vadiṣyāma iti |
meaning: तद् उ ह कुरुपञ्चालानाम् ब्राह्मणा ऊचुर् भगेरथो ह वा अयम् ऐक्ष्वाको राजा कामप्रेण यज्ञेन यक्ष्यमाणः एतेन कथां वदिष्याम इति ।
text: Then the Brahmans of the Kurupaficalas said: "Verily this king Bhageratha Aiksvaka is about to sacrifice with a wish-fulfilling sacrifice. With him we will have a talk."
text_mt: Then the brāhmaṇas of the Kuru-Pañcālas said: 'This King Bhageratha Aikṣvāka is about to sacrifice with a sacrifice that grants all desires. Let us engage in a discussion with him.'

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hābhyeyuḥ tebhyo hābhyāgatebhyo 'pacitīś cakāra |
meaning: तं हाभ्येयुः तेभ्यो हाभ्यागतेभ्यो ऽपचितीश् चकार ।
text: They went to him. To them having come to [him] he paid honors.
text_mt: They approached him. He showed honor to them when they had arrived.

sanskrit_iast: atha haiṣāṃ sa bhāga āvavrājoptvā keśaśmaśrūṇi nakhān nikṛtyājyenābhyajya daṇḍopānaham bibhrat |
meaning: अथ हैषां स भाग आवव्राजोप्त्वा केशश्मश्रूणि नखान् निकृत्याज्येनाभ्यज्य दण्डोपानहम् बिभ्रत् ।
text: Now he came to their place having cut the hair of his head and his beard, having cut his nails, having anointed himself with sacrificial batter, bearing a staff and sandals.
text_mt: Then that [king] went to their portion, having shaved his hair and beard, clipped his nails, anointed himself with clarified butter, and holding a staff and sandals.

sanskrit_iast: tān hovāca brāhmaṇā bhagavantaḥ katamo vas tad veda yathāśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchata iti |
meaning: तान् होवाच ब्राह्मणा भगवन्तः कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथाश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छत इति ।
text: To them he (Bhageratha) said: " Reverend Brahmans, who of you knoweth this: how address and response go to the gods?"
text_mt: He said to them: 'Reverend brāhmaṇas, which of you knows how the call and the response reach the gods?'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yadviduṣas sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti |
meaning: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यद्विदुषस् सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति ।
text: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth what he knoweth (= must know) of whom, a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good acthvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born?"
text_mt: Then he said: 'Which of you knows by knowing what one becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature?'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yac chandāṃsi prayujyante yat tāni sarvāṇi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti |
meaning: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यच् छन्दांसि प्रयुज्यन्ते यत् तानि सर्वाणि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति ।
text: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the metres are applied, to what all of them when used in praise together are equivalent?"
text_mt: Then he said: 'Which of you knows that when metres are employed, into what all of them merge when chanted together?'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yathā gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti |
meaning: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथा गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति ।
text: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the last two syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice?"
text_mt: Then he said: 'Which of you knows how the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again?'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca katamo vas tad veda yathā dakṣiṇāḥ pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: अथ होवाच कतमो वस् तद् वेद यथा दक्षिणाः प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: Then he said: " Who of you knoweth this: how the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure?"
text_mt:
Then he said: 'Which of you knows how priestly gifts, when accepted, do not injure?'
First subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: etān hainān pañca praśnān papraccha |
meaning: एतान् हैनान् पञ्च प्रश्नान् पप्रच्छ ।
text: These five questions he asked of them.
text_mt: These were the five questions he asked them.

sanskrit_iast: teṣāṃ ha kurupañcālānām bako dālbhyo 'nūcāna āsa |
meaning: तेषां ह कुरुपञ्चालानाम् बको दाल्भ्यो ऽनूचान आस ।
text: Of these Kurupaficalas Baka Dalbhya was learned.
text_mt: Among those Kuru-Pañcālas, Baka Dālbhya was learned in the Veda.

sanskrit_iast: sa hovāca yathāśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchata iti prācyāṃ vai rājan diśy āśrāvitapratyāśrāvite devān gacchataḥ tasmāt prāṅ tiṣṭhann āśrāvayati prāṅ tiṣṭhan pratyāśrāvayatīti |
meaning: स होवाच यथाश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छत इति प्राच्यां वै राजन् दिश्य् आश्रावितप्रत्याश्राविते देवान् गच्छतः तस्मात् प्राङ् तिष्ठन्न् आश्रावयति प्राङ् तिष्ठन् प्रत्याश्रावयतीति ।
text: He said: "' How address and response go to the gods?'—verily in the eastern quarter, O king, do address and response go to the gods. Therefore standing towards the east one maketh address, [and] standing towards the east one maketh response."
text_mt: He said: '[Regarding your question,] how the call and the response reach the gods: in the eastern quarter, O king, the call and the response reach the gods. Therefore, standing facing east, one makes the call; standing facing east, one makes the response.'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca yadviduṣas sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti yo vai manuṣyasya sambhūtiṃ vedeti hovāca tasya sūdgātā suhotā svadhvaryus sumānuṣavid ājāyata iti prāṇā u ha vāva rājan manuṣyasya sambhūtir eveti |
meaning: अथ होवाच यद्विदुषस् सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति यो वै मनुष्यस्य सम्भूतिं वेदेति होवाच तस्य सूद्गाता सुहोता स्वध्वर्युस् सुमानुषविद् आजायत इति प्राणा उ ह वाव राजन् मनुष्यस्य सम्भूतिर् एवेति ।
text: Then he said: " 'What he knoweth (=must know) of whom a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good adhvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born?'—verily he who knoweth the origination of man," he said, " of him a good udgdtar, a good hotar, a good adhvaryu, one who knoweth men well, is born. And the breaths, indeed, O king, are the origination of man."
text_mt: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] by knowing what one becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature: he who knows the origination of man—he said—becomes a good udgātṛ, a good hotṛ, a good adhvaryu, and a knower of human nature. The breaths indeed, O king, are the origination of man.'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca yac chandāṃsi prayujyante yat tāni sarvāṇi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti gāyatrīm u ha vāva rājan sarvāṇi chandāṃsi saṃstutāny abhisampadyanta iti |
meaning: अथ होवाच यच् छन्दांसि प्रयुज्यन्ते यत् तानि सर्वाणि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति गायत्रीम् उ ह वाव राजन् सर्वाणि छन्दांसि संस्तुतान्य् अभिसम्पद्यन्त इति ।
text: Then he said: "' How the metres are applied, to what all of them when used in praise together are equivalent?'—verily to the gāyatrī, O king, all the metres when used in praise together are equivalent."
text_mt: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] when metres are employed, into what all of them merge when chanted together: into the gāyatrī indeed, O king, all metres merge when chanted together.'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca yathā gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti vaṣaṭkāreṇo ha vāva rājan gāyatryā uttame akṣare punar yajñam apigacchata iti |
meaning: अथ होवाच यथा गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति वषट्कारेणो ह वाव राजन् गायत्र्या उत्तमे अक्षरे पुनर् यज्ञम् अपिगच्छत इति ।
text: Then he said: "' How the last two syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice?'—verily by means of the vasatkdra, O king, the two last syllables of the gāyatrī go again unto the sacrifice."
text_mt: Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] how the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again: by means of the vaṣaṭ-call indeed, O king, the two final syllables of the gāyatrī reach the sacrifice again.'

sanskrit_iast: atha hovāca yathā dakṣiṇāḥ pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: अथ होवाच यथा दक्षिणाः प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: Then he said: "' How the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure?'—
text_mt:
Then he said: '[Regarding your question,] how priestly gifts, when accepted, do not injure:'
Second subsection in the sixth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: yo vai gāyatryai mukhaṃ vedeti hovāca taṃ dakṣiṇā pratigṛhītā na hiṃsantīti |
meaning: यो वै गायत्र्यै मुखं वेदेति होवाच तं दक्षिणा प्रतिगृहीता न हिंसन्तीति ।
text: — Verily whoso knoweth the mouth of the gāyatrī," he said, "him the sacrificial fees, being received, do not injure.
text_mt: 'He who knows the mouth of the gāyatrī,' he said, 'him priestly gifts do not injure when accepted.'

sanskrit_iast: agnir ha vāva rājan gāyatrīmukham tasmād yad agnāv abhyādadhāti bhūyān eva sa tena bhavati vardhate evam evaivaṃ vidvān brāhmaṇaḥ pratigṛhṇan bhūyān eva bhavati vardhata u eveti |
meaning: अग्निर् ह वाव राजन् गायत्रीमुखम् तस्माद् यद् अग्नाव् अभ्यादधाति भूयान् एव स तेन भवति वर्धते एवम् एवैवं विद्वान् ब्राह्मणः प्रतिगृह्णन् भूयान् एव भवति वर्धत उ एवेति ।
text: Verily Agni, O king, is the mouth of the gāyatrī. Therefore in that one puts [things] in the fire, it thereby becometh greater, it increaseth; even so a Brahman knowing thus, receiving [sacrificial fees], becometh greater [and] increaseth."
text_mt: 'Agni indeed, O king, is the mouth of the gāyatrī. Therefore, whatever one puts into Agni, he becomes greater by that, he increases. In the very same way, the brāhmaṇa who knows this, upon accepting [gifts], becomes greater and increases.'

sanskrit_iast: sa hovācānūcāno vai kilāyam brāhmaṇa āsa tvām aham anena yajñenaimīti |
meaning: स होवाचानूचानो वै किलायम् ब्राह्मण आस त्वाम् अहम् अनेन यज्ञेनैमीति ।
text: He (Bhageratha) said: " Verily this one was a learned Brahman. I come to thee with this sacrifice."
text_mt: He [the king] said: 'This brāhmaṇa is indeed truly learned in the Veda! I approach you for this sacrifice.'

sanskrit_iast: tasya vai te tathodgāsyāmīti hovāca yathaikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam eṣyasīti |
meaning: तस्य वै ते तथोद्गास्यामीति होवाच यथैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एष्यसीति ।
text: " Verily, I will sing for thee its udgītha," he (B.) said, " in such wise that thou shalt go to the heavenly world having become sole king."
text_mt: 'Indeed, I shall chant the udgītha for you in such a way,' he said, 'that having become a sole ruler, you will go to the heavenly world.'

sanskrit_iast: tasmā etena gāyatreṇodgīthenojjagau sa haikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam iyāya tena haitenaikarāḍ eva bhūtvā svargaṃ lokam eti |
meaning: तस्मा एतेन गायत्रेणोद्गीथेनोज्जगौ स हैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् इयाय तेन हैतेनैकराड् एव भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एति ।
text: For him he sang the udgītha by means of the gāyatra-udgītha. He (Bhageratha) having become sole king went to the heavenly world. By means of this same \udgītha\ he goes to the heavenly world, having become sole king, [who knows thus].
text_mt: He chanted the udgītha for him with this gāyatra chant. Having become a sole ruler, he went to the heavenly world. Through this chant, having become a sole ruler, he who knows this goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: oṃ vā iti dve akṣare oṃ vā iti caturthe oṃ vā iti ṣaṣṭhe hum bhā oṃ vāg ity aṣṭame |
meaning: ओं वा इति द्वे अक्षरे ओं वा इति चतुर्थे ओं वा इति षष्ठे हुम् भा ओं वाग् इत्य् अष्टमे ।
text: Om vd are two syllables, om. vd the third and fourth, om vd the fifth and sixth, hum bhd, om, vdc the seventh and eighth.
text_mt: 'om vāc' are two syllables; 'om vāc' at the fourth; 'om vāc' at the sixth; 'hum bhā om vāk' at the eighth.

sanskrit_iast: tena haitena pratīdarśo 'sya bhayadasyāsamātyasyojjagau |
