text_mt: With this [udgītha], Pratīdarśa chanted for Bhayada Āsamātyasa.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hovāca kiṃ ta āgāsyāmīti sa hovāca harī me devāśvāv āgāyeti tatheti tau hāsmā ājagau tau hainam ājagmatuḥ |
meaning: तं होवाच किं त आगास्यामीति स होवाच हरी मे देवाश्वाव् आगायेति तथेति तौ हास्मा आजगौ तौ हैनम् आजग्मतुः ।
text: He said to him: " What shall I sing into thy possession?" He said: "Sing for me the two bay steeds of the gods." "Yes," he said. He sang the two into his possession. They both came unto him.
text_mt: He said to him: 'What shall I chant for you?' He said: 'Chant into being for me two bay divine horses.' 'So be it,' [he replied]. He chanted them into being for him. The two came to him.

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa udgīthaḥ kāmānāṃ sampad oṃ vā3c oṃ vā3c oṃ vā3c hum bhā oṃ vāg iti sāṅgo haiva satanur amṛtas sambhavati ya etad evaṃ vedātho yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati | ṣaṣṭhe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | ṣaṣṭho 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: स वा एष उद्गीथः कामानां सम्पद् ओं वा3च् ओं वा3च् ओं वा3च् हुम् भा ओं वाग् इति साङ्गो हैव सतनुर् अमृतस् सम्भवति य एतद् एवं वेदाथो यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति । षष्ठे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः । षष्ठो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: This same udgītha is the success of wishes, viz. om, vdc, om vdc, om vdc, hum bhd, om vdc. Verily he comes to life with limbs, with a body, immortal, who knows this thus, and he for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha.
text_mt:
This udgītha is the attainment of all desires: 'om vāc, om vāc, om vāc, hum bhā om vāk.' Complete with limbs, with a body, he is born immortal who knows this thus, and also he for whom one who knows this chants the udgītha.
Third subsection in the sixth anuvāka.
The sixth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: puruṣo vai yajñaḥ puruṣo hodgīthaḥ athaita eva mṛtyavo yad agnir vāyur ādityaś candramāḥ |
meaning: पुरुषो वै यज्ञः पुरुषो होद्गीथः अथैत एव मृत्यवो यद् अग्निर् वायुर् आदित्यश् चन्द्रमाः ।
text: Verily the sacrifice is man, the udgītha indeed is man. Now these are the deaths, viz. Agni, Vayu, the sun, the moon.
text_mt: The sacrifice is indeed the Puruṣa; the udgītha is indeed the Puruṣa. Now these are deaths: Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, and the Moon.

sanskrit_iast: te ha puruṣaṃ jāyamānam eva mṛtyupāśair abhidadhati tasya vācam evāgnir abhidadhāti prāṇaṃ vāyuś cakṣur ādityaś śrotraṃ candramāḥ |
meaning: ते ह पुरुषं जायमानम् एव मृत्युपाशैर् अभिदधति तस्य वाचम् एवाग्निर् अभिदधाति प्राणं वायुश् चक्षुर् आदित्यश् श्रोत्रं चन्द्रमाः ।
text: They put upon man, when he is being born, the fetters of death. Agni puts [them] upon his speech, Vayu upon his breath, the sun upon his sight, the moon upon his hearing,
text_mt:
They indeed bind the man right as he is born with the nooses of death.
Agni binds his speech, Vāyu his breath, Āditya his sight, the Moon his hearing.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmuñcatīti |
meaning: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुञ्चतीति ।
text: This they say: " Verily it is the udgdtar who releaseth the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer."
text_mt: Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who releases the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths.'

sanskrit_iast: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsya vāci mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
meaning: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्य वाचि मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
text: For whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his speech.
text_mt: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, whatever noose of death is in his speech, that he releases from him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati ya evāsya prāṇe mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति य एवास्य प्राणे मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his breath,
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, whatever noose of death is in his breath, that he releases from him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsya cakṣuṣi mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रतिहरति य एवास्य चक्षुषि मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the pratihāra, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his sight.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, whatever noose of death is in his sight, that he releases from him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsya śrotre mṛtyupāśas tam evāsyonmuñcati |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्य श्रोत्रे मृत्युपाशस् तम् एवास्योन्मुञ्चति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, for him he releases that fetter of death which is in his hearing.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever noose of death is in his hearing, that he releases from him.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmuñcati |
meaning: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुञ्चति ।
text: Thus an udgdtar knowing thus releases the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer.
text_mt: Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus releases the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛṇātīti | saptame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृणातीति । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: This they say: " He is an udgdtar who, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, rescueth him then with his limbs, with his body, from every death."
text_mt:
Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths, then rescues him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death.'
First khaṇḍa in the seventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān hiṅkaroti ya evāsya lomasu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
meaning: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् हिङ्करोति य एवास्य लोमसु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
text: Now for whom one knowing thus utters the hinkdra, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his hairs.
text_mt: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus makes the hiṅkāra, from whatever noose of death is in his body hairs, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsya tvaci mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्य त्वचि मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his skin.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, from whatever noose of death is in his skin, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān ādim ādatte ya evāsya māṃseṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् आदिम् आदत्ते य एवास्य मांसेषु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus begins the ddi, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his flesh.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus takes up the ādi, from whatever noose of death is in his flesh, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān udgāyati ya evāsya snāvasu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उद्गायति य एवास्य स्नावसु मृत्युपाशस् तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgitha, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his sinews,
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, from whatever noose of death is in his sinews, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsyāṅgeṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |

text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the pratihāra, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his limbs.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, from whatever noose of death is in his limbs, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān upadravati ya evāsyāsthiṣu mṛtyupāśas tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |

text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the vpadrava, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his bones.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the upadrava, from whatever noose of death is in his bones, from that he rescues him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsya majjasu mṛtyupāśas sa tasmād evainaṃ spṛṇāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्य मज्जसु मृत्युपाशस् स तस्माद् एवैनं स्पृणाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, him he rescues from that fetter of death which is in his marrow, s. = IV. 9. 9.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever noose of death is in his marrow, he rescues him from that.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛṇāti |
meaning: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृणाति ।
text_mt: Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths, then rescues him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death.

sanskrit_iast: tad āhus sa vā udgātā yo yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛtvā svarge loke saptadhā dadhātīti |
meaning: तद् आहुस् स वा उद्गाता यो यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृत्वा स्वर्गे लोके सप्तधा दधातीति ।
text: This they say: "Verily he is the udgdtar who, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, having then rescued him with his limbs, with his body, from every death, placeth him in seven parts in the heavenly world."
text_mt: Regarding this they say: 'He indeed is an udgātṛ who, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths and then having rescued him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death, places him sevenfold in the heavenly world.'

sanskrit_iast: sa vā eṣa indro vaimṛdha udyan bhavati savitodito mitras saṃgavakāla indro vaikuṇṭho madhyandine samāvartamānaś śarva ugro devo lohitāyan prajāpatir eva saṃveśe 'stamitaḥ |
meaning: स वा एष इन्द्रो वैमृध उद्यन् भवति सवितोदितो मित्रस् संगवकाल इन्द्रो वैकुण्ठो मध्यन्दिने समावर्तमानश् शर्व उग्रो देवो लोहितायन् प्रजापतिर् एव संवेशे ऽस्तमितः ।
text: That same one, rising, is Indra Vaimrdha; risen, Savitar; Mitra at the time when the cows are driven together; Indra Vaikuntha at noon; when returning, ^^Śva; when it is becoming red, the formidable god; Prajapati when it has gone home to lie down.
text_mt: He indeed, rising, is Indra the repeller of foes; risen, he is Savitṛ; at mid-morning cattle-gathering time, he is Mitra; at midday, turning around, he is Indra Vaikuṇṭha; turning red, he is Śarva the fierce god; at resting, set, he is Prajāpati himself.

sanskrit_iast: tad yasyaivaṃ vidvān hiṅkaroti ya evāsyodyatas svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: तद् यस्यैवं विद्वान् हिङ्करोति य एवास्योद्यतस् स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
text: Thus for whom one knowing thus utters the hinkdra, what heavenly world there is of him rising, in that he thus places him.
text_mt: Therefore, for whom one knowing thus makes the hiṅkāra, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] is rising, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān prastauti ya evāsyodite svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रस्तौति य एवास्योदिते स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the prastāva, what heavenly world there is of him when he has risen, in that he thus places him.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the prastāva, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] has risen, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān ādim ādatte ya evāsya saṃgavakāle svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् आदिम् आदत्ते य एवास्य संगवकाले स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
text: And for whom one know10. ' &«-. 'Śya. Śsambhavak-. ■*-« prim, m., corrected to-o. '-a. ing thus begins the ddi, what heavenly world there is of him at the time when the cows are driven together, in that he thus places him.

text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the udgītha, what heavenly world there is of him at noon, in that he thus places him.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the udgītha, whatever heavenly world is his at midday, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān pratiharati ya evāsyāparāhṇe svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् प्रतिहरति य एवास्यापराह्णे स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।

text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the pratihāra, whatever heavenly world is his in the afternoon, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān upadravati ya evāsyāstaṃyatas svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् उपद्रवति य एवास्यास्तंयतस् स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus sings the upadrava, what heavenly world there is of him going home (setting), in that he thus places him.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus chants the upadrava, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] is setting, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: atha yasyaivaṃ vidvān nidhanam upaiti ya evāsyāstamite svargo lokas tasminn evainaṃ dadhāti |
meaning: अथ यस्यैवं विद्वान् निधनम् उपैति य एवास्यास्तमिते स्वर्गो लोकस् तस्मिन्न् एवैनं दधाति ।
text: And for whom one knowing thus enters upon the nidhana, what heavenly world there is of him when he has set, in that he thus places him.
text_mt: Then, for whom one knowing thus reaches the nidhana, whatever heavenly world is his as [the sun] has set, in that he places him.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ vā evaṃvid udgātā yajamānasya prāṇebhyo 'dhi mṛtyupāśān unmucyāthainaṃ sāṅgaṃ satanuṃ sarvamṛtyos spṛtvā svarge loke saptadhā dadhāti | saptame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | saptamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: एवं वा एवंविद् उद्गाता यजमानस्य प्राणेभ्यो ऽधि मृत्युपाशान् उन्मुच्याथैनं साङ्गं सतनुं सर्वमृत्योस् स्पृत्वा स्वर्गे लोके सप्तधा दधाति । सप्तमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । सप्तमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Even so an udgdtar knowing thus, having released the fetters of death from the breaths of the sacrificer, having then rescued him with his limbs, with his body, from every death, places him in seven parts in the heavenly world.
text_mt:
Thus indeed the udgātṛ who knows thus, having released the nooses of death from the sacrificer's vital breaths and then having rescued him, with all his limbs and with his body, from all death, places him sevenfold in the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: ṣaḍ ḍha vai devatās svayambhuvo 'gnir vāyur asāv ādityaḥ prāṇo 'nnaṃ vāk |
meaning: षड् ढ वै देवतास् स्वयम्भुवो ऽग्निर् वायुर् असाव् आदित्यः प्राणो ऽन्नं वाक् ।
text: Verily there are six self-existing divinities, viz. Agni, Vayu, yonder sun, breath, food, speech,
text_mt: Six indeed are the self-existent deities: Agni, Vāyu, yonder Āditya, breath, food, and speech.

text_mt: They disputed for supremacy: 'I am the best! I am the best! Serve me as [your] glory!'

text: They did not recognize each the other's preeminence. They said: "Verily we do not recognize each the other's preeminence. Let us therefore explain together how we are best."

They did not yield to one another's supremacy.
They said: 'We do not yield to one another's supremacy. Come, let us explain together how we are the best.'

text: He said: " I, rising, become the day; I, setting, the night. By me as sight deeds are done. If I were not, there would be no day, no night; no deeds would be done." s. = 11.7. 4. = 11. 8.

He said: 'Rising, I myself become the day; setting, [I become] the night.
Through me as sight rituals are performed.
If I were not, there would be neither day nor night;
rituals would not be performed.

text_mt: Then they said to speech: "And how are you the best?"

meaning: ता अब्रुवन्न् एता वै किल सर्वा देवताः एकैकाम् एवानु स्मः स यन् नु नस् सर्वासां देवतानाम् एका चन न स्यात् तत इदं सर्वम् पराभवेत् ततो न किं चन परिशिष्येत हन्त सार्धं समेत्य यच् छ्रेष्ठं तद् असामेति ।
text: They said: " Verily these are complete divinities. We are dependent each upon each. Now if of us complete divinities any one were not, then this all would perish, then nothing at all would be left. Come, coming together let us be that which is best."
text_mt: They said: "All these deities indeed—we are one after another. If not even one of us, of all these deities, were here, this whole world would perish, and nothing at all would remain behind. Come, let us unite together and become that which is the best."

sanskrit_iast: tā etasmin prāṇa okāre vācy akāre samāyan tad yat samāyan tat sāmnas sāmatvam |

text: They came together in this breath, in the sound o, [and] in speech, in the sound a. Because they came together (y'i + satn), therefore the sāman is called so."
text_mt: They came together in this breath as the syllable o, [and] in speech as the syllable a. That they came together (sam-āyan), that is the sāman-nature of the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: tā abruvan yāni no martyāny anapahatapāpmāny akṣarāṇi tāny uddhṛtyāmṛteṣv apahatapāpmasu śuddheṣv akṣareṣu gāyatraṃ gāyāmāgnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
meaning: ता अब्रुवन् यानि नो मर्त्यान्य् अनपहतपाप्मान्य् अक्षराणि तान्य् उद्धृत्यामृतेष्व् अपहतपाप्मसु शुद्धेष्व् अक्षरेषु गायत्रं गायामाग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
text: They said: " Removing those syllables of us which are mortal, whose evil is not smitten away, let us sing a gāyatra in the syllables [which are] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure: in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech. Thereby having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, may we go to the heavenly world."
text_mt: They said: "Taking out those of our syllables that are mortal and not free from evil, let us sing the gāyatra chant upon the immortal, evil-free, pure syllables—in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech. Having thereby struck away death, having struck away evil, let us go to the heavenly world."

sanskrit_iast: ety agner amṛtam apahatapāpma śuddham akṣaram gnir ity asya martyam anapahatapāpmākṣaram |

text: A is the syllable of Agni [which is] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure; gnis is his syllable [which is] mortal, not having evil smitten away.
text_mt: "A" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of Agni; "gniḥ" is his mortal, evil-bound syllable.

text_mt: "Prā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of breath; "ṇaḥ" is its mortal, evil-bound syllable.

text_mt: "A" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of food; "nnam" is its mortal, evil-bound syllable.

text_mt: "Vā" is the immortal, evil-free, pure syllable of speech; "k" is her mortal, evil-bound syllable.

sanskrit_iast: tā etāni martyāny anapahatapāpmāny akṣarāṇy uddhṛtyāmṛteṣv apahatapāpmasu śuddheṣv akṣareṣu gāyatram āgāyann agnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci tenāpahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam āyan |
meaning: ता एतानि मर्त्यान्य् अनपहतपाप्मान्य् अक्षराण्य् उद्धृत्यामृतेष्व् अपहतपाप्मसु शुद्धेष्व् अक्षरेषु गायत्रम् आगायन्न् अग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि तेनापहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् ।
text: They, removing those syllables [which are] mortal, not having evil smitten away, sang the gāyatra in the syllables [which are] immortal, having evil smitten away, pure: in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech. Thereby having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, they went to the heavenly world,
text_mt: Taking out these mortal syllables not free from evil, they sang the gāyatra chant upon the immortal, evil-free, pure syllables—in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech. Having thereby struck away death, having struck away evil, they went to the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: apahatya mṛtyum apahatya pāpmānaṃ svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ veda | aṣṭame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: अपहत्य मृत्युम् अपहत्य पाप्मानं स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं वेद । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
text: Having smitten away death, having smitten away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus.
text_mt: Having struck away death, having struck away evil, he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus. / Third khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tā brahmābruvan tvayi pratiṣṭhāyaitam udyacchāmeti tā brahmābravīd āsyena prāṇena yuṣmān āsyena prāṇena mām upāpnavātheti |
meaning: ता ब्रह्माब्रुवन् त्वयि प्रतिष्ठायैतम् उद्यच्छामेति ता ब्रह्माब्रवीद् आस्येन प्राणेन युष्मान् आस्येन प्राणेन माम् उपाप्नवाथेति ।
text: They said to the brahman: "Standing firm in thee we will hold this one up." To them the brahman said: " With the breath in the mouth ye shall obtain yourselves, with the breath in the mouth me."
text_mt: They said to brahman: "Resting upon you, let us raise this [chant]." Brahman said to them: "Through the breath of the mouth you shall reach each other, through the breath of the mouth you shall reach me."

sanskrit_iast: tā etena prāṇenaukāreṇa vācy akāram abhinimeṣyantyo hiṅkārād bhakāram okāreṇa vācam anusvarantya ubhābhyām prāṇābhyāṃ gāyatram agāyann ovā3c ovā3c ovā3c hum bhā vo vā iti |
meaning: ता एतेन प्राणेनौकारेण वाच्य् अकारम् अभिनिमेष्यन्त्यो हिङ्काराद् भकारम् ओकारेण वाचम् अनुस्वरन्त्य उभाभ्याम् प्राणाभ्यां गायत्रम् अगायन्न् ओवा3च् ओवा3च् ओवा3च् हुम् भा वो वा इति ।
text: They, by this breath, the o-sound, being about to settle the a-sound in speech, and by the o-sound sounding the Ma-sound as speech after the hinkdra, sang the gāyatra with both these breaths: ovdSc ovdSc ovdSc hum bhd vo vd.
text_mt: With this breath as the syllable o, closing in upon the syllable a in speech, sounding speech from the hiṅkāra to the sound bha with the syllable o, they sang the gāyatra chant with both breaths: "ovā3c ovā3c ovā3c hum bhā vo vā".

sanskrit_iast: sa yathobhayāpadī pratitiṣṭhaty evam eva svarge loke pratyatiṣṭhan prati svarge loke tiṣṭhati ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: स यथोभयापदी प्रतितिष्ठत्य् एवम् एव स्वर्गे लोके प्रत्यतिष्ठन् प्रति स्वर्गे लोके तिष्ठति य एवं वेद ।
text: As one with both feet stands firm, even so they stood firm in the heavenly world. He stands firm in the heavenly world who knows thus.
text_mt: Just as a two-footed creature stands firm, even so they stood firm in the heavenly world. He stands firm in the heavenly world who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: ya u ha vā evaṃvid asmāl lokāt praiti sa prāṇa eva bhūtvā vāyum apyeti vāyor adhy abhrāṇy abhrebhyo 'dhi vṛṣṭiṃ vṛṣṭyaivemaṃ lokam anuvibhavati |
meaning: य उ ह वा एवंविद् अस्माल् लोकात् प्रैति स प्राण एव भूत्वा वायुम् अप्येति वायोर् अध्य् अभ्राण्य् अभ्रेभ्यो ऽधि वृष्टिं वृष्ट्यैवेमं लोकम् अनुविभवति ।
text: And he who knowing thus departs from this world, he, having become breath, goes unto Vayu, from Vayu unto the clouds, from the clouds unto rain. With rain he extends over this world,
text_mt: And whoever, knowing thus, departs from this world, becoming breath alone, he enters Vāyu; from Vāyu into the clouds; from the clouds into rain; through the rain alone he pervades this world.

sanskrit_iast: ṛṣayo ha sattram āsāṃ cakrire te punaḥ-punar bahvībhir-bahvībhiḥ pratipadbhis svargasya lokasya dvāraṃ nānu cana bubudhire |
meaning: ऋषयो ह सत्त्रम् आसां चक्रिरे ते पुनः-पुनर् बह्वीभिर्-बह्वीभिः प्रतिपद्भिस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारं नानु चन बुबुधिरे ।
text: The sages (rsi) sat a session (sattra). They again and again with many, many introductory stanzas did in no way perceive the door of the heavenly world,
text_mt: The sages performed a sacrificial session. Time and again, through very many introductory verses, they did not perceive the door to the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: ta u śrameṇa tapasā vratacaryeṇendram avarurudhire |
meaning: त उ श्रमेण तपसा व्रतचर्येणेन्द्रम् अवरुरुधिरे ।
text: And they with exertion, with penance, with the performance of vows, got possession of Indra.
text_mt: Through weariness, ascetic heat, and the observance of vows, they won over Indra.

sanskrit_iast: taṃ hocus svargaṃ vai lokam aipsiṣma te punaḥ-punar bahvībhir-bahvībhiḥ pratipadbhis svargasya lokasya dvāraṃ nānu canābhutsmahi tathā no 'nuśādhi yathā svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam iyāmeti |
meaning: तं होचुस् स्वर्गं वै लोकम् ऐप्सिष्म ते पुनः-पुनर् बह्वीभिर्-बह्वीभिः प्रतिपद्भिस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारं नानु चनाभुत्स्महि तथा नो ऽनुशाधि यथा स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् इयामेति ।
text: They said to him: " We have desired to obtain the heavenly world; yet again and again with many, many introductory stanzas have we in no way perceived the door of the heavenly world. Teach us so that we, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, may go to the heavenly world."
text_mt: They said to him: "We have desired the heavenly world. Time and again, through very many introductory verses, we have not perceived the door to the heavenly world. Instruct us so that, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, we may go to the heavenly world."

sanskrit_iast: tān hovāca ko vas sthaviratama iti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: तान् होवाच को वस् स्थविरतम इति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
text: He said to them: " Who of you is the oldest?"
text_mt: He said to them: "Who among you is the oldest?" / Fourth khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: aham ity agastyaḥ |
meaning: अहम् इत्य् अगस्त्यः ।
text: "I," said Agastya.
text_mt: "I am," said Agastya.

sanskrit_iast: sa vā ehīti hovāca tasmai vai te 'haṃ tad vakṣyāmi yad vidvāṃsas svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam eṣyatheti |
meaning: स वा एहीति होवाच तस्मै वै ते ऽहं तद् वक्ष्यामि यद् विद्वांसस् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एष्यथेति ।
text: "Then come," he said; "I will tell thee that which knowing ye, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, shall go to the heavenly world."
text_mt: "Come then," he said; "to you, indeed, I shall speak that by which, knowing it, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, you will go to the heavenly world."

sanskrit_iast: tasmā etaṃ gāyatrasyodgītham upaniṣadam amṛtam uvācāgnau vāyāv āditye prāṇe 'nne vāci |
meaning: तस्मा एतं गायत्रस्योद्गीथम् उपनिषदम् अमृतम् उवाचाग्नौ वायाव् आदित्ये प्राणे ऽन्ने वाचि ।
text: To him he told this udgītha of the gāyatra[-sdm,an, the upaniṣad, the immortal, in Agni, in Vayu, in the sun, in breath, in food, in speech.
text_mt: To him he declared this immortal upaniṣad, the udgītha of the gāyatra chant, in Agni, in Vāyu, in Āditya, in breath, in food, [and] in speech.

sanskrit_iast: tato vai te svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtās svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam āyan |
meaning: ततो वै ते स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तास् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् ।
text: Verily they then, perceiving the door of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, went to the heavenly woi-ld.
text_mt: Then indeed, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, they went to the heavenly world.

sanskrit_iast: evam evaivaṃ vidvān svargasya lokasya dvāram anuprajñāyānārtas svasti saṃvatsarasyodṛcaṃ gatvā svargaṃ lokam eti | aṣṭame 'nuvāke pañcamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | aṣṭamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: एवम् एवैवं विद्वान् स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य द्वारम् अनुप्रज्ञायानार्तस् स्वस्ति संवत्सरस्योदृचं गत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् एति । अष्टमे ऽनुवाके पञ्चमः खण्डः । अष्टमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Even so one knowing thus, perceiving the gate of the heavenly world, unharmed, having gone successfully to the end of the year, goes to the heavenly world.
text_mt: Even so, one who knows thus, having recognized the door to the heavenly world, unharmed, safely reaching the end of the year, goes to the heavenly world. / Fifth khaṇḍa in the eighth anuvāka. / The eighth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: evaṃ vā etaṃ gāyatrasyodgītham upaniṣadam amṛtam indro 'gastyāyovācāgastya iṣāya śyāvāśvaya iṣaś śyāvāśvir gauṣūktaye gauṣūktir jvālāyanāya jvālāyanaś śāṭyāyanaye śāṭyāyanī rāmāya krātujāteyāya vaiyāghrapadyāya rāmaḥ krātujāteyo vaiyāghrapadyaḥ | navame 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: एवं वा एतं गायत्रस्योद्गीथम् उपनिषदम् अमृतम् इन्द्रो ऽगस्त्यायोवाचागस्त्य इषाय श्यावाश्वय इषश् श्यावाश्विर् गौषूक्तये गौषूक्तिर् ज्वालायनाय ज्वालायनश् शाट्यायनये शाट्यायनी रामाय क्रातुजातेयाय वैयाघ्रपद्याय रामः क्रातुजातेयो वैयाघ्रपद्यः । नवमे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: Verily thus Indra told this ijdg'itha of the gāyatra \-sāman'\, the upaniṣad, the immortal, to Agastya, Agastya to Isa 9ysiva9vi, Isa ()y«\&(}\'i to Gfiusukti, Gausukti to Jvalayana, Jvalayana to Śatyayani, 9Styayani to Rama Kratujateya Vaiyaghrapadya, Rama Kratujateya Vaij'aghrapadya—
text_mt: Thus, indeed, Indra declared this immortal upaniṣad, the udgītha of the gāyatra chant, to Agastya; Agastya to Iṣa Śyāvāśvaya; Iṣa Śyāvāśvi to Gauṣūkti; Gauṣūkti to Jvālāyana; Jvālāyana to Śāṭyāyani; Śāṭyāyani to Rāma Krātujāteya Vaiyāghrapadya; Rāma Krātujāteya Vaiyāghrapadya— / First khaṇḍa in the ninth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: śaṅkhāya bābhravyāya śaṅkho bābhravyo dakṣāya kātyāyanaya ātreyāya dakṣaḥ kātyāyanir ātreyaḥ kaṃsāya vārakyāya kaṃso vārakyas suyajñāya śāṇḍilyāya suyajñaś śāṇḍilyo 'gnidattāya śāṇḍilyāyāgnidattaś śāṇḍilyas suyajñāya śāṇḍilyāya suyajñaś śāṇḍilyo jayantāya vārakyāya jayanto vārakyo janaśrutāya vārakyāya janaśruto vārakyas sudattāya pārāśaryāya |
meaning: शङ्खाय बाभ्रव्याय शङ्खो बाभ्रव्यो दक्षाय कात्यायनय आत्रेयाय दक्षः कात्यायनिर् आत्रेयः कंसाय वारक्याय कंसो वारक्यस् सुयज्ञाय शाण्डिल्याय सुयज्ञश् शाण्डिल्यो ऽग्निदत्ताय शाण्डिल्यायाग्निदत्तश् शाण्डिल्यस् सुयज्ञाय शाण्डिल्याय सुयज्ञश् शाण्डिल्यो जयन्ताय वारक्याय जयन्तो वारक्यो जनश्रुताय वारक्याय जनश्रुतो वारक्यस् सुदत्ताय पाराशर्याय ।
text: — to _9ankha Bfibhravya, Śafikha Babhravya to Daksa Katyfiyaiii Atreya, Daksa Katyfiyani Atreya to Kansa Vfirakji^a, Kansa Vfivakya to Suyajfia Śandilya, Suyajfia (Śfindilya to Jayanta Varakya, Jayanta Vfirakya to Janagnita Varakya, Jana9ruta Varakya to Sudatta ParJi9arya. That same upaniṣad of the gāyatra [sdmanl of Śiity'Śyani is to be worshiped thus.
text_mt: —to Śaṅkha Bābhravya; Śaṅkha Bābhravya to Dakṣa Kātyāyani Ātreya; Dakṣa Kātyāyani Ātreya to Kaṃsa Vārakya; Kaṃsa Vārakya to Suyajña Śāṇḍilya; Suyajña Śāṇḍilya to Agnidatta Śāṇḍilya; Agnidatta Śāṇḍilya to Suyajña Śāṇḍilya; Suyajña Śāṇḍilya to Jayanta Vārakya; Jayanta Vārakya to Janaśruta Vārakya; Janaśruta Vārakya to Sudatta Pārāśarya.

sanskrit_iast: saiṣā śāṭyāyanī gāyatrasyopaniṣad evam upāsitavyā | navame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | navamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: सैषा शाट्यायनी गायत्रस्योपनिषद् एवम् उपासितव्या । नवमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । नवमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text_mt: This is that Śāṭyāyanī upaniṣad of the gāyatra chant; it is to be meditated upon thus. / Second khaṇḍa in the ninth anuvāka. / The ninth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: keneṣitam patati preṣitam manaḥ kena prāṇaḥ prathamaḥ praiti yuktaḥ keneṣitāṃ vācam imāṃ vadanti cakṣuś śrotraṃ ka u devo yunakti |
meaning: केनेषितम् पतति प्रेषितम् मनः केन प्राणः प्रथमः प्रैति युक्तः केनेषितां वाचम् इमां वदन्ति चक्षुश् श्रोत्रं क उ देवो युनक्ति ।
text: Sent by whom does the mind, sent forth, fly? Yoked by whom does the first breath come forth? By whom is this speech sent which they speak? And which god yokes sight [and] hearing?
text_mt:
"By whom impelled does the mind fly forth sent?
By whom yoked does the first breath move forward?
By whom impelled do they speak this speech?
And what god yokes the eye and the ear?"

sanskrit_iast: śrotrasya śrotram manaso mano yad vāco ha vācaṃ sa u prāṇasya prāṇaḥ cakṣuṣaś cakṣur atimucya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāl lokād amṛtā bhavanti |
meaning: श्रोत्रस्य श्रोत्रम् मनसो मनो यद् वाचो ह वाचं स उ प्राणस्य प्राणः चक्षुषश् चक्षुर् अतिमुच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल् लोकाद् अमृता भवन्ति ।
text: Released from the hearing of the hearing, from the mind of the mind, from the speech of speech—and that is also the breath of the breath—from the sight of the sight, the wise departing from this world become immortal.
text_mt:
That which is the ear of the ear, the mind of the mind, the speech of speech, that indeed is the breath of breath,
the eye of the eye. Having relinquished [them], the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.

sanskrit_iast: na tatra cakṣur gacchati na vāg gacchati no manaḥ na vidma na vijānīmo yathaitad anuśiṣyāt |
meaning: न तत्र चक्षुर् गच्छति न वाग् गच्छति नो मनः न विद्म न विजानीमो यथैतद् अनुशिष्यात् ।
text: Sight does not go there, speech does not go there, neither [does] mind. We do not know, we do not distinguish, how one might teach that.
text_mt:
The eye does not go there, nor does speech go, nor the mind.
We do not know, we do not comprehend how one could instruct this.

sanskrit_iast: anyad eva tad viditād atho aviditād adhi iti śuśruma pūrveṣāṃ ye nas tad vyācacakṣire |
meaning: अन्यद् एव तद् विदिताद् अथो अविदिताद् अधि इति शुश्रुम पूर्वेषां ये नस् तद् व्याचचक्षिरे ।
text: "It is different from the known and likewise from the unknown;" thus we heard from those of old, who explained it to us.
text_mt:
It is indeed different from the known, and moreover above the unknown.
Thus have we heard from the ancients who explained that to us.

sanskrit_iast: yad vācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāg abhyudyate tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
meaning: यद् वाचानभ्युदितं येन वाग् अभ्युद्यते तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
text: That which is not declared by speech, that by which speech is declared, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
text_mt:
That which is not expressed by speech, by which speech is expressed—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

sanskrit_iast: yan manasā na manute yenāhur mano matam tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
meaning: यन् मनसा न मनुते येनाहुर् मनो मतम् तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
text: That which one does not think with the mind, that by which they say the mind is thought, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
text_mt:
That which one does not think with the mind, by which, they say, the mind is thought—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

sanskrit_iast: yac cakṣuṣā na paśyati yena cakṣūṃṣi paśyati tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
meaning: यच् चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यति तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
text: That which one does not see with sight, that by which one sees sights, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
text_mt:
That which one does not see with the eye, by which one sees eyes—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

sanskrit_iast: yac chrotreṇa na śṛṇoti yena śrotram idaṃ śrutam tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
meaning: यच् छ्रोत्रेण न शृणोति येन श्रोत्रम् इदं श्रुतम् तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
text: That which one does not hear with hearing, that by which this hearing is heard, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
text_mt:
That which one does not hear with the ear, by which this ear is heard—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.

sanskrit_iast: yat prāṇena na prāṇiti yena prāṇaḥ praṇīyate tad eva brahma tvaṃ viddhi nedaṃ yad idam upāsate |
meaning: यत् प्राणेन न प्राणिति येन प्राणः प्रणीयते तद् एव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यद् इदम् उपासते ।
text: That which one does not breathe with breath, that by which breath is led forth, only that know thou as brahman, not that which they worship here.
text_mt:
That which one does not breathe with breath, by which breath is guided—
know that alone as brahman, not this which they worship here.
The first khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: yadi manyase su vedeti dahram evāpi nūnaṃ tvaṃ vettha brahmaṇo rūpaṃ yad asya tvaṃ yad asya deveṣu atha nu mīmāṃsyam eva te manye 'viditam |
meaning: यदि मन्यसे सु वेदेति दह्रम् एवापि नूनं त्वं वेत्थ ब्रह्मणो रूपं यद् अस्य त्वं यद् अस्य देवेषु अथ नु मीमांस्यम् एव ते मन्ये ऽविदितम् ।
text: If thou thinkest: " I know [it] well," little dost thou even then know the form of the brahman, what of it thou [art?], what of it [is] among the gods. Now then I think what is unknown is to be pondered upon by thee.
text_mt:
If you think: "I know [it] well," indeed you surely know only a small form of brahman—what of it is in you, and what of it is among the gods.
Therefore now it is indeed to be investigated by you. I think it is [not yet] understood.

sanskrit_iast: nāham manye su vedeti no na vedeti veda ca yo nas tad veda tad veda no na vedeti veda ca |
meaning: नाहम् मन्ये सु वेदेति नो न वेदेति वेद च यो नस् तद् वेद तद् वेद नो न वेदेति वेद च ।
text: I do not think: "I know [itj well," neither do I know: "I know [it] not." He of us who knows this knows it (the brahman), and he does not know: " I know [it] not."
text_mt:
I do not think: "I know [it] well," nor: "I do not know." I know it too.
He among us who knows that, knows that; nor does he know: "I do not know," and yet he knows.

sanskrit_iast: yasyāmataṃ tasya matam mataṃ yasya na veda saḥ avijñātaṃ vijānatāṃ avijānatām |
meaning: यस्यामतं तस्य मतम् मतं यस्य न वेद सः अविज्ञातं विजानतां अविजानताम् ।
text: Of whom it is not thought, of him it is thought; of whom it is thought, he knows it not. Not understood [is it] of those who understand; [it is] understood '*,• of those who do not understand;
text_mt:
He by whom it is unthought, to him it is thought; he to whom it is thought does not know.
It is unknown to those who know; [it is] known to those who do not know.

sanskrit_iast: pratibodhaviditam matam amṛtatvaṃ hi vindate ātmanā vindate vīryaṃ vidyayā vindate 'mṛtam |
meaning: प्रतिबोधविदितम् मतम् अमृतत्वं हि विन्दते आत्मना विन्दते वीर्यं विद्यया विन्दते ऽमृतम् ।
text: It is thought to be known in awakening (?), for one finds immortality; by the self one finds strength, by knowledge one finds immortality,
text_mt:
When it is known with every awakening, it is comprehended, for [thereby] one finds immortality.
By the self one finds vigor; by knowledge one finds immortality.

sanskrit_iast: iha ced avedīd atha satyam asti na ced ihāvedīn mahatī vinaṣṭiḥ bhūteṣu-bhūteṣu vivicya dhīrāḥ pretyāsmāl lokād amṛtā bhavanti | daśame 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: इह चेद् अवेदीद् अथ सत्यम् अस्ति न चेद् इहावेदीन् महती विनष्टिः भूतेषु-भूतेषु विविच्य धीराः प्रेत्यास्माल् लोकाद् अमृता भवन्ति । दशमे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: If one has known [it] here, then it is true; and if one has not known [it] here, [there is] great loss. The wise, having separated [it] in the several beings, departing from this world become immortal.
text_mt:
If one has known it here, then truth exists;
if one has not known it here, great is the destruction.
Distinguishing [it] in each and every being, the wise, departing from this world, become immortal.
The second khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: brahma ha devebhyo vijigye tasya ha brahmaṇo vijaye devā amahīyanta ta aikṣantāsmākam evāyaṃ vijayaḥ asmākam evāyam mahimeti |
meaning: ब्रह्म ह देवेभ्यो विजिग्ये तस्य ह ब्रह्मणो विजये देवा अमहीयन्त त ऐक्षन्तास्माकम् एवायं विजयः अस्माकम् एवायम् महिमेति ।
text: The brahman won a complete victory for the gods. By the complete victory of this brahman the gods were exalted. They considered: " Ours is this complete victory, ours is this greatness."
text_mt:
Brahman indeed won a victory for the gods.
In that victory of brahman the gods grew exultant.
They thought: "Ours alone is this victory;
ours alone is this greatness."

sanskrit_iast: tad dhaiṣāṃ vijajñau tebhyo ha prādur babhūva tan na vyajānanta kim idaṃ yakṣam iti |
meaning: तद् धैषां विजज्ञौ तेभ्यो ह प्रादुर् बभूव तन् न व्यजानन्त किम् इदं यक्षम् इति ।
text: Now it (the brahman) became aware of this [thought] of them. It manifested itself to them. They did not recognize it [saying]: " What is this spectre?"
text_mt:
It knew this [thought] of theirs.
It appeared to them.
They did not know what this wonder was.

sanskrit_iast: te 'gnim abruvañ jātaveda etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti |
meaning: ते ऽग्निम् अब्रुवञ् जातवेद एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति ।
text: They said to Agni: " O Jfitavedas, find that out, what spectre this is." "Yes."
text_mt:
They said to Agni: "Jātavedas, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."

sanskrit_iast: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti agnir vā aham asmīty abravīj jātavedā vā aham asmīti |
meaning: तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् को ऽसीति अग्निर् वा अहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीज् जातवेदा वा अहम् अस्मीति ।
text: He ran to it. It said unto him: "Who art thou?" "I am Agni," he said; "I am Jatavedas."
text_mt:
He ran up to it.
It said to him: "Who are you?"
"I am Agni," he said, "or I am Jātavedas."

sanskrit_iast: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti apīdaṃ sarvaṃ daheyam yad idam pṛthivyām iti |
meaning: तस्मिंस् त्वयि किं वीर्यम् इति अपीदं सर्वं दहेयम् यद् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति ।
text: "What strength then is in thee?" " I could burn even everything which is here on earth."
text_mt:
"In that you, what is the power?"
"I could burn even all this whatever is here on earth."

sanskrit_iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad daheti tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśāka dagdhum sa tata eva nivavṛte nainad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti |
meaning: तस्मै तृणं निदधाव् एतद् दहेति तद् उपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन् न शशाक दग्धुम् स तत एव निववृते नैनद् अशकं विज्ञातुं यद् एतद् यक्षम् इति ।
text: It put down before him a blade of grass [saying]: "Burn this." Approaching it with all his might he could not burn it. Thereupon he returned [saying]: " I could not find out what spectre this is."
text_mt:
It placed a blade of grass before him: "Burn this!"
He went up to it with all speed.
He was not able to burn it.
He returned right from there: "I was not able to find out what this wonder is."

sanskrit_iast: atha vāyum abruvan vāyav etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti |
meaning: अथ वायुम् अब्रुवन् वायव् एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति ।
text: Then they said to Vfiyu: "O Vfiyu, find that out, what spectre this is." " Yes."
text_mt:
Then they said to Vāyu: "Vāyu, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."

sanskrit_iast: tad abhyadravat tam abhyavadat ko 'sīti vāyur vā aham asmīty abravīn mātariśvā vā aham asmīti |
meaning: तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तम् अभ्यवदत् को ऽसीति वायुर् वा अहम् अस्मीत्य् अब्रवीन् मातरिश्वा वा अहम् अस्मीति ।
text: He ran to it. " It said unto him: "Who art thou?" "I am Vayu," he said; "I am Matari9van." " What strength then is in thee?" " I could take even everything that is here on earth."
text_mt:
He ran up to it.
It said to him: "Who are you?"
"I am Vāyu," he said, "or I am Mātariśvan."

sanskrit_iast: tasmiṃs tvayi kiṃ vīryam iti apīdaṃ sarvam ādadīya yad idam pṛthivyām iti |
meaning: तस्मिंस् त्वयि किं वीर्यम् इति अपीदं सर्वम् आददीय यद् इदम् पृथिव्याम् इति ।
text: It put down before him a blade of grass [saying]: "Take this." Approaching it with all his might he could not take it. Thereupon he returned [saying]: "I could not find out what spectre this is."
text_mt:
"In that you, what is the power?"
"I could seize even all this whatever is here on earth."

sanskrit_iast: tasmai tṛṇaṃ nidadhāv etad ādatsveti tad upapreyāya sarvajavena tan na śaśākādātum sa tata eva nivavṛte nainad aśakaṃ vijñātuṃ yad etad yakṣam iti |
meaning: तस्मै तृणं निदधाव् एतद् आदत्स्वेति तद् उपप्रेयाय सर्वजवेन तन् न शशाकादातुम् स तत एव निववृते नैनद् अशकं विज्ञातुं यद् एतद् यक्षम् इति ।
text: Then they said to Indra: "O Maghavan, find that out, what spectre this is." " Yes." He ran to it. It was concealed from him.
text_mt:
It placed a blade of grass before him: "Seize this!"
He went up to it with all speed.
He was not able to seize it.
He returned right from there: "I was not able to find out what this wonder is."

sanskrit_iast: athendram abruvan maghavann etad vijānīhi kim etad yakṣam iti tatheti tad abhyadravat tasmāt tiro 'dadhe |
meaning: अथेन्द्रम् अब्रुवन् मघवन्न् एतद् विजानीहि किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति तथेति तद् अभ्यद्रवत् तस्मात् तिरो ऽदधे ।
text: In that same space he encountered a woman, greatly shining, Uma Haimavati. He said to her: "What spectre is this?"
text_mt:
Then they said to Indra: "Maghavan, find this out: what is this wonder?"
"So be it."
He ran up to it.
It vanished from him.

sanskrit_iast: sa tasminn evākāśe striyam ājagāma bahu śobhamānām umāṃ haimavatīm tāṃ hovāca kim etad yakṣam iti | daśame 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स तस्मिन्न् एवाकाशे स्त्रियम् आजगाम बहु शोभमानाम् उमां हैमवतीम् तां होवाच किम् एतद् यक्षम् इति । दशमे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
text_mt:
In that very space he came upon a woman, Umā Haimavatī, shining exceedingly.
He said to her: "What is this wonder?"
The third khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etad vijaye mahīyadhva iti tato haiva vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
meaning: ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद् विजये महीयध्व इति ततो हैव विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
text: " The JraAmaw," she said; " through the J^-aAwiaw'* complete victory ye are exalted." Then he knew: " [It is] the brahman.'"
text_mt:
"It is brahman," she said. "In the victory of brahman indeed are you exulting."
Then indeed he came to know: "It is brahman."

sanskrit_iast: tasmād vā ete devā atitarām ivānyān devān yad agnir vāyur indraḥ te hy enan nediṣṭham paspṛśus sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
meaning: तस्माद् वा एते देवा अतितराम् इवान्यान् देवान् यद् अग्निर् वायुर् इन्द्रः ते ह्य् एनन् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पृशुस् स ह्य् एनत् प्रथमो विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
text: Therefore indeed these gods—viz. Agni, Vayu, Indra—are as it were greatly above the other gods. For they touched it nearest; for he first knew it to be the brahman.
text_mt:
Therefore indeed these gods far surpass, as it were, the other gods—namely, Agni, Vāyu, and Indra;
for they touched it nearest; for he [Indra] first came to know: "It is brahman."

sanskrit_iast: tasmād vā indro 'titarām ivānyān devān sa hy enan nediṣṭham pasparśa sa hy enat prathamo vidāṃ cakāra brahmeti |
meaning: तस्माद् वा इन्द्रो ऽतितराम् इवान्यान् देवान् स ह्य् एनन् नेदिष्ठम् पस्पर्श स ह्य् एनत् प्रथमो विदां चकार ब्रह्मेति ।
text: Therefore indeed Indra is as it were greatly above the other gods. For he touched it nearest; for he first knew it to be the brahman.
text_mt:
Therefore indeed Indra far surpasses, as it were, the other gods;
for he touched it nearest; for he first came to know: "It is brahman."

sanskrit_iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yad etad vidyuto vyadyutad ā3 iti nyamiṣad ā3 ity adhidevatam |
meaning: तस्यैष आदेशो यद् एतद् विद्युतो व्यद्युतद् आ3 इति न्यमिषद् आ3 इत्य् अधिदेवतम् ।
text: Regarding it [there is] this direction: " What of the lightning hath lightened: ah! hath winked: ah!" Thus with regard to the divinities,
text_mt:
This is its teaching: that which is this flashing of lightning, "Ah!", that it winked, "Ah!"—
thus pertaining to the deities.

sanskrit_iast: athādhyātmam yad enad gacchatīva ca mano 'nena cainad upasmaraty abhīkṣṇaṃ saṃkalpaḥ |
meaning: अथाध्यात्मम् यद् एनद् गच्छतीव च मनो ऽनेन चैनद् उपस्मरत्य् अभीक्ष्णं संकल्पः ।
text: Now with regard to the self. That which both goes as mind, as it were, and through it (mind) imagination continually remembers it (the brahman).
text_mt:
Now pertaining to the self:
that which the mind goes to, as it were, and by which memory repeatedly recalls it—[that is] intention.

sanskrit_iast: tad dha tadvanaṃ nāma tadvanam ity upāsitavyam sa ya etad evaṃ vedābhi hainaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni saṃvāṅchanti |
meaning: तद् ध तद्वनं नाम तद्वनम् इत्य् उपासितव्यम् स य एतद् एवं वेदाभि हैनं सर्वाणि भूतानि संवाङ्छन्ति ।
text: Verily it is tadvana by name. As tadvana it is to be worshiped. Who knows this thus, unto him all beings desire together.
text_mt:
That is called Tadvana, "the longing for that."
It is to be worshiped as Tadvana.
He who knows this thus, towards him indeed all beings yearn.

sanskrit_iast: upaniṣadam bho brūhīti uktā ta upaniṣat brāhmīṃ vāva ta upaniṣadam abrūmeti |
meaning: उपनिषदम् भो ब्रूहीति उक्ता त उपनिषत् ब्राह्मीं वाव त उपनिषदम् अब्रूमेति ।
text: " Sir, tell the upaniṣad." " The upaniṣad has been told thee. Verily, we told thee the upaniṣad of the brahman.'"

sanskrit_iast: tasyai tapo damaḥ karmeti pratiṣṭhā vedās sarvāṅgāṇi satyam āyatanam |
meaning: तस्यै तपो दमः कर्मेति प्रतिष्ठा वेदास् सर्वाङ्गाणि सत्यम् आयतनम् ।
text: Penance, restraint, action are its foundation, the Vedas all its limbs, truth its abode.
text_mt: Austerity, self-restraint, action are its foundation; the Vedas are all its limbs; truth is its abode.

sanskrit_iast: yo vā etām evaṃ vedāpahatya pāpmānam anante svarge loke 'jyeye pratitiṣṭhati | daśame 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | daśamo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: यो वा एताम् एवं वेदापहत्य पाप्मानम् अनन्ते स्वर्गे लोके ऽज्येये प्रतितिष्ठति । दशमे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः । दशमो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Verily he who knows this \upaniṣad'\ thus, having smitten away evil, stands firm in the endless heavenly world that is not to be injured.
text_mt:
He who indeed knows this thus, striking off evil, is established in the endless, unconquerable heavenly world—he is established.
The fourth khaṇḍa in the tenth anuvāka.
The tenth anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: āśā vā idam agra āsīd bhaviṣyad eva tad abhavat tā āpo 'bhavan |
meaning: आशा वा इदम् अग्र आसीद् भविष्यद् एव तद् अभवत् ता आपो ऽभवन् ।
text: Verily this was in the beginning space, being about to become. It became. It became the waters.
text_mt:
Space (hope) indeed was here in the beginning, just about to become.
That became.
That became the waters.

sanskrit_iast: tās tapo 'tapyanta tās tapas tepānā huss ity eva prācīḥ prāśvasan sa vāva prāṇo 'bhavat |
meaning: तास् तपो ऽतप्यन्त तास् तपस् तेपाना हुस्स् इत्य् एव प्राचीः प्राश्वसन् स वाव प्राणो ऽभवत् ।
text: They performed penance. Having performed penance [uttering] huss, they breathed forth forward. That became breath.
text_mt:
They practiced austerity.
As they practiced austerity, they breathed forward with the sound "huss!".
That indeed became the forward-breath (prāṇa).

sanskrit_iast: tāḥ prāṇyāpānan sa vā apāno 'bhavat |
meaning: ताः प्राण्यापानन् स वा अपानो ऽभवत् ।
text: Having breathed forth, they breathed out. That became exhalation.
text_mt:
Having breathed forward, they breathed downward.
That indeed became the downward-breath (apāna).

sanskrit_iast: tā apānya vyānan sa vāva vyāno 'bhavat |
meaning: ता अपान्य व्यानन् स वाव व्यानो ऽभवत् ।
text: Having breathed out, they breathed asunder. That became the vydna.
text_mt:
Having breathed downward, they breathed dispersed.
That indeed became the dispersed-breath (vyāna).

sanskrit_iast: tā vyānya samānan sa vāva samāno 'bhavat |
meaning: ता व्यान्य समानन् स वाव समानो ऽभवत् ।
text: Having breathed asunder, they breathed together. That became the samdna.
text_mt:
Having breathed dispersed, they breathed together.
That indeed became the equalized-breath (samāna).

sanskrit_iast: tās samānyodānan sa vā udāno 'bhavat |
meaning: तास् समान्योदानन् स वा उदानो ऽभवत् ।
text: Having breathed together, they breathed up. That became the uddna.
text_mt:
Having breathed together, they breathed upward.
That indeed became the upward-breath (udāna).

sanskrit_iast: tad idam ekam eva sadhamādyam āsīd aviviktam |
meaning: तद् इदम् एकम् एव सधमाद्यम् आसीद् अविविक्तम् ।
text: This [all] was one, associated, not distinguished.
text_mt: This was then just one united whole, undistinguished.

sanskrit_iast: sa nāmarūpam akuruta tenainad vyavinak vi ha pāpmano vicyate ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: स नामरूपम् अकुरुत तेनैनद् व्यविनक् वि ह पाप्मनो विच्यते य एवं वेद ।
text: He made name and form. Thereby he distinguished it. Distinguished from evil is he who knows thus.
text_mt:
He made name and form.
By that he distinguished it.
He who knows thus is indeed separated from evil.

sanskrit_iast: tad asau vā ādityaḥ prāṇo 'gnir apāna āpo vyāno diśas samānaś candramā udānaḥ |
meaning: तद् असौ वा आदित्यः प्राणो ऽग्निर् अपान आपो व्यानो दिशस् समानश् चन्द्रमा उदानः ।
text: Verily yonder sun is breath, Agni is exhalation, the waters are the vydna, the quarters are the samdna, the moon is the uddna.
text_mt: Now that sun over there is the forward-breath; Agni is the downward-breath; the waters are the dispersed-breath; the directions are the equalized-breath; the moon is the upward-breath.

sanskrit_iast: tad vā etad ekam abhavat prāṇa eva sa ya evam etad ekam bhavad vedaivaṃ haitad ekadhā bhavatīty ekadhaiva śreṣṭhas svānām bhavati |
meaning: तद् वा एतद् एकम् अभवत् प्राण एव स य एवम् एतद् एकम् भवद् वेदैवं हैतद् एकधा भवतीत्य् एकधैव श्रेष्ठस् स्वानाम् भवति ।
text: Verily that became one, viz. breath. He who thus knows this as becoming one [saying]: " Verily this thus becometh onefold," he becomes at once the first among his own people,
text_mt:
That indeed became one: breath alone.
He who knows this thus becoming one—that this becomes singly unified—becomes the foremost of his own [people] in a single manner.

sanskrit_iast: tad agnir vai prāṇo vāg iti pṛthivī vāyur vai prāṇo vāg ity antarikṣam ādityo vai prāṇo vāg iti dyaur diśo vai prāṇo vāg iti śrotraṃ candramā vai prāṇo vāg iti manaḥ pumān vai prāṇo vāg iti strī |
meaning: तद् अग्निर् वै प्राणो वाग् इति पृथिवी वायुर् वै प्राणो वाग् इत्य् अन्तरिक्षम् आदित्यो वै प्राणो वाग् इति द्यौर् दिशो वै प्राणो वाग् इति श्रोत्रं चन्द्रमा वै प्राणो वाग् इति मनः पुमान् वै प्राणो वाग् इति स्त्री ।
text: Verily now Agni is breath, speech is the earth; Vayu is breath, speech is the atmosphere; the sun is breath, speech is the sky; the quarters are breath, speech is hearing; the moon is breath, speech is mind; man is breath, speech is woman.
text_mt: So Agni is breath, earth is speech; Vāyu is breath, the intermediate space is speech; Āditya is breath, heaven is speech; the directions are breath, the ear is speech; the moon is breath, the mind is speech; the male is breath, the female is speech.

sanskrit_iast: tasyedaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ śithilam bhuvanam āsīd aparyāptam |
meaning: तस्येदं सृष्टं शिथिलम् भुवनम् आसीद् अपर्याप्तम् ।
text: That creation of his, when created, was unsteady, not fully completed.
text_mt: This creation of his was a loose, unstable world, inadequate.

sanskrit_iast: sa manorūpam akuruta tena tat paryāpnot dṛḍhaṃ ha vā asyedaṃ sṛṣṭam aśithilam bhuvanam paryāptam bhavati ya evaṃ veda | ekādaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: स मनोरूपम् अकुरुत तेन तत् पर्याप्नोत् दृढं ह वा अस्येदं सृष्टम् अशिथिलम् भुवनम् पर्याप्तम् भवति य एवं वेद । एकादशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: He made the form of mind. By it he completed it. Verily stable becomes this creation which was created, not unsteady, completed, for him who knows thus.
text_mt: He made the form of mind; with it he encompassed it. Firm indeed, not loose, adequate does this created world become for him who knows thus. / First khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: saiṣā caturdhā vihitā śrīr udgīthas sāmārkyaṃ jyeṣṭhabrāhmaṇam |
meaning: सैषा चतुर्धा विहिता श्रीर् उद्गीथस् सामार्क्यं ज्येष्ठब्राह्मणम् ।
text: This is the fortune divided into four parts, viz. the udgītha, the sāman, the arkya, the chief brāhmaṇa.
text_mt: This is that prosperity, arranged in four ways: the udgītha, the sāman, the ṛc-nature (arkya), and the supreme brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vāvod vāg gī sa udgīthaḥ |
meaning: प्राणो वावोद् वाग् गी स उद्गीथः ।
text: Verily breath is ud, speech is gl/ that is the udgītha.
text_mt: Breath indeed is ud; speech is gī: that is the udgītha.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vāvāmo vāk sā tat sāma |
meaning: प्राणो वावामो वाक् सा तत् साम ।
text: Verily breath is he (ama), speech is she (sd); that is the sāman.
text_mt: Breath indeed is ama; speech is sā: that is the sāman.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vāva ko vāg ṛk tad arkyam |
meaning: प्राणो वाव को वाग् ऋक् तद् अर्क्यम् ।
text: Verily breath is ka, speech is rk; that is the arkya.
text_mt: Breath indeed is ka; speech is ṛk: that is the arkya.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vāva jyeṣṭho vāg brāhmaṇaṃ taj jyeṣṭhabrāhmaṇam |
meaning: प्राणो वाव ज्येष्ठो वाग् ब्राह्मणं तज् ज्येष्ठब्राह्मणम् ।
text: Verily breath is the highest, speech is the brāhmaṇa; that is the highest been told thee, since the elements have been told thee. With three elements separately (?) verily we told thee the upaniṣad."
text_mt: Breath indeed is the eldest; speech is the brāhmaṇa. That is the eldest brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit_iast: upaniṣadam bho brūhīti uktā ta upaniṣad yasya te dhātava uktāḥ tridhātu viṣu vāva ta upaniṣadam abrūmeti |
meaning: उपनिषदम् भो ब्रूहीति उक्ता त उपनिषद् यस्य ते धातव उक्ताः त्रिधातु विषु वाव त उपनिषदम् अब्रूमेति ।
text_mt:
‘Sir, teach the upaniṣad!’
‘The upaniṣad has been taught to you whose elements have been taught.
It was indeed the three-element [composition] in various ways that we taught you as the upaniṣad.’

sanskrit_iast: etac chuklaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tāmraṃ sāmavarṇa iti ha smāha yadaiva śuklakṛṣṇe tāmro varṇo 'bhyavaiti sa vai te vṛṅte daśama mānuṣam iti tridhātu sa aikṣata kva nu ma uttānāya śayānāyemā devatā baliṃ hareyur iti | ekādaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: एतच् छुक्लं कृष्णं ताम्रं सामवर्ण इति ह स्माह यदैव शुक्लकृष्णे ताम्रो वर्णो ऽभ्यवैति स वै ते वृङ्ते दशम मानुषम् इति त्रिधातु स ऐक्षत क्व नु म उत्तानाय शयानायेमा देवता बलिं हरेयुर् इति । एकादशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः ।
text: " That white, black, copper-red is the color of the sāman," he used to say; " when the copper-red color descendeth into the white and black, it snatcheth these two unto itself." He considered: "Where now may these divinities bring tribute to me lying supine?"
text_mt:
‘This white, dark, [and] copper-colored [form] is the color of the sāman,’ he used to say. ‘Whenever the copper color enters into the white and dark, that indeed wards off your tenth, human [state]’—this is the three-element [composition].
He reflected: ‘Where now may these deities bring tribute to me as I lie stretched out?’
Second khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: sa puruṣam eva prapadanāyāvṛṇīta |
meaning: स पुरुषम् एव प्रपदनायावृणीत ।
text: He chose man for a resort,
text_mt: He chose the person itself for entering.

sanskrit_iast: tam purastāt pratyañcam prāviśat tasmā urur abhavat tad urasa urastvam |
meaning: तम् पुरस्तात् प्रत्यञ्चम् प्राविशत् तस्मा उरुर् अभवत् तद् उरस उरस्त्वम् ।
text: He entered him from the front (east), turned toward him. For him he became wide (uru). Therefore the breast (toras) is called so.
text_mt:
He entered it from the front, moving inward.
For him, it became broad (uru).
That is the chest-nature (urastva) of the chest (uras).

sanskrit_iast: tasmā atrasada etā devatā baliṃ haranti |
meaning: तस्मा अत्रसद एता देवता बलिं हरन्ति ।
text: T'o him sitting there these divinities bring tribute.
text_mt: To him, sitting here, these deities bring tribute.

sanskrit_iast: vācam anuharantīm agnir asmai baliṃ harati |
meaning: वाचम् अनुहरन्तीम् अग्निर् अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
text: Agni brings to him as tribute speech bringing after.
text_mt: Following speech, Agni brings tribute to him.

sanskrit_iast: mano 'nuharac candramā asmai baliṃ harati |
meaning: मनो ऽनुहरच् चन्द्रमा अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
text: The moon brings to him as tribute mind bringing after.
text_mt: Following mind, Moon brings tribute to him.

sanskrit_iast: cakṣur anuharad ādityo 'smai baliṃ harati |
meaning: चक्षुर् अनुहरद् आदित्यो ऽस्मै बलिं हरति ।
text: The sun brings to him as tribute sight bringing after.
text_mt: Following the eye, Āditya brings tribute to him.

sanskrit_iast: śrotram anuharad diśo 'smai baliṃ haranti |
meaning: श्रोत्रम् अनुहरद् दिशो ऽस्मै बलिं हरन्ति ।
text: The quarters bring to him as tribute hearing bringing after.
text_mt: Following the ear, the directions bring tribute to him.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇam anuharantaṃ vāyur asmai baliṃ harati |
meaning: प्राणम् अनुहरन्तं वायुर् अस्मै बलिं हरति ।
text: Vayu brings to him as tribute breath bringing after.
text_mt: Following the breath, Vāyu brings tribute to him.

sanskrit_iast: tasyaite niṣkhātāḥ panthā balivāhanā ime prāṇāḥ evaṃ haitaṃ niṣkhātāḥ panthā balivāhanās sarvato 'piyanti prāṇā ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: तस्यैते निष्खाताः पन्था बलिवाहना इमे प्राणाः एवं हैतं निष्खाताः पन्था बलिवाहनास् सर्वतो ऽपियन्ति प्राणा य एवं वेद ।
text: These are his dug-out paths, carrying tribute, [viz.] these breaths. Thus dug-out paths, carrying tribute, approach from all sides him who knows thus.
text_mt:
These dug-out paths of his are tribute-bearers, these vital breaths.
In this way, dug-out paths, tribute-bearers, vital breaths come together from all sides to him who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: sā haiṣā brahmāsandīm ārūḍhā ā hāsmai brahmāsandīṃ haranty adhi ha brahmāsandīṃ rohati ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: सा हैषा ब्रह्मासन्दीम् आरूढा आ हास्मै ब्रह्मासन्दीं हरन्त्य् अधि ह ब्रह्मासन्दीं रोहति य एवं वेद ।
text: That [divinity] is seated on the brahman-throne. Unto him they bring the brahman-throne, he mounts the brahman-throne, who knows thus.
text_mt:
That indeed has mounted the brahman-chair.
They bring the brahman-chair to him, and he mounts the brahman-chair, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: tad etad brahmayaśaś śriyā parivṛḍham brahma ha tu san yaśasā śriyā parivṛḍho bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
meaning: तद् एतद् ब्रह्मयशश् श्रिया परिवृढम् ब्रह्म ह तु सन् यशसा श्रिया परिवृढो भवति य एवं वेद ।
text: That same brahman-glory is encompassed by fortune. But being the brahman he is encompassed by glory [and] by fortune who knows thus.
text_mt:
That is this brahman-glory surrounded by prosperity.
Being brahman indeed, he becomes surrounded by glory and prosperity, who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: tasyaiṣa ādeśo yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣann antaḥ tasya yac chuklaṃ tad ṛcāṃ rūpaṃ yat kṛṣṇaṃ tat sāmnāṃ yad eva tāmram iva babhrur iva tad yajuṣām |
meaning: तस्यैष आदेशो यो ऽयं दक्षिणे ऽक्षन्न् अन्तः तस्य यच् छुक्लं तद् ऋचां रूपं यत् कृष्णं तत् साम्नां यद् एव ताम्रम् इव बभ्रुर् इव तद् यजुषाम् ।
text: Regarding it [there is] this direction which is here in the right eye. What of it is white, that is the form of the ṛc's; what is black, that [is the form] of the sāmans; what is copper-red, as it were, brownish, as it were, that [is the form] of the yajuses.
text_mt:
This is its instruction: that which is here within the right eye.
What is white in it is the form of the ṛcs; what is dark is that of the sāmans; what is copper-colored as it were, brownish as it were, is that of the yajuses.

sanskrit_iast: ya evāyaṃ cakṣuṣi puruṣa eṣa indra eṣa prajāpatis samaḥ pṛthivyā sama ākāśena samo divā samas sarveṇa bhūtena eṣa paro divo dīpyate eṣa evedaṃ sarvam ity upāsitavyam | ekādaśe 'nuvāke tṛtīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: य एवायं चक्षुषि पुरुष एष इन्द्र एष प्रजापतिस् समः पृथिव्या सम आकाशेन समो दिवा समस् सर्वेण भूतेन एष परो दिवो दीप्यते एष एवेदं सर्वम् इत्य् उपासितव्यम् । एकादशे ऽनुवाके तृतीयः खण्डः ।
text: What this person in the eye is, that is Indra, that is Prajapati, the same with the earth, the same with space, the same with the sky, the same with all existence; he shines beyond the sky. One should worship him [saying]: " He is this all."
text_mt:
The person that is here in the eye—this is Indra, this is Prajāpati; equal to the earth, equal to the intermediate space, equal to heaven, equal to all being.
This shines beyond heaven.
It should be meditated upon as: ‘This alone is everything.’
Third khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: sac cāsac cāsac ca sac ca vāk ca manaś ca vāk ca cakṣuś ca śrotraṃ ca śrotraṃ ca cakṣuś ca śraddhā ca tapaś ca tapaś ca śraddhā ca tāni ṣoḍaśa |
meaning: सच् चासच् चासच् च सच् च वाक् च मनश् च वाक् च चक्षुश् च श्रोत्रं च श्रोत्रं च चक्षुश् च श्रद्धा च तपश् च तपश् च श्रद्धा च तानि षोडश ।
text_mt: The real and the unreal, and the unreal and the real; and speech and mind, and [mind and] speech; and the eye and the ear, and the ear and the eye; and faith and ascetic heat, and ascetic heat and faith: these are sixteen.

sanskrit_iast: ṣoḍaśakalam brahma sa ya evam etat ṣoḍaśakalam brahma veda tam evaitat ṣoḍaśakalam brahmāpyeti |
meaning: षोडशकलम् ब्रह्म स य एवम् एतत् षोडशकलम् ब्रह्म वेद तम् एवैतत् षोडशकलम् ब्रह्माप्येति ।
text: Being and non-being, non-being and being, speech and mind, [mind and] speech, sight and hearing, hearing and sight, faith and penance, penance and faith: these are sixteen. 4. Sixteenfold is the brahman. He who thus knows this sixteenfold brahman, him this sixteenfold brahman comes unto.
text_mt:
Brahman has sixteen parts.
Whoever knows this sixteen-part brahman thus, to him this sixteen-part brahman merges.

sanskrit_iast: vedo brahma tasya satyam āyatanaṃ śamaḥ pratiṣṭhā damaś ca |
meaning: वेदो ब्रह्म तस्य सत्यम् आयतनं शमः प्रतिष्ठा दमश् च ।
text: The Veda is the brahman, truth is its abode, tranquillity and restraint its foundation.
text_mt: Brahman is known. Truth is its abode, quietude its firm foundation, and self-restraint.

sanskrit_iast: tad yathā śvaḥ praiṣyan pāpāt karmaṇo jugupsetaivam evāhar-ahaḥ pāpāt karmaṇo jugupsetākālāt |
meaning: तद् यथा श्वः प्रैष्यन् पापात् कर्मणो जुगुप्सेतैवम् एवाहर्-अहः पापात् कर्मणो जुगुप्सेताकालात् ।
text: As one about to decease the next day would guard himself against an evil action, even so he should day by day guard against an evil action, until the time.
text_mt: Then just as one who is about to depart tomorrow would shrink from an evil deed, so day by day he should shrink from an evil deed until the end of his time.

sanskrit_iast: athaisāṃ daśapadī virāṭ |
meaning: अथैसां दशपदी विराट् ।
text: Now of these the virdj is ten-footed.
text_mt: Now this ten-footed virāj of theirs.

sanskrit_iast: daśa puruṣe svarganarakāṇi tāny enaṃ svargaṃ gatāni svargaṃ gamayanti narakaṃ gatāni narakaṃ gamayanti | ekādaśe 'nuvāke caturthaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: दश पुरुषे स्वर्गनरकाणि तान्य् एनं स्वर्गं गतानि स्वर्गं गमयन्ति नरकं गतानि नरकं गमयन्ति । एकादशे ऽनुवाके चतुर्थः खण्डः ।
text: There are ten heavens and hells in man. They, having gone to heaven, cause him to go to heaven; having gone to hell, they cause him to go to hell.
text_mt:
There are ten heavens and hells in the person.
Going to heaven, they make him go to heaven; going to hell, they make him go to hell.
Fourth khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: mano narako vāṅ narakaḥ prāṇo narakaś cakṣur narakaś śrotraṃ narakas tvaṅ narako hastau narako gudaṃ narakaś śiśnaṃ narakaḥ pādau narakaḥ |
meaning: मनो नरको वाङ् नरकः प्राणो नरकश् चक्षुर् नरकश् श्रोत्रं नरकस् त्वङ् नरको हस्तौ नरको गुदं नरकश् शिश्नं नरकः पादौ नरकः ।

text: Just one span to the north of the Plaksa Prasravana is the middle of the earth. And where these seven sages ( Ursa major) are, that is the middle of the sky.
text_mt:
A span’s length north of Plakṣa Prāsravaṇa: that is the center of the earth.
Now where these Seven Seers are: that is the center of heaven.

sanskrit_iast: atha yatraita ūṣās tat pṛthivyai hṛdayam atha yad etat kṛṣṇaṃ candramasi tad divo hṛdayam |

text: And where these salts are, that is the heart of the earth. And what is black in the moon, that is the heart of the sky.
text_mt:
Now where these saline tracts are: that is the heart of the earth.
Now that which is dark in the Moon: that is the heart of heaven.

text: He who thus knows the two centers and the two hearts of the sky and the earth departs not unwilling from this world.
text_mt: Whoever knows these two centers and two hearts of heaven and earth thus, does not depart from this world unsatisfied.

text: Homage to Atisama Etureta (?), to Dhrtarastra, to Parthu9ravasa, and let those who protect breath protect me. Hail. 'Action' is the householder's fire; 'tranquillity' is the dhavamya fire; 'selfrostraint' is the anvdhdryapacana fire.
text_mt:
Homage to the transcendent sāman, to Aitureta, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra Pārthuśravasa! And those who guard the breath, let them guard me!
Well-being!
‘Action’—such is the Gārhapatya; ‘quietude’—such is the Āhavanīya; ‘self-restraint’—such is the Anvāhāryapacana.
Fifth khaṇḍa in the eleventh anuvāka.
The eleventh anuvāka is completed.

sanskrit_iast: kā sāvitrī agnir eva savitā pṛthivī sāvitrī |

text: Where Agni is, there is earth; or where earth is, there is Agni. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

the waters are the Sāvitrī.

meaning: स यत्र वरुणस् तद् आपो यत्र वापस् तद् वरुणः ते द्वे योनी

text: Where mind is, there is speech; or where speech is, there is mind. These are two wombs. This is one couple, n. What is Savitar? What is Savitri? Man is Savitar, woman Savitri. Where man is, there is woman; or where woman is, there is man. These are two wombs. This is one couple.

sanskrit_iast: kas savitā kā sāvitrī puruṣa savitā strī sāvitrī sa yatra puruṣas tat strī yatra vā strī tat puruṣaḥ te dve yonī tad ekam mithunam | dvādaśe 'nuvāke prathamaḥ khaṇḍaḥ |
meaning: कस् सविता का सावित्री पुरुष सविता स्त्री सावित्री स यत्र पुरुषस् तत् स्त्री यत्र वा स्त्री तत् पुरुषः ते द्वे योनी तद् एकम् मिथुनम् । द्वादशे ऽनुवाके प्रथमः खण्डः ।
text: 'i)-. ' abbreviate here and in the following. »B.-ttn. *~lh{\).

Who is Savitṛ?
Who is Sāvitrī?
Man [alone] is Savitṛ,
woman is Sāvitrī.
Where there is man, there is woman; or where there is woman, there is man.

that is one pair.
First khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka.

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eṣa prathamaḥ pādo bhūs tat savitur vareṇyam iti agnir vai vareṇyam āpo vai vareṇyam candramā vai vareṇyam |
meaning: तस्या एष प्रथमः पादो भूस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति अग्निर् वै वरेण्यम् आपो वै वरेण्यम् चन्द्रमा वै वरेण्यम् ।
text: This is its first pāda: "Bhus; that desirable [splendor] of Savitar." Fire indeed is what is desirable. Waters indeed are what is desirable. The moon indeed is what is desirable.

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eṣa dvitīyaḥ pādo bhargamayo bhuvo bhargo devasya dhīmahīti agnir vai bhargaḥ ādityo vai bhargaḥ candramā vai bhargaḥ |
meaning: तस्या एष द्वितीयः पादो भर्गमयो भुवो भर्गो देवस्य धीमहीति अग्निर् वै भर्गः आदित्यो वै भर्गः चन्द्रमा वै भर्गः ।
text: This is its second pāda, made up of splendor: "Bhuvas; may we obtain the god's splendor." Fire indeed is splendor. The sun indeed is splendor. The moon indeed is splendor, a.

sanskrit_iast: tasyā eṣa tṛtīyaḥ pādas svar dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yajño vai pracodayati strī ca vai puruṣaś ca prajanayataḥ |
meaning: तस्या एष तृतीयः पादस् स्वर् धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यज्ञो वै प्रचोदयति स्त्री च वै पुरुषश् च प्रजनयतः ।
text: This is its third pāda: "Svar; who may impel our devotion." The sacrifice indeed impels. Woman and man propagate.

sanskrit_iast: bhūr bhuvas tat savitur vareṇyam bhargo devasya dhīmahīti agnir vai bhargaḥ ādityo vai bhargaḥ candramā vai bhargaḥ |
meaning: भूर् भुवस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् भर्गो देवस्य धीमहीति अग्निर् वै भर्गः आदित्यो वै भर्गः चन्द्रमा वै भर्गः ।
text: " Bhus, bhuvas; may we obtain that desirable splendor of god Savitar." Agni is splendor. The Sun is splendor. The Moon is splendor.

sanskrit_iast: svar dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yajño vai pracodayati strī ca vai puruṣaś ca prajanayataḥ |
meaning: स्वर् धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यज्ञो वै प्रचोदयति स्त्री च वै पुरुषश् च प्रजनयतः ।
text: "Svar; who shall impel our devotion." The sacrifice impels. Woman and man propagate.

sanskrit_iast: bhūr bhuvas svas tat savitur vareṇyam bhargo devasya dhīmahi dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayād iti yo vā etāṃ sāvitrīm evaṃ vedāpa punarmṛtyuṃ tarati sāvitryā eva salokatāṃ jayati sāvitryā eva salokatāṃ jayati | dvādaśe 'nuvāke dvitīyaḥ khaṇḍaḥ | dvādaśo 'nuvākas samāptaḥ |
meaning: भूर् भुवस् स्वस् तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि धियो यो नः प्रचोदयाद् इति यो वा एतां सावित्रीम् एवं वेदाप पुनर्मृत्युं तरति सावित्र्या एव सलोकतां जयति सावित्र्या एव सलोकतां जयति । द्वादशे ऽनुवाके द्वितीयः खण्डः । द्वादशो ऽनुवाकस् समाप्तः ।
text: Bhus, bhuvas, svar; may we obtain that desirable splendor of god Savitar, who may impel our devotion." He who knows this Savitri thus overcomes second death, he wins the same world with the Sfivitri itself; he wins the same world with the Sfivitri itself.
text_mt:
‘bhūr bhuvas svaḥ, that desirable [splendour] of Savitṛ, let us meditate on the radiance of the god, who shall impel our thoughts’.
Whoever indeed knows this Sāvitrī thus crosses beyond repeated death; he wins sharing the same world with Sāvitrī, he wins sharing the same world with Sāvitrī.
Second khaṇḍa in the twelfth anuvāka.
The twelfth anuvāka is completed.
Thus ends the Upaniṣadbrāhmaṇa.
